artworks.label: No. 001  —  April 8, 2023
artworks.title: Knight of Cups
artworks.diary: The Beginning of Moments of the Unknown outside of my art studio in Los Angeles, California. Ethan is smoking a joint with one hand, and in the other hand he is holding the Knight of Cups from Smoke and Mirrors; the archetype he was supposed to be representings. Let love and friendship guide the journey ahead.

artworks.label: No. 002  —  April 9, 2023
artworks.title: Butterflies
artworks.diary: Ethan and Colin visited me in Topanga Canyon. Ethan and I were discussing the next step for the project, where he would join me as an assistant to the project. We smoked joints and listened to Colin play his ukulele music until sundown. Then we decided to consume small traces of LSD. I was floored for the rest of the evening, literally.

artworks.label: No. 003  —  April 10, 2023
artworks.title: I <3 NY
artworks.diary: On a flight from Los Angeles to New York City I ran into Alexander on the plane. It was the week of NFT NYC 2023, which attracted artist and collectors from all over the country. After we retrieved our luggage at the baggage claim we walked through the airport to share a taxi into the city. When I saw the iconic I <3 NY. I knew this was a great symbol to represent a new homecoming and the general feeling I had being back to where I was born.

artworks.label: No. 004  —  April 11, 2023
artworks.title: Spinning in the Sunlight
artworks.diary: During the afternoon I visited art events with Anika Meier. We met at a gallery called, NFT Gallery, in the Lower East Side on Clinton St. I was introduced to one of the the gallerists named, Lillien, where we discussed the art they are exhibiting and the new project I was creating. Shortly after this conversation at a small table inside, we went outside and created this portrait of Lillien spinning in the sunlight. To honor her and her teams excitement for their new space supporting artists and NFTs.

artworks.label: No. 005  —  April 12, 2023
artworks.title: Magrittes Sunflowers
artworks.diary: On the way to Long Island I passed by the farmers market to buy sunflowers for my sisters birthday. I ran into a familiar face, Michael, on the 6 train heading uptown at 14th street station. By the time we reached 42nd street at Grand Central Station we had discussed the project and he was happily holding my sisters sunflower; as Magritte would hold an apple. Michael was embracing the shutter of the camera and people buzzing by.

artworks.label: No. 006  —  April 13, 2023
artworks.title: Aliens, Apes, and Zombies!
artworks.diary: There was a punks brunch being held at a large dining hall on the Bowery. After the brunch a handful of Cryptopunks and I walked over to the nearest park on Chrystie st to smoke and talk about art. My dearest friends; Crypto Novo, who dresses as his punk avatar, and Tschully, whom is the punks community admin, became the protagonists for the punks portrait. During the time I photographed them they naturally spoke about the state of Cryptopunks culture while reviewing a new Punks book by Redlion.

artworks.label: No. 007  —  April 14, 2023
artworks.title: Touching Grass
artworks.diary: My last day in New York, before departing to Europe, I was reading in the East Village at Thompkins Square Park. I decided not to attend NFT NYC after all and spent the time in nature touching grass with my bear feet, reading a book, and listening to the live music. Mostly loud punk music, playing on the other side of the fence next to the Hare Krishna tree. Joelle visited me in the park and this was the first time we had met in person after speaking online in photography community. We sat and talked for while about what the shot should be, until we could not hear anything but the music beating against our ear drums and the shutter clicking in the wind.

artworks.label: No. 008  —  April 15, 2023
artworks.title: The Healing Pools
artworks.diary: Upon an early morning arrival to Iceland, I was picked up by my friend and trusty guide, Ryan. He has been living in Iceland as a glacier guide and agreed to go driving with me for a cathartic adventure across eastern Iceland. Our first stop right out of the airport was called, the Blue Lagoon. To begin in the day energized by the sun rays and geothermal salt water. I brought my Super 8 camera into the healing pools , at risk of water logging the Rhonda camera or fogging the plastic lens, to create this silhouette of Ryan.

artworks.label: No. 009  —  April 16, 2023
artworks.title: Don't Go Chasing Waterfalls
artworks.diary: We met up with Ryan’s roomate, Skjöldur. During breakfast he had introduced me to horse meat, something I had not came across until now. He was a kind and interesting host. We then hopped into Ryan’s car and headed west towards Grundarfjarðarbær to see the landscape and waterfalls. At the waterfall I had asked Skjöldur to be a fashion model for the shoot and jump and spin with the waterfall.

artworks.label: No. 010  —  April 17, 2023
artworks.title: Scorpion
artworks.diary: Ryan and I arrived at Gljúfrabúi Waterfall in the late afternoon as we are now heading east towards the glaciers. I had never seen so many waterfalls in the same place at once flowing down the mountain side. As if a new waterfall can be born through a glacial river any given day, as there may be volcanic eruptions at any given time. I entered a cave towards the mouth of the waterfall and was struck with sublime feeling as the water pounded the ground with immense force. Beautiful and chaotic rumbling; peaceful yet powerful. After 30 minutes I had left, to approach strangers to get involved in the art project. I saw Arya and his brother approach with a big smile and vibrant yellow jacket shining on an overcast day. In this moment, I recognized how aesthetically well he compliments the environment and asked if he would like to be part of the film. He nodded yes, I directed him to take his shoes off and stand on the moss. He did, and then wandered down towards us. He fell, and thankfully caught himself. We didn’t realize was how slippery the ground was…

artworks.label: No. 011  —  April 18, 2023
artworks.title: Back 2 Skool
artworks.diary: We began the day at one of Icelands funkiest coffee shops, located on a school bus! A the Scool Beans Cafe, I was introduced to the owner, Holly. We went around to the front of the bus with her first cup of coffee for the day and we made her portrait. Thereafter, She and her crew made a delicious chai latte. It was starting to get busy with a bus filled with people drinking coffee and visiting her bus shop. I supported the shop and bought a groovy tea cup that filters tea to give as a gift to a friend. Ryan pointed at small vials and suggested I pick one up to collect volcanic sand. In that instant I knew I needed 7 vials. A lighting bolt shocked through my consciousness then into my core, where I received a transmission to collect a sample vial of sand from each continent, to unite the sacred sands of the Earth. She gave me the vials as a gift, and I said I would send her sand from Japan made up of microscopic fossilized plankton. Directly after, we went straight to Reynisfjara beach, which is made up of black volcanic sand, and I dedicated this vial to represent the European continent.

artworks.label: No. 012  —  April 19, 2023
artworks.title: Suspended Above a Bottomless Pit
artworks.diary: We arrived at the glacier. Strapped on the spiked chains to our boots and headed up the face of the blue and white ice beauty. There were crystalline clear cavernous tunnels and ice pools with pure waterfalls that you can drink from. We continued on higher through the cloudy haze to meet with Adam who was preparing the ice spikes to fasten a zip line over the large crater in the glacier. I created Adam’s portrait as he was testing the zip line suspension. Everything was okayed for us to give it a try too. Adam gestured to me that it was my turn to go. I nervously accepted as I grew up with a fear of heights; Deciding that this was the medicine, to face fear by embracing it and moving towards it. To welcome it into my world, where the fear can finally disappear. I ran straight off the ledge and slid half way across where I got stuck in the middle. Suspended above a bottomless pit. I laughed at the irony, then pulled myself across to get off. This was the year to face all fears, so why stop here?

artworks.label: No. 013  —  April 20, 2023
artworks.title: The Fairies in the Field
artworks.diary: It was the final day in Iceland and we were headed back towards Reykjavik to catch the plane in the morning. We stopped at the lava field in Eldhraun. Earlier that week, we stood above the green gnoll overlooking the vast mossy landscape. A mystic horizon separated by the sea. A landscape where you can nearly hear or hallucinate the fairies and otherworldly creatures at play hiding in the field. It was in this moment I knew we must come back to make a portrait here before leaving Iceland. We were a few hours out and had not made a video for the day; Excited to revisit this beautiful and blissful scenery. We pulled up and there were a handful of people there. People came and went to snap a photo on their phone and leave. I even snapped a few photos of a couple on their I-phone. I sat and waited, for what I felt was the “right” person to represent this place. Time was on our side. Patiently sitting by a patch of moss I listened to the wind and watched the sun on the moss. I noticed a young photographer walked by and smiled. She took her photos and went back to her car. This was the person I had been waiting for. I walked back to my car to get my cameras. She was parked right next to us, and I introduced myself sharing about the art project and mission I was on. Laura happily agreed to be the model for the day, as she worked in the photography industry and knew what it was like to find a subject to shoot. I asked her to sit on the moss and be herself. This was the enchanted energy I had felt earlier in the week, the fairies in the field.

artworks.label: No. 014  —  April 21, 2023
artworks.title: NXT
artworks.diary: After my arrival into Amsterdam. I was suggested by my friend and curator, Anika Meier, to meet with a digital art and immersive experience museum curator at Nxt Museum, Merel van Helsdingen. The moment we met outside of the museum cafe we made the portrait of the day! Naturally, since we were in tulip country, I could not resist including the vibrant flower into the frame to honor the country I just arrived in. Merel treated me to a matcha inside the cafe before we took a tour of the new immersive video game exhibition that had just opened up. It was inspiring to see a whole world of institutional appreciation dedicated for the digital art sector, in all of its form and glory from blockchain to digital displays to immersive and interactive experiences. It was clear to me that this is the a home for experimental, novel, and innovative art forms in the Netherlands. After the shoot, I had biked home to prepare for Ethan to arrive. This was the day Ethan and I reunited since mind mapping the journey when we were together the first couple days into the project. He joined me as a friend and assistant; and by the end of the project he would go onto becoming the sound engineer for the film score and clips, as well as my trusty musical co-host to the MOTU podcast.

artworks.label: No. 015  —  April 22, 2023
artworks.title: Red Light District
artworks.diary: Every morning I would post online, good morning, where I was that day. For example: gm Amsterdam! I did this to see how I can engage online with people who may be in those specific cities. To be potential subjects for the projects, artists to connect with, people who would like to guide us around their home. It was a great way for us to bring the online into the offline. Futuradora soon responded to our call. We met a few months back when my friend Rahilla had introduced us. So, we had planned to meet at a local coffee shop called, Grey Area. She did not smoke but was happy to sit with us as we enjoyed the Silver Haze. While we were smoking she was excited to be showing us the poetry she had been working on and had the idea to shoot her doing a poetry reading in the Red Light District. I always appreciate when the subject has a place in mind to shoot as most of the time I ask this question so I can best represent their character in the artwork to its truest form. We went deep into the alleys of the Red Light District. We passed all the women working in their windows, and all the men standing in groups drinking and chuckling to one another as they left the rooms with a big smile on their face. Futuradora said this was it! She stood in the alley to recite her poetry while we were being voyeured by the women banging on their windows telling us to stop filming. It was a delicate situation and we wanted to be as respectful as possible the workers, and we kept rolling. It was chaotic and thrilling. I counted down the 10 seconds listening to her shout her reading into the silent camera. They kept banging and cursing. So we left, with a big smile on our faces, since we got the shot Futuradora was adamant on. We went back to Grey Area to finish the hash from earlier, and have a round of mint tea with honey. Then the night ended with an Exquisite Corpse. Futuradora, Ethan, and I wrote a poem together.

artworks.label: No. 016  —  April 23, 2023
artworks.title: Prodigy
artworks.diary: Ethan and I spent the day riding bicycles all around the city like we were in Albert Hoffman shoes. After a few hours it was approaching the time to photograph someone, we cycled towards the Rijksmuseum and passed through what felt like a masonic tunnel. A great location for buskers to make a living, where the acoustic vibrations are felt thumping into the heart and heard crystal clearly in your ears. When we cycled through, the saxophonist was playing a Harry Potter theme song. It felt like we were wizards on our way to Hogwarts about to miss our train. Transported into another dimension until we reached the other end of the chamber where the echoes from the saxophone ceased to follow. We returned the bikes. Then Ethan reached out to his old roommate, Mathilde; They used to live in Bushwick, Brooklyn. Mathilde joyfully invited us over to her flat after she arrived from work. We took our shoes off and she started playing the violin for us. I have never seen anyone play this passionately before. She played like a prodigy preparing for Carnegie Hall. It was decided in this moment that this must be the video of the day. The way she moved, yet held her composure, moved me! The music guided the art today.

artworks.label: No. 017  —  April 24, 2023
artworks.title: Space and Shapes
artworks.diary: After we left Mathilde’s house, Ethan and I moseyed on over to another coffeeshop for another mint tea with honey. We went to Barney’s to plan for the shoot tomorrow. We had an afternoon flight to Berlin. We were deciding if I should make a portrait tomorrow morning in Amsterdam, or when we land in Berlin. And in that moment, while we smoked Amnesia Haze and pondered the shoot of the day tomorrow, a gentleman next to us had asked us for a lighter. His name was Felix. We sat closer to talk and enjoy a few puffs together. He saw my cameras and asked what we were working on. I told him about the project and asked if he would like to be the subject for tomorrow. He said, Yes! and was happy to help. I asked if he would meet us in the morning before our flight and he said, it was not a problem! After a few more puffs we parted ways, leaving him with the hash supply we had accumulated all week in Amsterdam since we would no longer be needing it. I called him in the morning at 8:30 and he was on his way to the park to meet us. He ran up the hill for a shot that represents space and shapes right be side the museum. At the time I was experimenting with zoom and blur to create an atmospheric effect based on the lighting and weather conditions.

artworks.label: No. 018  —  April 25, 2023
artworks.title: Rausch und Spiegel
artworks.diary: We arrived in Berlin and headed straight to Expanded Art gallery. It was my first soloexhibition in Europe and we were showcasing an entire set of my tarot scrolls from Smoke and Mirrors. The host of the show was non other than acclaimed art curator and writer, Anika Meier. I remember walking into the space and saw how perfectly arranged all 78 images on the wall. More than half of the artworks were horizontal and the rest vertical, yet they all fit together! A massive tarot puzzle that Anika navigated with ease. Thereafter, a large group of Germans arrived. The Friends of Finance group led by Mike, aka Warren Himself. What I appreciated and admired about this group of art collectors, was that they always traveled as a unit to support the newest event. It meant the world to me that the group, whom collected the entire series together months before the exhibit, came to meet in person and celebrate; It felt like a family. It felt like I belonged.

artworks.label: No. 019  —  April 26, 2023
artworks.title: Women Are So Much Stronger Than Men In Whatever Situation
artworks.diary: Stefan and his wife Ilona met with us for a private gallery tour. Ethan and I joined Stefan and Ilona in their car and saw a new sight of Berlin I haven’t experienced, in a car. Stefan arranged a museum tour and private meeting with the museum director of the Helmut Newton Foundation. It was my first time visiting and was inspired by all the work I learned in photography school. We learned about the commercial and personal life of the adventures of sir Helmut Newton. It was interesting to notice that he used many of the same cameras as I do. From Polaroids to Rollieflex and large format field cameras! After the tour and seeing all of Helmut’s Iconic work, we went upstairs into the office as a group. Talking about NFTs to the museum director to share with him how archival and attractive the blockchain technology is for photography to introduce a new audience to Helmut’s work and legacy. I sat quietly looking at rare Helmut books while Stefan and the director caught up, as they were friends. We smiled and shared ideas how it would be possible to partner and bring his work to life online. 45 minutes flew by and decided it was time to go. We shook hands and he handed me his card. As we descended the staircase I noticed the writing on the wall. “Women are so much stronger than men in whatever situation.” Then I saw Stefan and Ilona pass the paragraph behind me and thought to myself, Wow! That would be an interesting juxtaposition. Most, if not all, of Helmet’s work is about beauty and women, power and glamour. The statement rings true and is seen throughout his entire oeuvre. These fashionable women dominate his frame for many years, overshadowing and overpowering the photographer. I saw the lovers standing on the staircase and under these powerful words, and then they intimately kissed. The first kiss in the project!

artworks.label: No. 020  —  April 27, 2023
artworks.title: Guardian Angel
artworks.diary: I woke up and started to go on a bike ride to meet with Isa and her baby daughter for the portrait shoot at Großer Tiergarten. Isa was walking through the peaceful park with the baby’s carriage. She picked up her daughter out of the stroller and let her walk on the grass. We talked about Isa’s new portrait project photographing other moms going through motherhood in Berlin. Creating a support group of mothers through her artwork. She told me a fascinating story about a man that was stuck inside her wall. For her this was the reason she told me she wanted to move back to Spain with her family. A place where she can feel safe and not worry about strange men falling from the roof into her hallway. We walked and shot a few still photos in the shadows of the trees on my Rollieflex. We walked closer to Siegessäule, the Victory Column at the convergence of the nature park and road loop. She held her daughter up proudly and with grace. We stood there for a moment, and then I noticed the angel in the background. I thought how special this moment was. A mother with her daughter, with a guardian angel protecting them from above.

artworks.label: No. 021  —  April 28, 2023
artworks.title: Night Walk
artworks.diary: We had an early flight to France in the morning so we met with Ezra the poet during one of his meditative night walks through Berlin at 2 am. We spoke and smoked outside for an hour. Ezra is one of those people you can spend time talking with and exchanging radical spiritual ideals and prose. It was getting late and time to go. He gave me a gift before he walked off into the darkness, becoming a blur with the shadows in the night. Once we boarded the plane that morning I pulled the gift from my pocket. It was a small poem in a leather frame and I read it aloud to Ethan. It went along the lines of “The I, I am is the I, I am not.” Till this day these few words make me think so deep, “I am that I am.” So many questions… What we do is what we become? Who you are is based on how you live? It is what it is and we have to accept it? We are everything and nothing at the same time; Where oneness meets the self.

artworks.label: No. 022  —  April 29, 2023
artworks.title: fútbol
artworks.diary: Ethan and I were staying on the fourth floor of the corner apartment by Cimetière du Père- Lachaise on Av. Gambetta. We were walking towards the center of the city to have a late lunch when we spotted a cute community park called, La TEP Ménilmontant. We walked inside and adventured all around the garden. We sat under the trees on a bench soaking up the rest of the sunlight through the shadows of the leaves. In that meditative moment, I knew this was the place we had to make a portrait. The energy here was lively and there were groups of people sitting in the garden on other benches, playing football in the field, and men and women standing around the small cabin where they were growing flowers and a couple playing guitars inside. It was a true community space. I noticed this kind woman with a gentle smile on her face. Her name, Christine. We spoke in broken English and French to each other about how wonderful this park was, and I asked if she would like to be in the project. She kindly agreed and waited for me to direct her. I gestured to stand in front of the football game. She stood there and I said nothing. I watched and waited for the game to begin behind her. Looking for the moment where her stillness compliments the activity of the game, a marriage of motion and contemplation.

artworks.label: No. 023  —  April 30, 2023
artworks.title: The Great Dance Between Life and Death
artworks.diary: My friend Ozan, from Zurich, reached out to his friend Tru to meet with us at the Bourse de commerce. The Pinault Collection. She brought a small vial of liquid and we consumed a micro-dose; one drop each. The sun started shining through the rainclouds, and we wandered inside the gallery. The primary exhibition at that time was “Before the Storm” by Danh Vo in the central rotunda. The organic materials curated throughout the room dissolved you into the oak. This overwhelming meditative sensation of integrating with the tree trunks from the forest . Reflecting on themes of time and natural decay. We left the museum and headed toward the 4th floor apartment across the street from the iconic cemetery. She also had a vaporizer full of frog medicine. We decided to go for it! Before heading into the cemetery to meet Jim Morrison from The Doors who was buried at the exquisite landmark. A few puffs and we melted into this warm white ethereal space where everything is clear colored and nothing exists outside of light, or time. All feelings and all ideas crystallized into consciousness. Reflecting again on the themes of time and natural decay. The great dance between life and death. Eureka! My eyes gleamed wide open. I sprouted up and grabbed the cameras. It was time to go. It was time to make the video. We walked through the Cemetery without a map and equipped with intuition. We located the painter Pissarro, and found Oscar Wildes wild tomb. We retraced our steps and saw a crowd surrounding Jim Morrisons grave. The group took a few photos and went on their way. We had a moment alone with the Rock and Roll legend. Giving thanks and leaving flowers for Jim. We prayed… Amen.

artworks.label: No. 024  —  May 1, 2023
artworks.title: Standing Up and Speaking Out
artworks.diary: We were Flâneurs throughout the city. Reading the corners and corridors like a memory we never dreamed. Allured by this city; possessed by creativity and historical inspiration. There is romance written on the walls in metal and stone of the buildings masonry. We came across a protest at Place de la République. I scanned the crowded area and noticed a woman with a clown nose and beside her a friend with a bag of bread. We asked them about their signs and they said it was a mockery on tax evasion. Referring to their government officials corruption. They continued to express their woes with us and why they were standing up and speaking out for justice. This was the moment. An emblematic shot to document the protest with our two heroes. I asked the women if they would like to represent their messages in the project. Their wishes were to hold the politicians accountable for violating tax fraud, and for the peoples’ needs to be heard and acted on. I swung the camera upward to convey the strength of lady liberty. She was dressed in a yellow jersey with her bronze flame lighting the way to a brighter future..

artworks.label: No. 025  —  May 2, 2023
artworks.title: Mademoiselle
artworks.diary: It was a sunny day and we were walking through the 6th arrondissement towards Jardin du Luxembourg to study the sculptures in the park. A calming park that many French artists from art history found a sort of divine inspiration for their creations. We had met with my friend Karen, a French art collector who had shown me around Paris the first time I ever visited with a great group of crypto friends during the first NFT Paris. She invited us to go meet a top printer in the city as we were planning to go shoot the portrait of the day together. We arrived at the printer and she was with a handsome man in a suit. It turned out to be a wedding invitation printer and we were getting the master tour. At an early point during the tour I had nodded to Ethan and decided we should leave after realizing that Karen became too busy to do the shoot. We walked outside towards the sun and trusted the path ahead. Following the light we arrived at a four corner junction surrounded by bistros and people enjoying their afternoon café on the sidewalk. The woman in green was shining, her aura was golden. I approached her and shared how we noticed her radiant glow. She smiled. I asked if we may make her portrait for an project. She gleefully agreed and raised her glass to cheers. She said it was her birthday! I had a flashback to the feeling of approaching people in the wild for the birthday project a decade earlier; A connection across time. I stood in the street and started filming. There was a man in the background making chaotic faces and so I improvised. His funny expressions are a great juxtaposition to the woman grounded in her composure.

artworks.label: No. 026  —  May 3, 2023
artworks.title: Memoir
artworks.diary: We were flying to Japan, and stopped on a layover in Dubai. The cabin was empty like a ghost town. It was just Roksolana, the flight attendant, and myself. We were crossing between a few time zones on this flight eastward. It would be too late if we tried to make a portrait once we land in Japan. Roksolana asked what I did for a living and I told her that I was an artist working on a worldwide film project. Then, I asked Roksolana if she would be open to being involved in the art project. To create a video portrait of her since we had so much time in flight together. She agreed, and I joyfully jumped out of my seat, opened the taxi and grabbed my camera case. Once I had my cameras in hand I walked to the front of the plane by the cockpit, face down the lane towards the tail, and directed her to approach me from end to end of the cabin. Get as close to the lens as you can. We made the portrait just as the sun was rising. There was a softened golden glow in her smile. We talked for a while and she told me she was from Ukraine. Working on this airline to escape her war torn home. We talked a little while longer about her dreams. Once I sat back down I thought to myself. Wow! I never made art on a plane before, let alone 30,000 ft in the sky! This image represents a portal. The bridge between countries connecting the lands from above. A distance through time.

artworks.label: No. 027  —  May 4, 2023
artworks.title: Yokocho
artworks.diary: The moment we arrived in Japan we were greeted with the most hospitable locals thanks to the introduction by Emi Kusano. We met with her friends, Kohtaro and Takamichi. They led us through Shinjuku to what felt like a residential entrance. It turned out to be a secret sushi storefront that had no signs or symbols. You just had to know it was there by their numbers. Takamichi told us he is in the ginger trade and this was one of his clients’ establishments. We all bonded over fresh fish, sticky rice, and green tea. I can still taste the flavors on the back of my tongue of lime, squid, and ginger. After making portraits with the sushi chef; we left full of gratitude. We went onward into the night through Yokocho . There was a rose stand and I bought a couple yellow roses for my new friends. Illuminated by the lights that make up the nightlife. We stopped in a neon lit alleyway to make the Takamichi’s portrait. I asked Takamichi to hold his flower romantically, and he held it in his mouth like Romeo greeting his Juliet.

artworks.label: No. 028  —  May 5, 2023
artworks.title: Pika Pika
artworks.diary: We stayed with Kohtaro until midnight in the middle of Shinjuku illuminated by billboards of giant Nintendo characters. Right before the video shoot we were introduced to an extremely bright vending machine arcade. There were many crane games filled of fun prizes with blinding flashing lights and loud buzzing sounds. I chose to play. My mom, Gabrielle, had always used to play and win at these games back when I was a kid in the 90’s visiting the Atlantic City beach boardwalk amusement parks. I channeled my mother, and on the first try I lowered the crane over a large Pikachu’s head and it lifted it out of the box and down the shoot! I guess our family had a knack for carnival games. I gifted the Pokemon to Kohtaro and asked him to play with the large yellow plushie during his shot. I focused the lens of the portrait to express the film grains pigment. Crafting blurred soft shapes of iconic Japanese characters.

artworks.label: No. 029  —  May 6, 2023
artworks.title: The Harmony in the Chaos
artworks.diary: We walked to Shibuya to meet with the artist, Emi Kusano. Emi asked us to come see her exhibition at Bright Moments Japan. Being an early supporter of Bright Moments, and the reason for our trip to Japan, I was excited to see their new exhibition in a new city. Emi showed us her artworks in the show. This was the first time I saw her work and started collecting from her. The artwork I acquired was from the “Neural Fad” collection that Bright Moments released. Emi had an idea to do her video portrait outside at the iconic Shibuya crossing. We observed the movement of the crowds crossing flow over like a river. In synchronization we were the first people to the center. I stepped backwards a few feet to make space for the frame and focal planes. She stood in stillness. Present in the moment, yet surrounded by motion. She was the harmony in the chaos. The traffic light turned red and we left. Emi took us to a place nearby to have a world famous Japanese green tea matcha. We sat and talked for a while before she had to head home. Just as Ethan and I were leaving a robot greeted us at the table and took our empty cups.

artworks.label: No. 030  —  May 7, 2023
artworks.title: Precious Moment
artworks.diary: A pen pal from discord named James came by our apartment. The door was left open and he let himself in as we were waking up from major jet lag. Ethan served up some green tea and we began traveling around the outskirts of Tokyo. I ran out of film so we started looking for medium format rolls to make more photographs. We found film at a cute camera shop nearby James’ suburb. Then we all boarded the train and departed to opposite directions of the city. James planned to meet us again with his wife and daughter, Maya, for the video shoot. We met at a botanical venue. There were a handful of bride and grooms with their families planning on getting married. James surprised us with a tea ceremony before heading into the flower garden to walk around the landscaping. I noticed Maya had a pink toy camera around her neck right as we were passing a pink floral bush. I directed Maya to walk towards me and gestured to use her toy camera to take a photo of me. This was a precious moment for the whole family as we were teaching James daughter the power of photography!

artworks.label: No. 031  —  May 8, 2023
artworks.title: Fragrance Hidden in the Frame
artworks.diary: A photographer named, Mag, met with us in the morning. We spoke through photography. He led us around Tokyo to follow the light and shadows. We made our way to the train station to meet with Sawaco in Chiba. Sawaco, just like Emi, happily introduced us to her friends across different Japanese cities to meet us for the project. Friendships spanning from Okinawa to Hokkaido. We arrived in Chiba. Sawaco picked us up in her car and surprised us for the location of the portrait. After 20 minutes, we arrived at an empty parking lot at a nature trail somewhere in her home town. It was a sacred place from her childhood. A beautiful blossoming rose garden. Colors of roses ranging the entire rainbow. There is a trail from the parking lot. Over a few small stone bridges aside calm running water. We entered the garden and were surrounded by many species of blooming flowers and honey bees. The fresh air was filled with sweet scents. Sawaco showed us her favorite part of the park with a large concentration of pink and yellow roses by the clocktower. The only people there were 3 gardeners who maintain the roses; the clocktower was their maintenance shed. Even though it was Sawaco’s portrait it felt strange to leave out Mag who has been with us the whole day. I asked if it was okay if Mag and Sawaco would be in the portrait together. Sawaco said, of course, in Japanese. Once I started rolling Mag started taking pictures of Sawaco. I directed her to kneel beside the flowers and to smell them. Representing the aromatic fragrance hidden in the frame.

artworks.label: No. 032  —  May 9, 2023
artworks.title: Shooting Hearts
artworks.diary: It was our last night in Tokyo. Kohtaro called us and wanted to introduce us to his new wife Ozawa. They had just married and she just returned from an anime cosplay convention. Ozawa and Kohtaro met with us in the same location in Shinjuku that we photographed him a few days earlier on May 5th. It was significant for the couple to draw the connection across time to match their mid-night portraits. We walked around the square until we felt the right scene. She stood in the busy street all dressed up in her favorite characters uniform. Lit up by neon rainbows shooting hearts right out of her hands.

artworks.label: No. 033  —  May 10, 2023
artworks.title: The Alter Ego of a Super-Hero
artworks.diary: James invited us over to his home in the outskirts of a Tokyo suburb. He was eager to show us his vast Phantom collection as his father introduced him to and reminded him of the super hero. “The Phantom is an American adventure comic strip, first published by Lee Falk in February 1936. The main character, the Phantom, is a fictional costumed crime-fighter who operates from the fictional African country of Bangalla.” In the comic universe we dream and wonder. A champion and their powers. Their origin stories. Imagination and unbounded physics is pure freedom to creating worlds. Following along the hidden life of a vigilante. A symbol of hope. The purple savior. Who is behind the Phantom’s mask? Representing the unconscious. The alter ego of a super-hero. A parent is our first hero. They protected our life and gave us a home to learn who we become. James, father of Maya, shares the love of his paragon, The Phantom, with his friends and family.

artworks.label: No. 034  —  May 11, 2023
artworks.title: Painting with Her Floral Brush
artworks.diary: We were headed Southwest from Tokyo towards Kamakura. Ethan and I took the train to the local village and dropped off our backpacks and cameras at the paper thin home. It was a tea house. There was an earthquake that night and we felt the walls rumbling. We set out towards the forest to hike to the big Buddha sculpture in town. It took a couple hours to make it through the nature trail and into the town. We paced around the Buddha three times and noticed an entrance on his right side. We respectfully entered the body after bowing to the large bronze sculpture for permission. Once inside you can hear the echoes of a breath. We waited for people to leave until it was just us. Once it was empty we both nodded to one another, without saying a word, and started to hum. The hums slowly become OMs and the vibrations were rattling through our body. It felt like an activation. We stopped when new people entered, smiled, and walked outside. Everything felt different, more lighter on the inside and brighter on the outside. James had arranged for us to meet his wife’s friend from kick boxing class, Yufi. She guided us to her town of Chigasaki, which was not too far on the train from where we were staying. We met a rasta man on the train and shared a few laughs. Yufi was waiting for us in her jeep. I picked up a flower from the train station thinking it would be a great prop for her portrait. She brought us to her home as it started raining. Yufi poured us tea and showed us upstairs to her art studio. It was filled with purple and blue pastel paintings reminiscing of her time in Los Angeles. I fell in love with her work and collected a painting on the spot, which reminded me of my time surfing in Los Angeles too. She was having her first solo show in Taiwan in a week. We said we would be there, and changed all of our travel plans to go. When it was time to shoot her portrait, I asked Yufi to paint with the flower I brought. She stopped and looked at me then continued painting with her floral brush surrounded by all her artworks going in the show.

artworks.label: No. 035  —  May 12, 2023
artworks.title: Time to Do Something New
artworks.diary: I met Brian many years back living in New York City when he was operating the Con Artist Collective. He was unlike other gallerists I have met before . He genuinely cared for his artists, like they were his friends. He built a unique business as a community space for artists to rent time in studios, and encouraged to foster relationships across ages and stages in their career. His gallery held many, many, group exhibitions over the years with artists who just wanted a chance to prove themselves to be seen and heard in NYC. Brian held space for me too. He opened up a small gallery called, Lazy Susan, on Henry st. after selling the Con Artist Collective business to a someone who turned out to be a con man. The gallery was in the lower east side off of division st. We installed a Twin Flames exhibition there called, Enter-Mission. It was a photography show of 10 twin cyanotypes framed on the wall when you first enter the gallery. In the back, there were milk crates holding editions of lo-fi mixed media artworks of printed Polaroids bonded to VHS tapes and wheat pastes of double exposure photographs aged on to cardboard panels. We even held a street art exhibit on the Williamsburg bridge the morning of the gallery exhibition at sun rise. Brian married a Japanese woman, before the pandemic, then they left New York to move to her home town in Ito, Japan. It has been years since we last spoke or saw one another at the gallery closing party in July, 2019. While Ethan and I were riding the fast train, I remembered Brian was living in Japan. So , I gave him a call and answered almost immediately. He told me to come on down to the cute surf town of Ito. It was perfect timing. We were already on our way towards Kyoto and jumped off at his stop. Brian had helped us find a place to stay nearby his brewery. We met with him as he was sweeping up the shop, ready to close. He gave us the grand tour of his new beloved enterprise, Beer! I asked him why he left the art world and he said it was time to do something new. He seemed very happy about the drinks he was creating. And, the business was starting to take off! A few of his local friends got off work and came by for a night cap. We all shared a few laughs, listened to raggae music, while watching a Japanese action flick he had projecting on the walls. He locked up the bar and we went out for dinner at his favorite yakitori spot that was open late on the other side of town.

artworks.label: No. 036  —  May 13, 2023
artworks.title: Where the Giant Sleeps in the Sky
artworks.diary: Ethan and I settled at a zen home in a small village near the base of Mt Fuji. It was clear most of the day and we sat outside in the green facing the peaceful landscape. The sun was setting and we observed the colors of the sky shift behind the snowy peak of the sacred mountain. The clouds suddenly came over and covered Fuji and it began to gently rain. Ethan and I fell asleep drinking tea and listening to meditative playlists in the main room with the windows facing the mountain. We could feel her earthly presence even though we could not see her heavenly glow through the mist and fog. In the early morning, I was woken up by a light in my dream. Opened my eyes adjacent to the floor and see through the window the spirit of a giant. Fuji appeared and the sight was sublime. Seconds later, the wind carried the clouds in the sky and she disappeared again in an instant. Tagawa & Fukasawa visited us at our home. We served our guests tea and sat together speaking two very different languages. Talking about family, relationships, and how to love. The heavy rain had stopped so we walked outside facing Mt Fuji behind her cloudy veil. Tagawa & Fukasawa walked passed me, lovingly held hands, and joyfully stood where the giant sleeps in the sky.

artworks.label: No. 037  —  May 14, 2023
artworks.title: Rainshine
artworks.diary: Our first day in Kyoto we sat and meditated by the ancient river. We observed the large blue herons standing in the flowing water while a school of hawks were soaring swiftly through the air. It was after work hours and we were waiting to be introduced to a new friend named, Takehiro, who had just got off. He was dressed in Japanese traditional attire for the portrait. We met him in a lovely narrow alley filled of restaurants and knife shops around the Kabuki theater; Where wandering geisha’s lit by floating lanterns were clicking their wooden shoes on the stone ground rushing to their next performance. Takehiro led us down the stone alley to a small park with many trees. It was lightly raining and he was carrying a clear umbrella. I asked him to use the umbrella and walk from the hill through the trees and towards me while I backed up behind the leaves. He emerged into the light and rainshine. It started to pour so we went to the closest shelter in the alley to have a cup of finely grounded green tea and a community bowl of curry noodles.

artworks.label: No. 038  —  May 15, 2023
artworks.title: The Shredded Light
artworks.diary: A famous and talented Japanese photographer named, Hisa, met us by the river in the morning. We drove to a beautiful zen garden at a temple on the outskirts of Kyoto in a village at the top of a hill. Inside the palace there was a circle window which framed the square room. Half of the circle were trees and the rest moss. Where hues of green gently sweeps across the room through the cream colored sliding paper walls with intricate pink floral patterns. We stayed a while. There was a room to meditate in so we took our shoes off and sat to breathe with a few other visitors who entered the prayer room. We received a call from Kawashima, and planned to meet with him at a small ramen shop close to the bamboo forest. This was the first time Hisa and Kawashima met each other too. We sat, ate noodles, and drank tea before the shoot. We talked about photography and philosophy. Kawashima drew caricatures of Ethan and I, and we the same for him on an ink pad I always brought around. Hisa was showing us his gorgeous street photography and the recent exhibition he had with Apple. He was shaking hands with Tim Cook at the opening. I paid the bill and we left. We walked to the bamboo forest. It was nearly empty and we ran into a friend from the Grailers on the way to find the light. The group made it to the end of the park and we turned back. The sun was starting to hover over the mountain and we had a few minutes left of light. We found a private location in the park deep in the bamboo forest close to a small river. I asked Hisa and Kawashima to stand in the shredded light together. They stood back to back. Faced one another and bowed to honor their presence. A symbol of respect. In this moment, Kawashima screamed Bamboo Boys. and jumped into the air And the name for the group stuck. Kawashima was a playful and funny new friend. He knows how to make people laugh and have fun. He pulled out 2 more green and yellow jackets and gave them to Ethan and I. We threw on the jackets and we jumped and screamed, Bamboo Boys! We were united like a fraternity with our matching moss colored jackets. It was good ol’ fun. Once we found our way back to the path to the car. Hisa surprised us with a visit to hidden temple ruins a half hour away. The sun was setting and we were descending into the forest. Climbing down large stone steps to a small lake where we saw large stones with carved figures and bright red wooden gates still standing tall. It felt like we found a secret, to see and appreciate. Then, to leave and forget.

artworks.label: No. 039  —  May 16, 2023
artworks.title: Under the Holy Gate
artworks.diary: We started our morning meditation sitting by the river. By this point in our trip we were in a group chat of dozens of Japanese locals and we were introduced to Junko & Takakura. Takakura suggested we meet them at Kiyomizu-dera Temple in the late afternoon. Junko was dressed in traditional Japanese raiment for the portrait. She stood at the top of the stairs awaiting Takakura to ascend and embrace her under the holy gate. We walked around the temple garden for a while learning more about Takakura’s paintings and digital artwork. Ethan was talking to Junko about the music he is working on. The sound for this clip by Ethan is a heartwarming feeling of coming home to love. We parted ways with the couple for sun set and descended the staircase back towards the center of town. We sat by the river again as the sky drew pink and tangerine. There was guitar busker playing psychedelic blues calmly into the night.

artworks.label: No. 040  —  May 17, 2023
artworks.title: Humble Queen
artworks.diary: Ethan and I started our morning at a different part of the river this time. A bit further north where we found crossing stones aside the bike path. We were running and exercising at sunrise along the river and took rest underneath a willow tree. Listening to the birds and watching people flow past us like the river over pebbles. Our friend Yuyu called us and said that he was bringing his friend, Miyako. He surprised us with tickets to a Kabuki theater show for us all to go see. He said he’s never been to one so it was new for us all! Miyako arrived at the large stones. Her skin had a soft touch of white foundation shielding her face. She was glowing in the sun like a humble queen. Dressed in royal white traditional clothes and a sunbrella to protect her from the bright light. We started shooting and she skipped across the stones in her wood sandals. Miyako stopped in the middle of the river, where she faced the blazing sun and opened her umbrella. A peaceful gaze unto the horizon where the river disappears into the distance, back and forth, in both directions. We helped her back across and to the path and walked towards the theater. We entered the theater a few minutes before they closed the doors. Perfect timing… We sat and watched the play. The actors wore the face of comedy and the story was wearing the tears of tragedy. Women fighting over a man. A kingdom to wield his power. I turned around and saw Yuyu sleeping. Even though we could not understand the show because it was in Japanese, we all laughed together. The Jokes transcend languages and barriers. The humor connected the audience. The show was very long, and then suddenly it ended. Then another show began… We laughed. It was only the intermission! We walked outside to get some fresh air. We bonded over the show, asked them what it was all about, then we left to go drink green tea together.

artworks.label: No. 041  —  May 18, 2023
artworks.title: Déjà Vu
artworks.diary: Ethan and I left Kyoto and rode a bullet train to a suburban town to catch a ferry to Naoshima, aka. Art Island. The island is best known for its many contemporary art installations and museums. The first artwork you arrive to when landing to the pier is a massive public art polka dot pumpkin by Yayoi Kusama. Karen & Seiko were just an hour behind us so we checked into our house and went back to the pier. They arrived. As Ethan and I sat by the artwork and inside of it I thought how fun and playful the mom and daughter duo could pop out of all the wholes of the pumpkin. I asked Seiko if they would and she happily held her daughters hand and ran into the big red pumpkin. They couldn’t see me from the inside unless they jumped up so I hollered, Action! We saw their heads bopping about in different circular windows like we were in some sort of psychedelic cartoon. What felt like The Beatles Yellow Submarine animation. Once we made the portrait of the day we all rented bikes and adventured around the island together to go see the rest of the art on the island. I was determined to spot the big yellow Kusama pumpkin on the other side of the island. We rode for an hour and made it at the top of the hill to stop for lunch at this tiny wooden udon shack with a family sitting and talking together while running their business. Seiko translated and they happily served us their best dish. We were lit up by the soup and tea and it was time to continue on the bike path. Biking around…It was freedom, it was so much fun. We finally made it to the first museum. There was a lawn of sculptures, all shaped like animals of the kingdom. Seiko told us she was a healer and saw that my lungs were in pain. I took off my shirt and she laid me on the ground hugging the grassy earth. Deep breathing and deep releasing, to the point where it expands throughout your entire body. She performed reiki on me while breathing. I started to wheeze and blow out old air and dead energy deep within far fetched bronchial passages. After what felt like an hour, I sat up crying and could feel no pain in my back or lungs. We had a mini healing ceremony before we walked into the zen cement architecture to visit Hiroshi Sugimoto and James Turrell permanent installations. It was a big grey bunker with rooms highly curated to compliment the architecture. There were only 4 artists showing. It was time to go find the yellow pumpkin. We were close! We were heading back to where our bikes were parked we serendipitously ran into the great Andre 3000. He was with a couple friends carrying his flute and working on his new album. We shared smiles and good grace and continued on our way, until we saw him again later that day at a 7-11 by where we were staying. Some people call it Deja Vu or fate, but I like to call it divine alignment. I see it as artists and musicians just living their life and on their journey working their hardest to make their newest masterpieces.

artworks.label: No. 042  —  May 19, 2023
artworks.title: Cosmic Field of Vision
artworks.diary: We packed our bags and left on the first ferry out of Naoshima, there was no one else on the boat other than the sailors driving it. The sky started pouring rain. Ryuichi & Yumi met us at the ferry landing to make their portrait. Ryuichi offered to drive us closer to the airport before our next train to fly out to Okinawa. He ended up driving us all the way to the airport because Yumi wanted to show us a secret at the airport. There was a hidden hot udon fountain to taste their iconic broth, it was delicious! And yes, we had a few re-fills before we boarded the plane to the smaller island. I have never seen anything like that other than in movies, like a Hawaiian punch water fountain in an old comedy flick. We flew out to Okinawa, then to a smaller island called, Ishigaki. We rode a bus to the car rental lot. I thought I was going to be able to rent a car, and was surprised that we did not have the international papers to allow us to drive in Japan. There were no taxi’s so we walked back a few miles to the terminal. Hitched a ride in a cab and did not have the correct address or cell service. when we jumped out of the car After asking 4 different strangers for directions we were guided home by the locals. Later that night, we walked an hour to dinner at the only restaurant for 5 miles. We were the only customers there. The owners are the sweetest couple on the island. Listening to raggae roots music. The owner who is also the chef made us a taste of the local island fish special and special fruit drink. We came here every night we stayed on the island. It was pitch black dark out now. Ethan and I walked barefoot in the middle of the road into the darkness with foolish courage. The forest began glowing white like super novas softly expanding and sparkling like a trace of a nebula. It became a cosmic field of vision. We began to see bright yellow beams in the distance headed our way. A small blue car passes by, then the same car 15 minutes later returns toward us, slowing down in the same direction. The driver stopped and the passenger asked if we would like a ride home. We said no thank you, then she screamed to watch out for the habu… the snakes. Our eyes glowed and then we knew. So, we accepted the ride home. She drove us home and then parked her car in the driveway next door. She was our neighbor!

artworks.label: No. 043  —  May 20, 2023
artworks.title: We Found the Stars!
artworks.diary: Yoko was our neighbor who rescued us from the habu when we first arrived in Ishigaki. Her family invited us over for breakfast as they run a bed and breakfast business. We told her about the art project we were working on and the reason we came to her island. To discover the phenomenon of the star sand beach. Star shaped fossilized plankton particles that make up the entire beaches. Yoko, her mother, and her aunt decided that they were going to come with us and proudly show us their home. All 5 of us smooshed into Yoko’s car and headed towards the ferry wharf. We sat and waited for our boat and shuttled to the galaxy of Taketomi Island. It was a very hot day and the sun was directly above us without any shade. The women lead the way to the beach. It was a good long walk until we finally made it. It was low tide and the perfect time to research the sand. I picked up a patch and felt that it was regular sand. I followed their directions around a few bends to a specific quieter site of the island that we may find the star sand. Takako, Yoko’s mother, kneeled down and pointed to the ground. We found the stars! I collected a small sample in a tiny jar to study the fossils under a microscope. Takako’s sister started singing and dancing their traditional dance. I asked Yoko and her mother to sit by her on each side to represent family and let the sand fall gently between their fingers. Then, I held the shutter down longer……. I paused, and sat on the ground; Stared out in the horizon to reminisces of what we all just created a moment ago and the beauty of we are now. Caught in a place between paradise and heaven.

artworks.label: No. 044  —  May 21, 2023
artworks.title: By Her Side
artworks.diary: Ethan and I rented two small electric bikes from Mitsuru & Megumi, the owners of our favorite cafe in Ishigaki. The batteries were half fun and we estimated how far we can go. We rode for 30 minutes north up the coast to the lake, locked up the bikes, and went into the lake for a while. There were tiny crabs pinching our feet so we stepped out of the water. We hopped back on our bikes and decided to head back home. We saw a coloful sign and stopped at a passion fruit farm to pick up some fruits, and we left with passion juice. Ethan’s bike was running out of juice. Thankfully, it was all down hill from the farm and we rode it all the way home in neutral. Mitsuru & Megumi greeted us when we returned the bike as the sun was setting. I had my cameras with us and asked the owners if they would like to be in the art project. Megumi sat on the swing and Mitsuru stood by her side. They looked at each other deeply and in love. The perfect match. We finished making their portraits. I gifted them a polaroid as a gift for their kindness and hospitality. We sat for a small dinner and was fed what felt like a 12 course meal of small dishes, their specialty! We were joined by a Japanese woman who was visiting the island from Tokyo. She sat with us to eat; we talked about her work and our adventures. The next morning we met her again to go snorkeling in the ocean to swim with sea turtles. It was low tide and we were swimming tightly between the coral. We swam with seaweed, starfish, and schools of small fish in the clear blue water. We got out of the water and walked home. Then, we departed to Osaka for our last day in Japan.

artworks.label: No. 045  —  May 22, 2023
artworks.title: Green & Yellow
artworks.diary: It was our last day in Japan and we ended in our time in Osaka. During the day we met with our friends from Kyoto and their friends who lived in Osaka. Yuya, Yu , Tomoro, Atsushi & Kawashima lead us to the great Osaka Temple. We started on to a long walk through the park into the landmark. We approached the incline up to the temple and we started playing the Super Mario theme song as the castle reminded us of a level from the video game. A nostalgic memory from whence we used to be game boys. Kawashima brought the extraordinary group of gentlemen a few pairs of his royal green & yellow rain jackets. Ethan and I were already dressed in ours since we received his gift. He knighted the rest of the group as initiates of the bamboo boys. I started recording the guys trying on the jackets. Then, asked the group to get together and embody the spirit of teamwork, teathered by the jackets gifted by Kawashima. They all put their hands in the middle, hand over hand, and lifted up to the sky to celebrate their new connection by the ancient temple. The guys floated towards me and the sacred temple was moving in stills.

artworks.label: No. 046  —  May 23, 2023
artworks.title: Peace Offering
artworks.diary: Jeong & Choi greeted us at the airport. Choi had not been to the DMZ so was more than happy to join us on the adventure. We went straight to the zone. Surprisingly, it was a long drive past the city of Seoul. We made it up to the boarder after lunch. We shared a large kim chi spread at a humble spot right outside the city. The car approached the parking lot to what felt like a theme park. I didn’t expect there to be a ferris wheel and a public art park at the DMZ. It looked like there was a festival coming soon. We entered the main building which exhibited an entire history of the Korean war and the establishment of the zone. This is where the gondola transports you across the river. We flew across the sky in a small box on wires with an empty floor to see the ground, trees, and water. Once we arrived there was a trail that lead you to different sites. We found a gate that separates the north and south. It was up a hill away from the main path nearby a restricted zone. Jeong & Choi stood at the top facing one another. Jeong handed him yellow flowers as an offering of peace followed by a bow of respect. Choi accepted the flower offering and bowed back to his ally in solidarity. They were performing this dance to represent healing for the neighboring countries. I held the shutter down until the roll was finished. We rode the little grey box back across the river. In the car ride home we spoke more about healing. Jeong said he read my aura and he would like to help me. We arrived at our small wooden home with two bedrooms in the historic district. Ethan flipped through a few records and started playing vinyls. Jeong laid me down with his healing hands on my back. Breathing through the process. Surrounded by my friends listening to music; Feeling magnetic vibrations move through my body as he was praying over me. He clapped and I sprung up then started to serve black tea to everyone. The landlord knocked on the door to introduce themselves. They were artists too! We handed them small glasses and poured them tea. It was getting late so everyone started to leave. The couple went home downstairs, and Jeong planned on staying with Choi. I turned off the vinyl player that was playing Transylvania classical music and went to bed.

artworks.label: No. 047  —  May 24, 2023
artworks.title: Versace Moonbase
artworks.diary: Song invited us to meet him at an NFT gallery called, Uncommon Gallery, in the south side of the city over the bridge. As soon as we walked into the futuristic space, Song introduced us to the gallery director, Lucia. She gave us a tour of the exhibition, where we went through every artist and art work. I gravitated to two distinct pieces. A playable grand piano sculpture, where I snapped a polaroid, and the immersive video wall in the center of the space, where I made their moving portrait. It was June’s artwork, I did not meet her until she saw that her work was posted in the behind the scenes on social media. I asked if she would like to be in the project when we made it back to California. She said, Yes! June was happy that we used her art as the background for the video at her exhibition. We had planned to meet her in Joshua Tree! Lucia and Song stood together in the silhouette. The flowers of digital art was moving through space behind where they were planted like a tree. Lucia and Song talents complimented one another. A representation of an artist and a curator collaborating to support upcoming artists in a brave new digital world. Discover new talent by trusting the taste of the artist. Who they suggest or look up too. Opening doors. Giving people an opportunity to be seen and collected. By a gallerist who is willing to try something different and putting new people on! These are the risks, and art is the reward.

artworks.label: No. 048  —  May 25, 2023
artworks.title: Make a Wish or a Prayer
artworks.diary: We met with a friend from online named, Rain. She is a tattoo artist. We spent the day going to see art shows and stumbled upon a Buddhist festival. Turns out it was Buddha’s birthday! We took our shoes off and went inside the temple to observe the celebration and pray with the locals. After meditating and listening to the mantras for 30 minutes by the monks we quietly and slowly walked outside. I saw large yellow candles and was inspired to light a candle up for my mother to celebrate Buddha’s birthday. My mom taught me to appreciate all religions and people at a young age. I bought a second candle for Rain and asked her to light it up for the portrait and stand with Buddha and make a wish or prayer. She closed her eyes for a moment. Then looked up at me, the wind started howling. You can hear whistle and paper shuffling. The small flame was extinguished. So I lit it up for her again. We bowed to our smiling stoney friend and walked under the colorful paper lanterns to the street sidewalk. I look across the way and saw two tea shops. We went into the first on the right side, but the staff was too busy to help us. We quickly left and went to the other shop. The woman behind the tea table smiled and welcomed us in for a glass of tea. She was an academic and expert in the art of drinking tea. She served us many variations; one notable blend that felt euphoric and psychedelic. After 3 hours of tea drinking we decided we would love to buy a brick of black Puer tea. There was a Hagi tea set that was gleaming at me. So, I asked if I may buy this tea set. She boiled the tea and set the Hagi down for us to try. She busted out her rarest black tea from 1969. We drank and stayed for another 2 hours. Rain was translating the whole time, but the storekeeper quickly became our tea master.

artworks.label: No. 049  —  May 26, 2023
artworks.title: And Then We Flew
artworks.diary: It was our last day in South Korea. At sunrise, Ethan and I went on a long hike into Waryong park. There was a small outdoor gym in the mountain and we started to exercise! After 30 minutes we continued up the hill. We made it to the historical houses and large mountain gates at the top. Hiked for another two sun gates a few miles apart. Then we descended down the other side of the hill and were trapped on the side of the road. We hailed a cab to take us into the center of the city. We met with Rain and she lead us to a street market for lunch. She showed us a place that takes a live octopus out of the fish tank and the chef cuts up the tentacles and serves you moving pieces on a plate. Ethan ordered beef tar tar with 2 yolks of eggs. This meal was raw… I tried the tentacles, and it felt like I was eating intelligence. The octo pieces were crawling down my throat and suctioning onto my esophagus. We went to a few other stalls to try more conventional dishes like dukbokki and chop chey. Rain left and we went home to rest before meeting with our hosts, Chun and Woo. They were eager to show us the top of Seoul. So we embarked towards another gondola to reach the top of Seoul Tower. It was a packed car, and I could hear many different languages being spoke. Once we made it to the stop it started to rain a bit. None of us had umbrellas, but it was okay. The water didn’t bother us. We were having fun! We walked all around the tower and saw all the letters of love on the chainlink fences and stairwells. Reading the names of the couples who locked their love on display. It started to pour and everything was closing. We rode the last cab down back to the landing. It was getting late and we still had to pack for our flight to Taiwan tomorrow. We drove up the mountain just after midnight. It was eerie and foggy out. Quiet on the road. I asked them to slow down as we saw electric scooters lining the side of the road. Stop the car! This is the shot. Chun left the car headlights on so I can light them for the portrait and play with the atmosphere. Woo hopped on the scooter and picked up Chun then went back up the hill. Action! They sped down towards me with a moonbeam. Woo stopped, and Chun landed a powerful kiss on his beloved wife to end the night. The sky cleared… and then we flew.

artworks.label: No. 050  —  May 27, 2023
artworks.title: Alishan
artworks.diary: We were in Taipei to visit Yufi’s art show and learn more about the country. My friend Amber, who I always ran into in LA randomly, happened to be in town so we met up with her in Daan park before visiting the Wistaria tea house nearby. We sat for an hour drinking unique blends of black, white, and green teas. Amber asked us why we were in Taiwan so we told her about the project. She suggested we meet with her aunt, Fenmei, who lives with the Tsou. An indigenous community in the southern mountains. We planned the roadtrip with Amber and her mother’s driver. It was 7 am and we started the 5 hour drive down to the Alishan national forest to meet with Aunt Fenmei. We talked and slept the whole way down and arrived at a beautiful misty mountainside. Fenmei greeted us and showed us around her home and market. She gifted me a long red fabric, which she prayed on, then used it as my new camera strap. I gifted her a piece of fabric too. It was my vintage camera strap with psychedelic textures. She winked at me and said lets go! We followed her in her car to the Tsou village. We got out of the cars and walked through the village and down the steps to the large community steps. She walked me to her favorite tree and whispered to it, then whispered to me to make the portrait with this special tree. I walked to the center of the outdoor space and started recording. She held the tree then looked at me. Walking toward the camera. She was wearing the traditional clothes of her tribe. She smiled and the roll faded. I put the cameras away. We walked further down towards the forest. We were all barefoot. We played in the garden for a while. She knew we loved tea so she took us to a tea field to have some tea with the laughing tea maker. We sat, drank, and gurgled the tea. Apparently, thats how you taste the tea according to the master. We had a final meal with 1,000 year old eggs with Fenmei in the evening. Then parted ways with our new aunt and started the 5 hour drive back home.

artworks.label: No. 051  —  May 28, 2023
artworks.title: Divine Kiss of Light
artworks.diary: We met Luke at Yufi’s gallery show in Taipei. He was the DJ for the art show. He invited us over to his house to hangout and listen to more music the next day. Our mutual friend Kevin and his girlfriend came over to hangout too. Luke started playing his dance music with Ethan and then things started to get a bit hazy… We spent hours in the afternoon chilling together. Reading books, talking, and sharing laughs. The sun lifted over the building and brightened the cavernous lofty room. The darkness was lifted and the dust settled. He lived across the street from a large church. The golden light was shining through the window illuminating the room with a soft heavenly glow. It felt like a psychedelic & religious experience. A divine kiss of light on your third eye. In this moment of clarity, we started talking about our fathers and shared the same prayer. For family, for healing. Luke had a gig to play and we left his house. Ethan and I were walking through a tree filled back alley between streets. He asked me to help him be an influence to help quit smoking. He pulled out his pack of cigarettes when we were walking home. He didn’t want to smoke anymore. I asked if I can take them. He said yes, I grabbed the pack and tossed them away. We didn’t look backward… and we went forward to the tea house, yet again. We sat and drank while planning our 50 state journey ahead back home in the US.

artworks.label: No. 052  —  May 29, 2023
artworks.title: Delicious Path to Peace!
artworks.diary: Ethan and I walked through a park in the morning and found a group of bird watchers taking photographs. I had my camera too so we went to see what they were looking at. There was a big yellow and black bird and her baby feeding in the nook of a tree. The 9 photographs huddled around their elder, who was the only person sitting down. They all showed us their cameras and their images. The man who was the park OG showed us his new bird calendar. Everyone let out an “ooh and aah.” Blown away by his pristine photographs from this park over the years and the birds whom inhabit. Then we learned how to bird watch by watching this team of hobbyists. I lost track of time listening to the singing chirps and the vibrant colors flapping through the green. We left to meet with our friends Kevin and his girlfriend Jannie at the Wisteria tea house. They wanted to help us on the art project and suggested we meet with their friends Henry & Naomi. Kevin said that they are a wonderful couple; Henry was from Taiwan and Naomi was from China. We drank more tea and an hour later Henry answered, Yes! We walked to meet the duo at their favorite beef noodle place in town for lunch. As we were walking there I bought Sunflowers off the street to gift to the couple. We arrived at the location and ordered the classic beef noodle soup. Everyone went upstairs to wait for Henry and Naomi. They were running late and the noodle place was closing soon. Once we had finished our bowls of beef and brothy tendons they arrived five minutes before the staff stopped taking orders. They greeted us upstairs. I had set up the shot and tables to make it easy since it was busy and closing soon. I laid the flowers on their table. The couple sat to start eating and I started recording. They were sharing a couple bowls of Beef Noodle soup and eating each others plate. What brings people together? Food. What is culture made of? The food we eat represents the country we are in. It may be a simple soup, but it represents respect. It represents unity. Who is our family and friends? The people we feel comfortable to eat with. This couple symbolizes the bridge between peoples, between conflicting regions. Sharing a bowl of soup can be one step forward And, it was delicious path to peace!

artworks.label: No. 053  —  May 30, 2023
artworks.title: As If No One Else Exists
artworks.diary: Have you had DMT? The dream in the night that you can feel but cant remember? A cloud of smoke for a spiritual delight. I breathed in through my nose and smelled the cosmic ashes in the air. Someone just broke through; they’re awareness. I sat and watched as they passed it over. Then started getting ready for a meeting with Yufi to talk about her paintings. I left the group and returned a couple hours later with her. They passed me a joint and we started listening to music from the 70’s. It started to feel stuffy from all the colors and kinds of smoke so we went outside to get fresh air. It was long after midnight. Kevin showed us a special place by the river he and Jane like to visit. We couldn’t see much other than the tungsten lanterns on buildings and bridges. It was so dark but there were groups of older people drinking whiskey and laughing hysterically all night under the street light. We all stood by the flowing water. It was 2 am and we were leaving at 8 in the morning to Hong Kong. It was too dark to shoot so we promised Kevin and Jannie we would come back for sunrise a few hours later. We under slept, and met with our friends again in the same place we just were. The light dramatically changed the landscape. It was an entirely different place then we were hours ago. We could now see the distant structures and details hidden by the dark of night. I turned around and saw the couple hugging and kissing. It was time to shoot! The young sweet lovers started walking as if no one else exists. I silently followed them along the river as they held hands in the grassy field. Kevin an Jannie walked off into the sunrise as silhouettes and Ethan and I hitched a cab straight to the airport.

artworks.label: No. 054  —  May 31, 2023
artworks.title: A Human Shape
artworks.diary: It was time to see some art! My friend Yael introduced me to Sunny once we arrived in Hong Kong. He is a wonderful curator at M+ museum. This new museum carries one of the greatest collections of Chinese art spanning from before the 60s until now! It was eye opening to experience and discover all these artists I never heard of or was taught at school, coming from the west. Sunny generously gave us a tour of all the floors. I asked him what art piece in the museum best represents him, and he gave us a big smile and said, right this way! We approached a nook in the corner of the museum to an immersive LED room with mirrors. It was an artwork by Kong Kee. I started recording once the main animation stopped playing. The blinking yellow color lit up the room except his face. A human shape. We finished making art with art and went on to see Beeple’s Human One. Ethan and I were joyously surprised to be met with a large installation by Yayoi Kusama in the center of the building ascending multiple floors. Beeple’s piece was in a concrete hall by itself. Kinetic, like a rift in time and space. Chromatic shifts round and round while the human astronaut in the digital cube is walking on and on and on…. Forever. Like Sisyphus, without his rock and mountain, he carries on.

artworks.label: No. 055  —  June 1, 2023
artworks.title: Between the Men and the Trees
artworks.diary: We planned to meet with Jacky and Jing Lee for an early morning adventure to the Tian Tan Big Buddha at the top of the hill. The group met at the gondola station that lifts you high across Lantau North Country Park. It was raining, otherwise we would have done the walk to Buddha. We arrived at the entrance to the temples and walked through a park with twelve statues with faces of animals. It was the creatures of the zodiac. Each animal was equipped with a unique tool or weapon. Some warriors, others olympians. I always look for the monkey, because I am a monkey. Slowly walking to observe the details on every single statue, as if it were a ritual. We continued toward to what felt like a stairway to heaven. The big Buddha was smiling and waving us in. I made Jackys and Jing Lees portrait the moment we saw the Buddha between the men and the trees. We are one! Ascending the stairs slowly and mindfully in the rain as if in a meditative trance. Quietly listening to the water dripping on the stone; The bronze, like a bell ringing. Once we made it to the top we stood there for ten minutes admiring the scale and the location of the enlightened “super-human.” We entered the Buddha and realized it was an art museum. There were many Buddhist scrolls and illustrations on the three floors. Once you reached the crown of the Buddha building there is a mystic crystal. A Śarīra, which are crystalline, pearl-like objects sometimes found among the cremated remains of Buddhist masters, particularly high-level monks or bodhisattvas. Ethan and I were in awe that this was possible to achieve. We talked about this crystal meditation and philosophical ideas on its origins in this attic chamber for a while. Jing Lee came up and suggested we go light some incense for our ancestors. We decided to get the life size incense sticks for a bit of a prayer boost; these sticks were the length of a baseball bat. We sat to watch it burn… The bat engulfed less than a an eighth of the way before leaving, since it would take all day to burn away. The sun started shining through the rain clouds and we were walking past the zodiac again. This time taking a few more minutes with each one in the sun, reveals new dimensions. We hopped back on the gondola and rode over the mountain to go back to the city and drink some tea with our friends.

artworks.label: No. 056  —  June 2, 2023
artworks.title: Strangers Becoming Friendly Faces
artworks.diary: It was our last night in Hong Kong. We were introduced to Jeffrey & Stefanie by my friend Renée. Jeffrey is from the United States and Stefanie is from China.
