It was just after midnight. Not too far from where we were staying. Jeffrey told us to meet him outside of his apartment. We entered the building and went up in the elevator to the roof. It was too dark too shoot and there were no lights, even for the night film. We had to improvise, quickly. So I suggested we can goto the park next door lit up by lanterns. Stefanie joined us downstairs and we all walked to the stone gazebo. The couple brought out there cats and held them in their arms. During the portrait one of the cats climbed on Jeffreys back. We finished the shoot and they said it was time to go to bed. I thanked them, and we left down the hill. We rode escalators and descended large stairwells, perfect for skateboarding, built into the sidewalks on our trek home. We took a detour down a stoney alley. Ethan and I found a bite to eat at a small window serving burgers and falafel. We sat on a small bench next to the take out window under a panda mural. Sitting in silence appreciating the quiet of the night in a busy city. Reminiscing on our time in Asia. Concluding…The moments we lived and the art we created. The laughs we had with strangers becoming friendly faces. The journey continues to our home country. Preparing for our trip to all 50 states that starts tomorrow on a small island in Hawaii. I had to renew my passport to travel abroad as it was about to expire. We planned to stay in the United States while we wait for my new passport to arrive. It was a big gamble on the project, because there was a six to eight month wait period. Thankfully! With a bit of faith and luck and expenditure. It will arrive in July on the same day we reach New York.

artworks.label: No. 057  —  June 3, 2023
artworks.title: Packing Up His Coconuts
artworks.diary: Ethan and I woke up in the early morning to go hiking at the Kalaulau Trail to enjoy the beautiful nature of the island. We walked for a few miles along the coast, smoked a couple joints beside a lovely little waterfall, and then headed back, since we were only wearing sandals and I was barefoot. We forgot to bring water, and as we arrived at the car in the lot I saw a man packing up his coconuts. His name was Kawika. There were roosters clucking around his truck. Circling it. His wife was helping him pack up shop. I approached Kawika and asked if we could buy some coconuts. At first he hesitated and shook his head no. We walked towards the car and then he yelled for us to come back. I opened my wallet and had a fresh 50$ bill from the airport. I gave it to him and he gave us the rest of his coconuts for the day. He cracked them all open and we drank one by one with him. He waved goodbye and they rode off… Ethan and I decided to stay by the water and go watch the sunset at Turtle beach. We took a couple more coconuts with us and walked barefoot on the sparkling white beach a few miles down where the rocks meet the trail we hiked earlier. We sat and swam and drank some coconuts. There was a few families swimming and sunbathing. There were a dozen sea turtles floating buoyantly by the shore. They kept being pushed around by the waves. They dunked their heads up and down and you can see there little faces smiling. We jumped in to the clear ocean to swim with the turtles. We kept a safe distance and respected the school. This was a special place for Ethan as his family once vacationed here more than ten years ago. The happiest memories with his father, Jeff, swimming with the turtles for the first time. The turtles are a symbol of slowing down…patience; a family who stays and swims together. The sun set and we walked back to the car as the sky drew purple and the sand grew pink.

artworks.label: No. 058  —  June 4, 2023
artworks.title: Where the Sun Left and the Moon Greeted Us
artworks.diary: We met Makani in the same parking lot as Kawika, the man with the coconuts. I noticed him and his friend smoking a bong in their truck and we smelled the purple clouds of haze. We asked if we can trade some grass for coconuts. He took a sip from the coconut then handed us a big bag of herbs. He said, enjoy the island bros! We were thrilled, and took down his number before he left, so we can meet again. It was the next day and we gave him a call to be part of the project. He was at a family barbecue. It was a BIG family because the field was filled with people. Makani came out to meet us. We asked if he would like to make art with us now before the sunlight dissapears He was excited and said, let me get my wife! We hopped in our rental car and followed him to his favorite part of the island. A beach across the street from one of his uncles house. His wife, Jade, was pregnant and the sun was setting… There a was massive tree on its side with the roots covered in moss. He wanted us to make his family portrait there. The sun was setting and there was a small shred of light fixated on the young couple. We said our prayers to their new family and to the unborn child. We watched the couple interact in a lovingly gentle way with one another. Started recording and a bit more light shined a spotlight between the trees onto them. It was magic in paradise. Makani and Jade rode back to the family bbq. Ethan and I stayed with the fallen tree. We sat for a while talking; Between where the sun left and the moon greeted us.

artworks.label: No. 059  —  June 5, 2023
artworks.title: The Mechanical Dragonfly
artworks.diary: Ethan had the bright idea to try out a helicopter ride without the doors on to scope out the island from above. I used to have a fear of heights and realized the only way to conquer them is to expose yourself and embrace the fear with courage as much as you can. Samantha was our pilot and we trusted her to keep us safe, and she did. Once we buckled up and equipped the mics she turned on her playlist. It started playing Creedence Clearwater’s Fortunate Son. We drastically took off! She set the mood and momentum off perfectly with that specific song. Associating that tune with all the movies we have seen that juxtaposes with helicopters scenes in war zone. It was as if it was a battle cry. At war with our ego. I was clutching on to the chair in front of me. Breathing in and out as best as I can as the wind howled into the cockpit with fierce force. It didn’t stop until we landed. I was somewhere between afraid and in awe, a perfect balance of presence. Knowing you are alive; adrenaline pumping. We got over a ridge and I started to calm down a bit. Once we made it to the other side of the island she lowered us into an extinct volcano hull. We got extremely close to the mountain side and Samantha’s soundtrack started playing the Jurassic Park theme song, which fit the scene quite well. It was BIG reveal. There was another chopper nearby. We waved to them as they followed our lead. Our Heli ascended upwards and Samantha took this opportunity to send us through the mountain obstacle which felt like we were a football being kicked through a field goal post. She full sent us through and scored a touchdown for the home team! We all laughed in excitement. Before we knew it an hour had passed and we descended back to the airport. We got out and touched the ground with our knees to kiss the Earth. Samantha was preparing for her next ride. We had 15 minutes before lift off. I asked if we could make her portrait with her getting in the red helicopter. The mechanical dragonfly whizzed behind her on the helipad in the background. We all eft, and left our fears there too.

artworks.label: No. 060  —  June 6, 2023
artworks.title: They Exchanged Fruits
artworks.diary: Ethan and I woke up early and drove to the other side of the island. I went scuba diving under water and he snorkeled up top with the turtles. After our ocean morning we drove a little bit further to Polihale State Park. We ran into a hippie in a van who smoked us up. As I took a big bong hit a woman approached us and started cursing out the hippie for selling fruit. She said, “Not in my Haena!” The interaction was getting very uncomfortable so Ethan and I slipped away as they still argued. It was a cloudy day and we could not see the view. Suddenly, the wind blew the clouds away and I was met with a perspective shift. I did not realize the scale and distance we were up from the water and it felt like a scene from Inception when the world curled over itself. We hiked for an hour and went back to the car. Both the woman and the hippie were gone! There was another woman in the parking lot arguing with her husband on the phone and as she got mad and we overheard her say, awww Henry “God Bless It.” It taught me to bless the things we cant undo and understand or are frustrated with. We drove towards our side of the island. I was speaking to Ethan in the car about wanting to photograph a school teacher from the island. We saw a beautiful overlook and parked the car. Smoked a joint and saw this couple approach us. I introduced myself and they asked me to take a photo of them. I then asked if they would like to be part of our art project. Sharon & Ray reluctantly said yes. She said she was a school teacher on the island. My skin started to have goosebumps. I couldn’t believe it! We manifested what we were thinking about, and it happened within the hour. I took a pineapple and mango from the car and gifted it to the couple. They exchanged fruits in the film. It was a reminder that we can wish for something and it can happen at anytime, even moments later.

artworks.label: No. 061  —  June 7, 2023
artworks.title: Wild Lavender
artworks.diary: We arrived back in Los Angeles to start the 50 state road trip! It took us a few days to rent a car for 3 months and gather all the supplies: Taking the film to be developed, re-stocking more super-8 and polaroid film, find a change of clothes, organizing the tea we had collected with the new set, and checked out what was piling up in the storage from the last 5 years. I rented a place for a few days in Topanga. The nature there is a sweet retreat in this cement and motor city. It was where I first lived when I moved to California in 2019. It was a sacred haven; more like heaven. We were a 10 minute drive down to surf at the local Topanga Beach. This was where I spent the entire pandemic practicing and riding the waves. Letting go my love for skateboarding down staircases and ledges, and falling in love with riding on the water catching waves with the dolphins. Nicole met us at the apartment to have some tea we brought back from Asia. She brought over my cat Sandy. She was watching over him while I was traveling the past 2 months since the project started. She loved Sandy and was family to her. We had decided since he was getting old and I would take him on the 50 state road trip with us for a final Hoorah! Nicole and I went on a long walk into Topanga state park as the house was a few minutes away from a back entrance to some trails. She brought her Bichon, Yogi, aka Yo-yo! He was a rescue during the pandemic. We talked and walked the dog in the park where we found a wild lavender flower blooming. I recorded Nicole as she and Yogi approached me, smelled the flowers, and opened her third eye towards the skies.

artworks.label: No. 062  —  June 8, 2023
artworks.title: Next to the Smiling Buddha
artworks.diary: Ethan’s roommate Henrick drove down from San Francisco to meet with us for the project. He brought their dog Aida. After a few joints we drove a couple hours through traffic to head to the furthest part of Malibu on the PCH to goto his favorite nature park. We arrived and I realized I forgot to change the film! I was devastated and felt defeated. I panicked. The light was starting to fade. So we drove all the way back home right as the light was dissipating from the sky into twilight. He grabbed Aida and decided to make his portrait on the porch next to the smiling Buddha and the beautiful flowers at our house. We did it! The lesson here was to always carry extra packs of film even though it may have a roll inside. I’m grateful for this experience because even when you feel defeated and like a dummy for forgetting a key part of your project. You can still persevere if you focus on the solutions and not on the problem. Don’t dwell on what could’ve been and make something what can be! Ever since this day I never forgot a roll of film. So sometimes our biggest failures or regrets become our greatest lessons to be prepared for the future. After the shoot we all got into the hot tub to smoke and drink tea until sunrise. We had planned that we will goto Burning Man together this year once we came back from our 50 state road trip. And that was the next time we saw Henrick!

artworks.label: No. 063  —  June 9, 2023
artworks.title: A White Box Filled with Colors
artworks.diary: We met up with Jason at Gabba Gallery; which is at the intersection of Hollywood, Silver Lake, and Korea town, to make his portrait. Gabba Gallery was where this journey all started. We lit the spark of the soul here, and other things… Outside the gallery where I shot Ethan for the first day of the project. Everything came full circle. A base, an HQ, our home where we created art and closed business deals. A white box filled with colors splashing and joints smoking. Since March of 2021, I was spending most of my work days surfing in the early morning then driving over to Gabba Gallery until the late evening. In the back of the private studio was where my silkscreen and computer station was. Printing away winter after winter, and summer after summer for a couple of years until Smoke and Mirrors Tarot Scrolls was completed. When I finished printing the papyrus prints we held an exhibition for Smoke and Mirrors at the gallery on March 23rd 2023. Showcasing the Gold and Silver scrolls I made for the special edition books. The show sold out instantly, it was a huge success! My family; my Father and Sister, came to my first LA exhibit and it was so deeply healing and fun. And then, we cleaned up shop. I moved all my artwork into a storage in Venice beach before starting the epic journey across the globe. Today marks the return to Gabba, before Gabba moved into its new location in Downtown Los Angeles. Gabba was also closing up shop and moving on to bigger and better things. This was the final exhibit. Passing through the halls of the gallery one last time… and never looking back…

artworks.label: No. 064  —  June 10, 2023
artworks.title: LACMA
artworks.diary: It was our last day in Los Angeles before heading east. We had planned to meet with Yael at LACMA to see a new exhibition, Coded: Art Enters the Computer Age. Since we were all geeks for digital art we were eager to discover artists working in the digital realms. We very much enjoyed the show; All the mixed mediums and installations on view inspired new ideas. We took our time to walk through the galleries. Her husband, Joel, and their 2 kids joined us. After we saw all the artworks we went outside to see the public art piece that Yael curated for the museum. It was Ai Weiwei: Circle of Animals/Zodiac Heads. The Zodiac Project is Ai Weiwei’s first major public sculpture. For this monumental new work, Ai has recreated the famous twelve bronze animal heads that once adorned the Zodiac Fountain in Yuan Ming Yuan, the Old Summer Palace, in Beijing. Cast around 1750, the original heads were looted by Anglo-French troops who took part in the destruction of Yuan Ming Yuan in 1860 during the Second Opium War. The heads remain a potent trigger for Chinese nationalist sentiments. Ai’s new work suggests a dialogue about the fate of art objects that exist within dynamic and sometimes volatile cultural and political settings. With his subversive wit, the artist adapts objects from the Chinese material canon going back to antiquity, twisting traditional meanings toward new purposes. Ai’s continuous exploration of the historical object finds great resonance with the encyclopedic collection of LACMA, which includes Chinese art from the Neolithic to the Qing Dynasty period. Yael shared with us the concept for the installation. I asked her to stand by her Zodiac animal. She chose the Ram. And so I went on to make a venerable portrait of her with the royal bronze steed.

artworks.label: No. 065  —  June 11, 2023
artworks.title: Joshua Tree
artworks.diary: Our first destination on Justin and Ethan’s big adventure was the desert. Where the sacred cactus-trees are. The anthropomorphic Yucca’s dancing in the sun and under the moon. We walked amongst the trees. Making photos and hiking while we waited for June & Chadwick to arrive. They met us at Big Rock. We all hopped in one car and rode to different nature sites together. The trees are all the same, yet they are characters from a cartoon. Different shapes and sizes. The plants are almost human… They look like they move like we do. We drove around the park from end to end and back again. June pointed out a tree from the desert forest. It was perfect. We parked and walked up to the tree to make her portrait. She approached the Joshua Tree and the wind blew her hat right off her head. The spirits of the land visited us as the wind. We watched the sun set on top of the boulders in the middle of the park. The sky grew purple and the land quietly dimmed. We met Lucy in the sky that night; As the sun was setting over the horizon. Ethan and I agreed to start the drive to the Grand Canyon. I invited June and Chadwick to stay the night at the desert bungalow since we had it for the night. Their anniversary was coming up so it felt right to share the home since we planned to leave in the night. They were thrilled and called off work. The sky started to shine purple and yellow stars across the galaxies… The further we drove the brighter the dippers and mythological figures. 8 Hours felt like 2, driving like Lucy was sipping caffeine at every Love’s truck stop. The joints kept flowing to keep us going only at rest stops.

artworks.label: No. 066  —  June 12, 2023
artworks.title: Electric Vision
artworks.diary: We drove through the night from Joshua Tree. Electric vision all the way through. Stopping at every gas station along the highway. We pulled up to the Grand Canyon the moment the light broke the morning sky. We found an overlook and got out of the car to head on the trail. The sun started waking up against the shadows of the gorge. The hollow Earth was a beautiful sight. The canyon overtakes the horizon. It encompasses you with its vastness. An ecosystem hidden inside the effect from a glacial phenomenon long, long ago. Carving into a crater over millions of years. We sat and saw other visitors enjoying the view. Ethan and I were observing the sky, the people, the light in the park. Until a German family arrived. They stood together holding one another. You can feel their awe. From what they see. I approached them and share what I was seeing. Asked them if they would be a part of the project. They agreed. Carlotta, Philip & Fiona re-enacted what they were doing before I approached them. They were embracing looking outward, together. It was natural for them. The ignored me and became themselves again. A family on vacation enjoying one another’s company.

artworks.label: No. 067  —  June 13, 2023
artworks.title: Spreading Her Wings
artworks.diary: We left the Grand Canyon after sunrise and drove straight through the National Forest south to our next destination, Sedona. A spiritual haven in the southwest. Some say this city is an energy vortex. We arrived into our astral home. It was a Xanadu–We will learn more from the owners of the property… in a few days. We rested for hours since we had not slept. Jumping from vortex to vortex; Joshua Tree, to the Grand Canyon, to here… we woke up the next day. Early. We were planning to meet John’s mother, Kelly. She had just moved her during the pandemic from New Jersey. She was happy here. Kelly introduced us to her favorite hiking trails around the area. It was scorching hot and the sun beamed down in the middle of the day, but we still had a blast on the red rocks. She said to Ethan, can I show you a trick? He said yes. She had him lay down facing the rock and over the ledge with half of his body. She sat on top of him and held him in place. She shown him to hang over more of the rock and let go with trust. He was flying…then he got up. I took out my camera and started to record her spreading her wings with joy and laughter. It was time for a chai. We descended the mountain and went back to the cars. Drove over to a local chai spot and introduced her to the sweet spices of life. Its healing when sharing what we love with other people. From hiking to drinking tea… It is what connects us to be.

artworks.label: No. 068  —  June 14, 2023
artworks.title: Xanadu
artworks.diary: It was early in the morning and we knocked on the main door. Paul & Laura are the owners of the Xanadu. Waking up for a golden sunrise at their homemade stone henge in the backyard. Once the shoot was over they invited us into their music recording studio. They were preparing for a podcast and asked if we would like to be on with them. We smiled, said hello to their guest and silently let ourselves out as they continued interviewing… Sedona’s Xanadu is a one-of-a-kind architectural wonder made up of ten interconnected white domes nestled in the desert landscape. Originally built in the 1990s using monolithic dome construction, it blends futuristic design with organic flow—curved walls, skylights, sunken lounges, and tunnels create a dreamlike atmosphere. Once painted in rainbow colors, it now stands in bright white, reflecting Sedona’s sunlight and spiritual energy. Designed to be incredibly durable and energy-efficient, it’s not just a home. It is an immersive experience that feels like stepping into a sculptural, otherworldly sanctuary. It was a blessing to stay with Paul and Laura’s home during our time in Sedona. An organic architectural phenomenon. That night we sat in the backyard surrounded by stone henge. I looked up at the constellations and saw a purple haze in the sky just above our heads. It was a faint yet static. A shimmer of electricity, of energy. Like a magnetic chainlink web in the atmosphere. Alas! We were inside the vortex.

artworks.label: No. 069  —  June 15, 2023
artworks.title: White Sands
artworks.diary: It was sunrise at White Sands National Park. A selenite landscape, where the trinity tests took place. Atomizing the sand in the middle of nowhere in the 1940’s during the nuclear arms race. A military base born from destruction created a healing desert landscape. We drove in to the park the night we arrived minutes before sunset. Then the park closed and we had to leave. The gps was set to off-road only, no main highways. We were high on the coattail end of an acid trip as the day was fading into night. Smoke filled up the car slowly since the windows were up. Suddenly, we approached a few signs on a strange dark back road. There were no other cars around. Big red signs that said, “Active missile site.” I brushed it off. I did not realize we were entering the military base. Then, I saw a sign that said “No Cannabis use.” Then I started to get worried. We put out the blunt roach and opened the windows. Plumes of smoke poured out as we approached what look like a toll booth. It turned out to be the entrance to an active military base. There were agents at the gate that were surprised to see us, as surprised as we saw them. Sandy cat was on my lap, the car smelling like freshly roasted weed with traces of smoke still pillowing out, Ethan with a soft and glazing smile. Both of us praying for the best… In my mind I said to remain calm and just tell them the truth. We are lost. There was a main guard on the left who approached us confused and kindly. He must have been the staff sergeant. There were 4 other officers on our right side who listened to his command. On duty with their arms crossed, noses perked up sniffing, and gave us an intimidating glare. Ethan said, “I dont think we are supposed to be here.” The officer agreed. I held up my phone to the sergeant who asked us for our section 3 clearance to enter the base. The directions on the map showed him that we were heading home and the gps brought us straight through their military base. He laughed at us and gave us a laundry list of directions back. I nodded profusely, and at the soonest moment I could I said our goodbye. Turned the whip around, and got the fuck out of there. My heart had sunk into anxiety as the acid was kicking in again… PHEW! We made it out of that mess. I drove home for another twenty minutes in disbelief. We tried to calm our nerves drinking tea and smoking gelato. It worked and went to bed. We woke up before sunrise to head over to the entrance gate of the National park. We were the first people to arrive at opening time. Continued to the end of the parking lot roadway and went to one of my favorite trails. It was a large open space you can run for miles and feel enveloped by the crystal sand dunes. It felt like a cartoon when running through. Leaving foot prints behind, seeing the wind gently blow the lines in the grain of the sand patterns. I let Sandy loose in White Sands. He was happy. He was free. I knew this was our final hoorah as he was growing old. Im grateful that we brought him on the 3 month road trip. He spent the whole time on my lap while driving 10,000 miles across the country. When do our pets become family? How does life connect one another; transcending the animal kingdoms and consciousness? There is a presence, a feeling of knowing; I would call it love.

artworks.label: No. 070  —  June 16, 2023
artworks.title: Landed in Our Earthship
artworks.diary: We drove through Taos past the Rio Grande Gorge. A big reveal to Ethan… Landed in our Earthship. Intruiged by our neighbors homes. We went to the visitor center at the first entrance. There we met Ryan working at the official Earthship center in Taos, New Mexico. “An Earthship is a type of passive solar house that promotes sustainability. American architect Michael Reynolds designed Earthship in 1970, using recycled and natural materials such as tires, cans, bottles, cement, and adobe. Earthship aims to be self-sufficient, independent of the economy and government, and reduce environmental impact. The main features of Earthship are its thermal mass, renewable energy, water harvesting, and food production. It uses earth-packed tires to create walls that store heat and stabilize the interior temperature. Earthships also use solar panels, wind turbines, and batteries to generate and store electricity. It collects rainwater and snowmelt, filters it for drinking, and reuses it for gardening and flushing toilets. Earthship has indoor and outdoor gardens that grow fruits, vegetables, and herbs. Earthships can vary in size, shape, and cost, depending on the model and location. It can be built in any climate as long as there is enough sunlight and rainfall.” Ryan gave us a tour around the Earthship community. Then teaching us how to build them from tires and bottles, growing food inside, cooling naturally, and collecting rain water outside. To become symbiotic with nature through the home you live. Where nothing goes to waste. Where energy is recycled to restore.

artworks.label: No. 071  —  June 17, 2023
artworks.title: Heart Opening Monkey Hero
artworks.diary: We spent the day visiting the Neem Karoli Baba Ashram and Hanuman Temple in Taos. I was not familiar with Hanuman, as I am a follower of Ganesha. I learned more about this heart opening monkey hero that can move mountains. I saw the light and understanding through Ethan and his compassion towards his guru. I was taught about Neem Karoli; to surrender to new ideas and ancient deities that are here to support us. That it is okay to believe in many paths of spiritual resonance. It actually connects us more as we can relate to one another. The marble temple was recently built in honor of his legacy. There were many Indian families and we made new friends chanting the Hanuman chalisa with respect to their lord. As we sat and recited the words to the song, there we met Zander who was an expert at playing the harmonium. Zander was traveling across country to pray and perform. Before lunch and a handful of chai, I had asked if we could record them playing in front of the bronze Hanuman in the garden. The wind started blowing frantically as we started shooting. Ethan told me that Neem Karoli Baba mission was to help enlighten and feed people. This temple will feed anyone who shows up. It was a beautiful idea that we embraced on to the rest of our journey around the world. Whenever we saw someone in need of food, we fed them, just as the temple fed us as travelers… That is how we can pay it forward on a karmic path. To do more good in the world. We met an elder in the original temple. The bedroom with his original bed. It was humbling in relation to the majesty of the new temple. We can feel his spirit. The woman sitting in the room with us become our friend. Told us stories and life lessons, some that made us tear up. It was is if Neem Karoli Baba showed up and was speaking through her. She winked at us and we knew… His spirit was with us now.

artworks.label: No. 072  —  June 18, 2023
artworks.title: Honor the Ancestors
artworks.diary: When Ethan and I left the Hanuman temple we were told that there was a Led Zeppelin concert happening in town. As we walked into the square we saw a line of people on the sidewalk for a few blocks waiting to enter the outdoor venue. We were going with the flow… We asked the staff if there were tickets to my favorite band from growing up. It was completely sold out. We disappointingly brushed it off and went to have a dinner at a hipster bistro nearby. We sat inside. Ate vegan burgers and drank ginger kombucha. I went to the bathroom and noticed there was a backyard alley that connects to different shops and behind the concert venue. We walked outside after paying the bill. There was a sign that said, “Gallery Show.” I went inside to check it out . It was an art exhibition of the local indigenous children and elders. From paintings to pottery. There we met the chief, Tarynce & later on in the night his wife, Lorna. I bought some of the art and his mothers ceramics. It turned out all of the art in the space was made by his children. We spent hours into the night smoking blunts and eating pizza with Tarynce. The music grew louder. An Encore! We were nearly backstage and could hear the concert. We were perfectly where we needed to be… The concert ended and the crowd left. Tarynce noticed that the band was leaving in their tour bus and they would have to pass us by in the only exit. His children had painted a very creative “Welcome” sign and blocked the road. The bands tour manager pleaded to let them through and Tarynce wanted to gift them a book. They accepted and then were allowed through. Their infamous song Ramble On was playing, and it perfectly complimented the wackiness of what was happening during the roadblock. Tarynce, Ethan, and I couldn’t believe what just happened and we laughed like coyotes late into the night. We met him in the afternoon at his home on the Pueblo. It was a holiday; We made his family portrait on Father’s Day! Tarynce had Nine children with Lorna. They have been together since middle school. It was such serendipitous timing that we celebrated this loving holiday for the project with a father and his many kids. A family portrait. A gift to remember. A beautiful new friendship and honor the ancestors of his tribe.

artworks.label: No. 073  —  June 19, 2023
artworks.title: Three Cyclones
artworks.diary: Once we got into Denver we met with my friend from art school, John G, at a hip yogi wellness cafe around the corner from our home. We were all in town for the 2023 Psychedelic Science conference. We had a healthy breakfast while catching up and planning the adventures for the week ahead. We wrapped up our pow wow and I started to get ready to discover and create with a local for the portrait of the day. I asked myself the mystery; who will we photograph today? In that exact moment, I looked up and saw John and Ethan talking to someone. They introduced me to Gerald . He was just getting off work and it suddenly hit me. This is it. This is the moment! I asked him if he would like to be the portrait of the day for our art project. He was psyched we asked him and he said, of course! Everything felt like it was unraveling… so gently, yet suddenly. We walked outside into the parking lot. As I turned to the guys, I noticed a beautiful mural on the side of his building. It all clicked! He told us he loved to dance. So, I suggested he dance for his clip. Mainly, to be yourself and express yourself! And he did. He surprised us with three cyclones. Whirling through the air like he was hardcore at parcour. It was magic to see it all unfolding so naturally… improvising on both sides of the camera… it was so REAL! Gerald calmly landed at the end of the ledge. He sat straight up and stared directly into the camera until the film ran out. Then the clip started over again in an endless loop of dance and stillness; a balance of chaos and composure. Like Sisyphus, constantly up and down the hill.

artworks.label: No. 074  —  June 20, 2023
artworks.title: Bending and Playing with Light
artworks.diary: The beauty of the art world and the internet is that you can reach out to like-minded people. I met Samantha many moons ago when we curated a public art exhibition together for the month of photography in Denver. We provided billboard spaces to showcase local photographic artists. And when you are in the photography world you tend to run in to similar circles. I have been a big advocate for the Colorado Photographic Art Center, aka CPAC for quite a while. When I become a part of something like an art community I do my research. For example: What organizations exist to support this mission, who are the curators, who are the collectors, who are the artists, what is the general themes and trends of the times… You don’t want to enter a space that you want to participate in without doing your homework. So, after years of online engagements and phone calls ,during the pandemic, we finally met Samantha at the new CPAC building that was recently constructed. The wall paint was still fresh and the photo chemicals had not been poured in the drums yet. So much potential awaits this space. We met and it was like seeing an old friend. She gave Ethan, Chris, and I a tour of the facility. I loved the darkroom. I spent most of my college and early entrepreneurial days in the darkroom making prints and learning the craft; mostly the c-41 printing process and alternative darkroom printing. We talked a while then asked if she would represent this new space in the video portrait. Samantha boldly approached me starting from inside the building and into the hot sun. If you look closely you can see the traffic in the reflections behind her passing by. A nod to the photographic magic of bending and playing with light. How it works…. Once the portrait was completed we walked on over to the Denver Museum. It was our first time there! Chris, who had collected an entire set of tarot scroll silkscreen portraits, was dreaming up ways how we can exhibit the collection in his home town museum. He became a member of CPAC. As it takes participation and contribution to get involved in the art world. As well as time and patience. It starts with an idea, that blends into a dream, that someday will manifest into reality. Because that is how art works!

artworks.label: No. 075  —  June 21, 2023
artworks.title: Johnny Red Rocks
artworks.diary: John G has been my friend since art school at SVA, more than a decade. We used to skate Chelsea piers together in between classes. He was a professional! Gone on long roadtrips across the country, lived in new cities on the other side of the coasts from which we came. Helped me let go of dealing…Shared a bond in healing… He met with us early in the morning to go on a hike at Red Rocks. I wanted to honor his legacy as a skateboarder on Go Skate Day! Which is June 21st every year. We were preparing for a psychedelic weekend at the convention center for MAPS conference. Starting in nature allowed us to restore and reset our energy for an interesting “trip” to say the least. We found our way to the concert area of the park where all the legendary bands and singers perform their hits. The camera started rolling and John started lunging up the stairs with big strides. He is a master of balance and control over his body. You need to be if you plan to be a pro skateboarder; Quick reflexes and agility. It felt good to see my friend having fun again. He came back down and we walked barefoot through the park to ground some more before heading to the conference. We warmed up with a rap battle on the drive back into town, something we would do on our long road trips to express ourselves and have a good time. Life is full of friendship and having fun in it… Remember to “Be Here Now” for that is where the love goes.

artworks.label: No. 076  —  June 22, 2023
artworks.title: Day Trippers and Therapeutical Misfits
artworks.diary: It was the first day of the MAPS psychedelic science convention of 2023. Most of the psychonauts of the planet congregated here to share their ideas and research of the development of their scientific and psychological experiments with plant medicines. We listened to some of our heroes like Paul Stamets, Dennis McKenna, and William Leonard Picard. A couple of Mycological masters and a Lysergic designer. We took a few droplets from a vial to set the tone for the occasion. Going through multiple panels and checking out the artwork that I was hanging for an art show. It was time to go outside to smoke a joint and meet the curators of the booth. There were a handful of day trippers and therapeutical misfits laying out in the colorful dog park. We thought to hangout, why not! Sat on the turf and lit one up. A pastor came over and asked where the nearest dispensary was. We pointed him down a few blocks from the convention center. He left his belongings and said I’ll be right back fellas! Ethan and I were confused, but we remained holding the space for the priest. His name was St. Peter, a holy man from Maine. He came back with the Alaskan Thunderfuck. He rolled one up and passed it on as we heard the preacher peach. Peace and love; The Taurus vortex to channel sacred energy. “We are what we think… so let go… let God.” We were so high on drops of acid. I thought it was the Heavenly Father; God themself. A mighty white beard electrified with wisdom. An innocent blue eyed glaze. Clear minded. I asked for permission to carry his vision with a heavenly glow. Recording Peter channeling the Taurus’s energy flow. The humans were flocking around us in the dog park playing and laying on the faux grass. Seeking nature, yearning connection. It felt like what it must’ve been in the summer of 67… Now a psychedelic journey infiltrating the legislation, the pharmacy’s, and old thought patterns. A new age, a new hope for healing. The medicines are the tools… To becoming.

artworks.label: No. 077  —  June 23, 2023
artworks.title: Sending All the Love to You
artworks.diary: It was day two at the Psychedelic Science fair. There were so many lessons this day. Stand your ground while being calm. Set boundaries strong. Forfeit the people pleasing. Letting go of the ego. Again… Chasing the ideals to have Rick Doblin and Paul Stamets to be a part of the art project. To represent the conference days, the founder of the conference and the counter culture movement towards complete freedom. Legalize. Regulate. Educate. Honoring the moment of this milestone in medicine. I was met with great resistance to make it happen and so I exited the building. Until I had a realization sitting outside in the dog park on a fruit cocktail of plant medicines. A stranger approached me asking for a light. Her name was Rebecca. She is an MDMA therapist. I never tried MDMA before so I asked her a few questions about the process . We somehow dove into a deep conversation about her family upbringing. Where she told me how she came out as gay to her husband, and has since found her joy. Being happy with her true self. In that moment I realized. She’s right! Be courageous, And, Know yourself. I asked myself, Why do I need to chase the ego and fame to photograph inside the building, when I can see the real and authentic sharing their time with me in the dog park . A genuine conversation about identity and healing, Opening up. Turns into trust… Rebecca got me to open up. I felt safe. She is the symbol of friendship. What this conference represents is bringing a lot of people together through the medicine; Through healing! Rebecca recited her heart opening story of coming out to the world. Delivered directly into the camera lens. Sending all the love to you.

artworks.label: No. 078  —  June 24, 2023
artworks.title: You Can Feel Its Wind
artworks.diary: It was graduation day in Boulder. We pulled up to Kanali’s school to celebrate their big day. We were greeted with hugs and smiles by Anjali. She was proud and ecstatic for her daughter. We wanted to be brief as they had a full day of festivities with the school. I intended to honor their family, this achievement, their support as a portrait. The trees and grass started moving as the mother and daughter hugged. Parenting is a powerful force of nature. And, so is love! You can feel its wind. Off of the energy being ignited. The sensation of goosebumps on your arms, butterflies in your stomach, and a sudden chill going down the spine from the crown chakra. Their embrace was sweet. It’s not everyday that we get to witness this connection. And the graduation made it that much more special. Anjali thanked us for showing up and surprising her with this precious gift. For their family to remember; for us to be a part of a living artwork woven with memories and people. We hugged goodbye and took off in the Equinox to meet with Chris whose family will show up the next couple of days. A lot of this project is about love, family, connection, relationships, what it means to be human. To feel, to create empathy and compassion through the love we see and show. Moments that remind you about your past and future. A timeless story. A humble day of life on Earth.

artworks.label: No. 079  —  June 25, 2023
artworks.title: The Best Gift You Can Give Is Presence
artworks.diary: It was an early morning in Boulder. Chris planned to pick up his brother Trevor before he had to go to work at Sprouts. We met the brothers at the atmospheric science research center near the base of the mountain. The Boulders in the background looked like a woven blanket of earth behind the brothers jamming out to Trevor’s favorite song, that he knows by heart, SpottieOttieDopaliscious. It’s my favorite song too. They were swaying in the wind to the trumpet and the hip hop beats. Dancing and singing together. It felt like we were bringing them closer through art, music, and nature all at once. You can feel the love and humility. To honor their father who had recently passed. The best gift you can give is presence. We sang a few more Andre 3000 songs, and an encore. Then Trevor taught us about odds and evens and evens and odds; he has a beautiful mind. It was time for Trevor to goto work so Chris dropped him off and came back to meet us an hour later where we parked. Meanwhile, Ethan and I sat by the sunflowers under a tree looking over the city distance. Smoking a couple joints and eating a mushroom gummy we were ready to go on a hike in to the magical forest. Chris told us how meaningful this spot where we were sitting to him and his family. We all hugged under the tree as brothers. There was a trail from the parking lot that lead us directly to the other end of the trail which was the entrance to the small village in the town. We smiled at everyone who passed us by, and before lighting up a joint in the woods we noticed a ranger with a rifle and decided not to embarrass ourselves… we found a trail that was quiet around the corner and deeper in the woods with a large rock in the shape of the Buddha. It was silent. This is where we sat to think for a while. Under the fluttering leaves and splitting light beams. Sharing the fruits we brought with one another. Medicated and meditated. No one came down this path. It felt as if we had the forest to ourselves. Watching the birds above us singing and hearing children’s echoes of laughter ringing through the trees. We felt joy. We were at peace. And alas, all good things come to an end as we needed to drink water and it was time to go. We emerged from the other end of the trail into the prairie village and took a taxi back to our cars. We spent the rest of the day absorbing the sun. We visited a couple other nature trails and parks until the sun started to set over our heads and beyond the mountains. We all thought, where did the day go? The light is the measurement. Time doesn’t exist when you are enjoying the light of day and the presence of friends.

artworks.label: No. 080  —  June 26, 2023
artworks.title: The Youngest at the Table
artworks.diary: It was our last day in Colorado before we started back on to the 50 state road trip. We spent the week making art. Learning about psychedelic research and clinical healing processes for the future. Laying around in nature enjoying the fresh summer breeze. Connecting with a dear friend and his family. Becoming a part of his family. Chris invited us over to his Mother’s house in the morning. She surprised us with a classic American breakfast. Eggs and toast with some avocado. There was bacon , greens, and beans too! As we were sitting at the table. With Chris, his son, his wife who was now pregnant with their next son, his brother, his mother, and his step-father, along with Ethan and myself. It was a round table of love. In this moment I began to remember how beautiful family is. Sharing a meal brings us all together. I grew up in the kitchen and can relate to this moment so much. Every Monday my father would be home from his long days into night of working all week at the restaurant, Mama’s. Monday was THE day we would spend it as a family. My mother, my sister, my father, and me together once a week. I listened and never spoke. I didn’t have much to say growing up; I simply listened and observed being the youngest at the table. In an Italian household the kitchen is where the family happens and the love and joy is shared. You can taste the energy in the room and in the food. It was an art form of its own. Food is a fabric of family. Of our livelihood. So being with Chris’s family brought me back to a wholesome time in my life. When everything in life was simple and naive… Mid meal I grabbed the camera and asked if I may gift them a Polaroid as a family heirloom, for their graciousness of having us over. For becoming a part of their family through friendship and art! I sat at the table as if I were still eating and recorded the family one at a time as they ate and looked up at me. I only had 10 seconds, and it was perfectly timed to see all their smiling faces around the table. We wrapped up our breakfast and Chris’s mom gave us some treats for the road. We gave the family a big hug and departed on a long and winding journey across our home country. We drove the slowest route imaginable. Off of the highways. Through every little town and national forest that we flowed through. To see the real America in all the of its greatness.

artworks.label: No. 081  —  June 27, 2023
artworks.title: Toadstool
artworks.diary: We rode out to our first destination from the heart of the country. Toadstool Geological Park in Northern Nebraska. We aimed to travel state to state by the natural beauty. Scoping the map of America, I found and was fascinated by the idea of mushroom rocks and geologic events. It was the a blazing hot day and we found ourselves in the barren. We were sitting in the truck formulating a plan. It was time to make the portrait. I chose to shoot most of the portraits in forests and parks because I am representing the people of this country through the beauty of it’s nature. The primal gathering places for humans to honor the land and mother. There was a couple people coming and going. A ranger on duty at the entrance. And a mom and her son. When crossing their paths they shared water with us. They warned us to stay hydrated and be careful in this heat. We bowed thank you and continued on. Ethan turned back to return to the car and I kept going a little bit further. Watching out for snakes, walking cautiously. And Just as I am about to turn back to head to the car I run into a group of men once I turned the corner. I said hello to the group. Introduced myself and met the entire family, Christopher, Austin, Jack, Mark. It was an awkwardly hot day and you can tell we were all overheating. I shared with them the story of the project I am working on and they all agreed to be filmed by me. The family mounted on the mushroom rock and then they departed. A family photo somewhere between the stillness and exit. They walked back to the parking lot and I kept on walking further. Soaking up more of the sun in excitement of connecting and creating art with strangers, who are simply a family enjoying each other’s company. My path wrapped around to the beginning of the mushroom rock trail and was greeted by Ethan meditating. There was a sudden overcast and it started to drizzle. We decided to head up north to South Dakota. To visit the migrating buffalo’s at Kruger national park right before sun down. We got there an hour before it was dark and were parked in the middle of the roadway with cars on each end letting the buffalo ruffle through the metallic river. Their horns scathing against the truck. I am glad I checked the insurance box at the rental lot. We left and I saw in the rear view mirror red tail lights reflecting off the sacred buffalos face. We continued up north to have a pizza party at midnight at Mount Rushmore. We got to the pizza place 500 miles and 5 minutes before closing. “It took us 6 hours to get here!” Ethan and I each had a personal pie. Apparently, the lights were on and the gate open. The Federal Park was open all night so we were the only two people there, eating pizza, high on acid and weed, grateful as can be. Face to faces with the presidents of the “Founding Fathers” Purple lighting bolts shooting through the sky. Electricity right above their political heads. It was time to go see Crazy Horse. Suddenly there was a tornado and we were driving blindly into the rain in the night. I thought we were going to die. It felt dangerous and I could not see where I was going. It was like the biblical flooding on my wind shields… A sign to surrender and stop, before we would drive head first into the super cell. Thankfully, we saw a beacon of hope. A gas station with a few locals in trucks sitting patiently and a police cruiser parked on the other side of the lot. It felt right to sleep here. The storm passed and we continued on the winding and whacky road ahead.

artworks.label: No. 082  —  June 28, 2023
artworks.title: The Magical Mushroom Rock
artworks.diary: After watching the purple haze clouds in the stormy night float away. We waited for the tornadoes to simmer and the rain to let up on the down pour. We made it back home to Sandy to pick him up from our cross-state detour to see a few iconic landmarks and parks. I was nervous that there was a tornado tearing through that part of town! Everything was cool at the schoolhouse we were lodging at. It was a home straight out of Smallville. We took the freeway through Nebraska and were waiting to cross into Kansas. I stopped at a gas station and we ran into someone who suggested we go see Car Henge that was pretty close by and it was their main attraction. I couldn’t believe it! We were in the same town of this American homage1 to Stone Henge, using nothing but steel cars. The sun was over our heads and the cars were sprayed with a matte grey finish. It was more of an art piece than it was an attraction in my opinion. It felt manicured and curated to where the cars almost did not feel real. Like as if they were just sculptures and not cars at all. When I thought about “Car Henge” I thought rusty old American Cars stacked in a lot. And realized what we came to see was almost like a zen garden like back in Japan. The car arrangement in the stone henge motif carried the whimsical joy. The fun of it all. To see something weird in the middle of nowhere…. I made some double exposure photographs and we picked up on the trail to our next stop. Mushroom Rock State Park in the heart of Kansas. There was no one there when we got there. We waited in the parking lot for someone to arrive. And a half an hour later some one did. Patiently waiting for the right moment and the right approach. I started to get the camera gear ready and also walk the trail. I was starting to make photos of the Mushroom Rock a few minutes before the family walked towards us where we were standing. I said hello and asked them where they were from. How did they find this park too? Were they local? It seemed like the best question to ask at the time. Melissa & Kary’s Nephew introduced themselves and I shared about the project. They agreed to have their portrait to represent Kansas on this lovely day. It was a lot of fun and memorable. I was transported. It felt like I was in a Winnie The Pooh adventure from my childhood. Celebrating friendship and kinship, a sense of adventure into mother nature. A lesson for every story. Creating art and playing in the park with the magical mushroom rock.

artworks.label: No. 083  —  June 29, 2023
artworks.title: From Woman to Woman
artworks.diary: Once we made it to Kansas City we stretched a ring around the urban area . Living in a brick home slap dab in the middle of the boarder of Kansas and Missouri. A buddy of mine named, Kurt, introduced me to a woman who’s family was royalty around these parts. Her name is Robin. She insisted on picking me up and showing me around her city as if she were the mayor. She was proud of her town, and I enjoyed every minute of it. Ethan stayed home and I went solo. Robin really wanted me to see this painting at River Club. It was a high society country club and her family were big patrons there. It was completely empty and the hostess did not want us to come inside. She used her family’s name and won our way inside for just a moment to admire the painting. I think it was of a horse…. or a landscape of the river with a steamboat. I can’t quite call what that painting was over the fireplace mantle, but I do remember how odd it felt to stand there while the hostess was watching us look at the painting. I thought we were going to do the shoot with her favorite painting but the vibes were not right and I suggested we leave. We walked outside and I saw the Lewis and Clark statue with Sacagawea right across the street in a small park. “Today on the bluff at the western edge of downtown Kansas City, Missouri, you’ll find Case Park where this statue stands to honor the Corps’ visit in mid-September 1806. Created by sculpture Eugene Daub, “Corps of Discovery” features the two Captains, York, Sacagawea holding Jean Baptiste, and Seaman. Created of bronze and granite, it stands 21 feet tall and about 18 feet wide. It was dedicated in April 2000.” I thought, this was it. This is where I should make Robin’s portrait. Outside in the public space. Understanding local folklore. She walked up to Sacagawea and held her hand. Robin had never been this close to the statue before. he said this small gesture transformed her. She started to cry… From woman to woman, with empathy and compassion. A pain that no peoples should endure. You can feel the sacred tear drops that became the early morning dew.

artworks.label: No. 084  —  June 30, 2023
artworks.title: Both Sides of Himself
artworks.diary: We landed in Bentonville. I always wanted to visit the Crystal Bridges museum so we ended up here. Our friend John G recommended we check out whats going on in this cool little bicycle town run by the Walmart family. I posted good morning Arkansas on the twitter feed as I usually did every day wherever we were to connect with local online communities. A follower turned friend, Joshua, messaged me and was happy to meet up with us. He arrived with his wonderful wife and new born baby, I believe there was a dog too! It was a happy family. We sat over a croissant and talked about the digital art space. Learned more about what he is working on. We went to the museum for a while to appreciate the fine art they have on display. Greeted with a spider by the master, Louise Bourgeois. Walking past 10 years of skyspace by renowned land artist, James Turrell. We went inside and found ourselves in the Kusama Infinity room, again. The first time being with Sunny back at M+ in Hong Kong. She’s everywhere! We wandered through the halls of the museum admiring their modern and contemporary collections. There was an event happening so we scurried out before they closed. Joshua wanted to show us around his town so took us to the town square. It was done up with classic Americana festive nativity. Independence day is right around the corner so I thought they were decorating the town for the holidays. Or, is it always like this? From a silhouette to the main subject, Joshua walked towards and passed me on the red brick road. To show us both sides of himself, the town and park. His home.

artworks.label: No. 085  —  July 1, 2023
artworks.title: A Lineage of Love
artworks.diary: It was our second day in Bentonville. Joshua invited us over for a warm and welcoming breakfast at his family farm. It was a grand and beautiful entrance to his forefathers land. We were greeted by his dad, Tim. He said howdy and had a big cowboy hat on with a welcoming smile. We were thrilled to be there and share a meal. They saw we had Sandy cat with us. They were okay with us bringing Sandy in to their home so we let him loose to roam around their living room while we sat for breakfast. They had prepared a big and hearty meal for us as their special guests. We of course brought our favorite tea and tea set from South Korea to share and sit for a cup or two of white peony tea. It was a lovely contribution of a juxtaposition between a classic American meal and a journey across the world to Asia with our tea offerings. While we were sipping tea, I looked around the room and I noticed a painting of a Heron and had gestured to Ethan that the bird spirit is with us. Tim had asked us what we meant. So we told him. The heron was a symbol of spirit. A representation that we are where we are supposed to be. In life and on this journey. The sacred bird guided us all the way around the world and back home. Whenever we saw a real heron or an image of one. It was a sign for us that this is the way… and keep going… We sat for a little while longer talking about their history and family, how they had this farm in their family for generations. And, speaking of generations, I wanted to honor their family by making a portrait with their newest member! Only 4 weeks old, Joshua’s son. They loved the idea. We walked out back where the animals are for a tour of their property. Before we started I respectfully asked if it was okay to smoke a joint. He laughed and asked if we were serious. We said yes, and so did he. Joshua later said how funny that was because his dad was a conservative man and we were two hippies trying to get inspired. And I quickly learned that with respect comes approval. Tim was proud of his horses. I suggested we create the family portrait right here. Joshua handed over his son to his father. Gently swaying to coo the baby to relax for a moment. Joshua’s mother was brushing the horses in the background and I realized how lovely this shot was shaping up to be. The foreground and background became one with the family tree growing in real time. What this place meant to them and what it will become in the hands of this toddler and their children thereafter. A lineage of love, kindness, and respect.

artworks.label: No. 086  —  July 2, 2023
artworks.title: Black Wall Street
artworks.diary: We arrived to Tulsa. I heard about this town through Larry Clarks original photography series in art school. It was a quiet town with many thrift shops lining up the roadway. Good ol’ Route 66. Our intention was to learn more about what had happened to Black Wall Street and made our way over to Vernon Church. Ethan’s mother had met the priest before and suggested we go find him there. And so we went. I noticed all the beautiful street art that distinguished the cultural neighborhood and history. We parked in the lot right across the street from the church. It was a Sunday service so church was in session. Ethan and I mustered up the courage to get out of the car and go inside. I saw a man in the parking lot in a pink suit parked next to us. I said good morning and asked if it was okay if we go inside. He shook our hands and said to follow him in. We were led by an angel. Once inside he introduced us to the pastor. Church service had concluded so everyone inside was saying hello, goodbye, hallelujah and god bless! It felt awkward being the only white jewish boys in the African methodist church standing patiently and quietly in the corner of the lobby by the stairs, but at the same time it also felt so right… with deep respect to their faith and an earnest understanding for these lovely people. A woman name Francetta came right up to us and asked if we would like a tour of the church. We excitedly said yes mam’. She showed us around the entire building, while teaching us the truth and horrors of the The Tulsa Race Massacre. The Historic Vernon African Methodist Episcopal Church was founded in 1905 and the basement of the current edifice was built in 1919. During the worst race massacre in American history, the Tulsa Race Massacre of 1921, the superstructure, parsonage, and sanctuary still underconstruction were destroyed but the basement remained as a symbol of God’s persevering power. The congregation completed the current sanctuary in 1925. In fact, Vernon AME Church is the only intact, standing black-owned structure that remains from the Historic Black Wall Street era. We were horrified to hear what had occurred here a hundred years ago. I remember vividly in the basement of the building she showed us where the fire had been burning and bullet holes in the bricks. Ethan and I cried for the grief and pain that was endured here. The discrimination and blame was worse than anything imaginable, it was a literal overnight war on American soil, a terrible tragedy. The white folks in town were so envious of the success of the African Americans and jealous of their economic boom in their circular economy, they instigated a riot and it turned into a catastrophe for the black community. Ethan and I were devastated in learning what had happened here as they do not teach us this in history class. We felt ashamed, hurt, and distraught that these wonderful people had endured so much agony as they just wanted to live their lives in peace amongst one another. To provide and support their brothers and sisters, who had escaped the slave trade and were making a fruitful life for themselves. Francetta brought us outside to meet the pastor, Ketih. Before saying goodbye I shared with them about the art project we were working on and felt as if it was our duty to document them with their church. A way to honor them, their faith, and families. They joined hands and prayed. We prayed with them. God bless us all. Keith and Ain went inside and Francetta took us around the block, while she told us her story on how she became the first female pastor in town. She invited us to be on her radio show that was recorded live every week. We were happy to be a participate. We went upstairs in a building nearby and sat with her while she set up on the radio. Then, another guest rolled through for a meeting, and I thought this was our cue to leave. So we provided Francetta a donation to the church after her kind walkthrough and a big hug goodbye.

artworks.label: No. 087  —  July 3, 2023
artworks.title: May This Moment Last a Lifetime
artworks.diary: Once we touched down in the lone star state I gave my buddy Jimmy a call. I had shot his wedding earlier in the year with his wife Dawn in San Francisco with their family. It was a beautiful union in Golden Gate park at the botanical garden. I was blessed to be asked by him to be their fine art photographer to make shots for the wedding. I normally don’t do weddings but this was a special day for a special friend. And I am glad he trusted me with my film cameras to do what I do and have fun making art. He also had a real wedding photographer there so that took the pressure off a bit to make sure I did not mess up the kiss shot or their “I do’s.” He was thrilled to see us in his town as we were passing through, as I was thrilled to see them. He was smiling grin to grin when we rolled up and said that his wife, dawn, was pregnant and they were going to have a baby! I gave Jimmy a big hug and said he was going to be a great dad. We sat down in his back yard to reminisce on his wedding four months earlier and now they are having a baby! He was really ready to start his family and I was so happy for them. He rolled up a tobacco leaf with marijuana and we started smoking a blunt together. I thought to myself, wow I have not done this since high school, but we are celebrating this mans family, so, fuck it why not! All of us were giggling and chirping aside Dawn’s sunflower garden. She gave us a tour of her backyard farm. and then I saw the light on her belly and asked Jimmy to go on over and kiss her and the baby for the super 8 portrait. It was truly a beautiful moment, somewhat an extension of the energy of our wedding shoot we had done, now turned into a baby shower! It’s funny how life just works like that. This is what this project is all about. These moments, that become memories, that is made through my art. I remember we went inside afterward and got right to business….. I tried to work out a deal to make a trade for his invader piece, but the wifey was not down with it. I am grateful that art brought us together and through that we were able to make more meaningful art together, and for a day I was part of the family. He really made me felt like I belonged. Thank you Jimmy. For all your support and brotherhood and may this moment last a lifetime for you and your beloved family.

artworks.label: No. 088  —  July 4, 2023
artworks.title: Two Photographers Speaking Through Light
artworks.diary: Today was as American as you can get! It was Independence day in Texas. I had planned for us to stay at a cabin in Lago Vista right on Lake Travis in the Colorado river. I figured there would be people blasting off fireworks over the water. Ethan mentioned to me he knew a girl named Leah who had just moved to Austin and was happy to come visit us at the lake since she did not have plans for the 4th of July holiday. Before Leah arrived I suggested we goto the grocery store to buy some produce to have a spread of food for our guest. I cut up a ton of watermelons in the kitchen. And decorated them with chia seeds, mint, and lime juice. It was my favorite vegan snack to cool you down on a hot day, which it was. Leah arrived and we introduced ourselves. It was the first time meeting her. She asked us if we had any alcohol and we said we do not drink, although we like to smoke occasional joints. She laughed and said she quit drinking and was happy we weren’t doing that. I served her some watermelon and then we went off to go hiking to the lake. I walked barefoot and quickly realized we had to climb on a bunch of large rocks to get to the water. We sat by the water for a while and started hearing the fireworks bursting in the sky. The sun was starting to hover over the forest and I was inspired by the water and the light. Leah started sharing about her story on becoming a photographer. She brought her Polaroid camera too! We were geeking out on polaroid pictures and asked to make a portrait of her with her camera. I had an idea. I suggested that we can do the portrait of the day with her shooting me with her Polaroid while I am shooting her with my Super 8 film camera. It was an eye to eye exchange. Two photographers speaking through light. Playing with our cameras… Sharing our visions… Having fun making a moment, together. We wrapped up the shoot and all sat on the rocks together; A romantic lake view. Eating the watermelon that I brought to the rocky picnic. Smoking another joint while watching colorful and bright explosions in the purple twilight sky. We watched as local boats passed by waving at us. A golden dog from a neighbor nearby ran up sniffing us to say hi. We stayed for another hour and then it was time for Leah to go back home. Ethan and I walked her to her car and waved goodbye and a safe drive. Ethan and I had munchies again and went back into the kitchen to finish up all the watermelon because we had to leave the place clean in the morning. We sat in the backyard hot tub to relax. A triangle of watermelon in one hand and a roll of wedding cake in the other. A wonderfully calm evening with my brother.

artworks.label: No. 089  —  July 5, 2023
artworks.title: A Lovely Pink Home
artworks.diary: We met up with Kyle in Austin at a barbecue joint. And then to another. I just stopped being vegan at the time so it was the first time having meat in a while. I thought this was the taste of America and had to embrace the culture and our traditions wherever we go. Whatever we eat must be local. Ethan, Kyle, and I arrived at his favorite spot and ordered us up a smoke meat platter. It was busy. It seemed like there was a comic book convention in town all going to the same place like a big party. We went on over to Kyle and his wife, Avery, home to meet their cats and dogs. Their home felt like something right out of the Simpsons neighborhood. A lovely pink home with a vibrant green lawn. The pets came out and ran around their yard. I was able to capture it for the project. A housewarming gift. We were invited inside to drink a cup of sweet tea. Avery started telling us stories about lessons in her occupation at the prison working with inmates. She doesn’t take shit from nobody, yet is compassionate to listen and aid the incarcerated citizens.

artworks.label: No. 090  —  July 6, 2023
artworks.title: Under the Shadows of the Tree
artworks.diary: We got back on the road and headed to San Antonio to meet my friend Sadaf, who is a wonderful curator and nonprofit leader. She was at her aunties house so we picked her up on the road from there. We headed to a falafel spot nearby for a pita wrap. We drank some chai at a table outside surrounded by sunflowers and then carried on to interrogated one another as it was the first time finally meeting in person. Sadaf spoke of her vision with the artists and themes she works with to bring awareness to the significance and relevancy of South Asia, and nonprofit work in Haiti. Sadaf asked me about the art project I am working on. And I suggested that we can begin the portrait shoot to show and live through the art in how it works. But first, I asked if I may make her portraits with the six foot sun flowers with the golden haze. We shot a couple rolls on the Rollieflex before heading out to her special place in the forest. We walked deep into the woods, without a trail. Trusting the Sadaf and the forest to show us the way. She knew where we were going and I kept on flowing. You can hear a gentle rustle. A body of water was close by. There was a blue heron sitting in the river. Drinking, then flapping its wings passing us towards the sun. I looked at Sadaf and smiled with delight. She brought us to the magical place. To the nature that breathes birds and feeds life. I asked her to stand under the shadows of the tree. Then, to look at me… and I recorded and walked around the mother tree. The camera was following the golden light from the sun that was glowing on her face. She looked beautiful. Illuminated like a goddess in the forest amongst the hidden critters and winged feathery creatures. You can hear the echoes of birds chirping and the buzzing sound of my shutter clicking. I shot the roll until it ran out of film. After the portrait we continued on the path down to the stream and back to the car. It was time for her to be with her family. We dropped her off and said goodbye to start the drive to Houston. Sadaf became the curatorial consultant for my ai photography series, Atlas, and helped make the final selections for each country.

artworks.label: No. 091  —  July 7, 2023
artworks.title: Visiting an Old Friend
artworks.diary: Shane greeted us when we arrived to his home city of Houston. He showed us around the neighborhood filled with galleries and art museums. We walked a bit and talked about the state of photography and its place in art history. He is also an incredible photographer and runs a gallery called, Assembly. For some reason we did not think to goto the Houston Center for Photography, perhaps because it was closed at the time we met up. Although, it has been a dream of mine to go visit the Rothko Chapel and we were staying close by. I remember walking in and it being eerily quiet. There were a few people. Like shadows in the room sitting quietly and unmoved. Even the security guard was against the wall melting into the cathedral. I stood in front of this massive Rothko. It was black and purple. A wave of sadness and grief washed over me. You can feel the emotions engrossed in the paintings. I cried and I wept in all of its glory. A dream come true to visit a place, and the artwork transforms you. It felt like a religious experience; Something between an exorcism by the artist and a blessing by god all at once. I can still hear the silence ringing in my ears when I think back on standing in that dimly lit atrium. I’ve only seen his most colorful works at museums around the world. This was a special place. A destination for all art lovers to visit and immerse oneself into the prayer and awe. We left the sacred space and went on to wander the neighborhood. I saw a funny red swing and asked Shane to try it out. He started swinging and I shot a few seconds then decided to quit. This wasn’t it. We continued on and he started walking on this long branch that was hanging off the tree and laying on the ground. I never seen a tree do this before. I instantly started recording Shane and I thought this was great! This is fun. This is it! Not as silly and childish as a grown man swinging on a jokingly large red wooden swing. I saw his innocence… A young man taking care of his inner child by a simple balancing act on the tree. He was creating harmony with nature and proudly showing us where he grew up. It felt like we were kids again visiting an old friend. While Shanae was climbing I was making beat boxing sounds like I used to do when I was younger. Sometimes I still do! Ethan surprised me with this song since he snuck the sound into the track. We grew up listening to Houston rap in the early 2000’s and Ethan and I had a funny inside joke about Mike Jones still tippin on fo fos. So much so we blasted this music in our rental car while we were riding around Houston. We got to re-live a fun time from our past lives as kids that grew up from different parts of the country that were brought together through art, nature, and music.

artworks.label: No. 092  —  July 8, 2023
artworks.title: Grit and Graffiti
artworks.diary: On the road to New Orleans we passed a massive gator that stretched out the entire length of the road. It was roadkill, but it was certainly a sight I would not forget. We are in gator country now! We arrived in New Orleans and landed at Nyssa’s spot. Last time I saw Nyssa she was living in her van in Bushwick with her cat. Nyssa is one of my oldest friends from Bushwick. She held space for me for my first art studio at The Living Gallery back in 2014. This is where I created the Cognition series. She is a master of community building and supporting the locals, and taught me everything I know about bringing people together. The last time we saw one another was before the pandemic. We did a photoshoot at Dead Horse Bay in Brooklyn. This beach was filled with glass, yet none of us got hurt walking barefoot through the sand and water. It was a polluted and quiet place to make art. We shot her Smoke and Mirrors portrait as well as a surrealist short Super 8 film called, Laundry. When I saw her in Louisiana I gave her a big hug hello. She had more face tattoos from when I saw her last. Nyssa gave us her home to sleep in for the next few days as long as we take good care of her new kitten and grown cat. We embarked on a photoshoot before her plane ride back to New York to see her dad. It started to rain and she brought us to a place she liked to go an write poetry. By the train tracks filled with grit and graffiti. The perfect stomping ground to get inspired to write songs and slam poetry. Before heading to the airport I mentioned I wanted to collect some of her art and the T-shirt she is wearing in the film. She didn’t give me a price and said I can have it all. But that did not feel right to me so I took out a few hundred dollars and gave it to her. She smiled, took a swig from her flask, and kissed me on my cheek. We drove her to the airport and waved her goodbye before heading back to the home to rest and play with the cats on a rainy day in the hood in New Orleans.

artworks.label: No. 093  —  July 9, 2023
artworks.title: The Artist Makes and Breaks the Rules
artworks.diary: Waking up with a cat on my chest. Checking in on Ethan as he was sleeping on a stiff massage table in the other room. There was no air conditioner so it was humid in the house. Just a cool breeze from a small fan. I was feeling a little rough around the edges and thought it was finally time to get a hair and beard cut; I do so every three months. I called up Nyssa to check in on her and told me she was back at The Living Gallery in Bushwick before heading to the Hamptons to see her pops. I asked if she knew any barbers or friends who cut hair. She txted me the number of her friend named, Grace, but they liked to be called by their nickname, Ransom. I called them up and she said to come by around 2 pm. Ransom was the best in town, and I was eager to cut down my beard a few inches since it was so damn hot outside. I suited up the camera case with my Polaroid and Super-8 and headed on over to their house. Ransom welcomed me inside the living room. There was their Salon. A sink by the window and a high chair for cutting hair. in front of a large distressed mirror A beauty studio with peach walls and a rosey fragrance. Ransom sat me down in the chair and I said, I trust you. and Jokingly said, please work on me like Michelangelo treated a marble block. We talked for a while about their life, adventures, and friends in New Orleans. How they became the neighborhood hair stylist. I was looking in the mirror and thought, this would be a great shot for the portrait for today. A diaristic approach through a personal experience, yet captivating the essence of Ransom’s passion and focus.
