It’s up to chance. Luckily, Sophia arrived as the sun was setting and we had a bit of light to work with. She stepped into the spot the man with the cat in the hat was standing and she jumped on the stones like hopscotching into the fountain and back. The original plan had worked out after all. I learned a very valuable lesson that day. Fear forced me to find a way through. I was afraid to fail, afraid to disappoint, afraid to miss out on the moment especially as the light was washing away into the clouds into twilight. What is this fear and why? It was me trying to adapt because I did not know if Sophia was coming or not. So the man in the top hat with the cat was reflecting his fear back on to me in a way. The lesson is to trust and be patient. But also to try and take action. There is a balance. And maybe both ways are right. To always have a back up plan and improvise. To adapt to the situation and surroundings if time is delayed. It’s also trusting yourself as well as the process and how those two meet in the middle. Perhaps me shooting the cat and that hat was a way to pass time and practice before my friend showed up so we knew exactly what the frame would be. Sophia brought her own flare with her warm smiles and good vibes. We worked fast and the light dipped behind the clocktower. We hung out all night with her and her friends spending the evening walking around her fair city and making art in our air b and b. At the end of the day, I realized we just have to make art when it feels right. Even if other people say yes in one instance and no in the next. We are still creating a vision and sharpening our craft. For when the real piece is made it will manifest itself. She showed up and my fear disappeared. How could I have known it would work out? It was our first time meeting. And her and her family were the stars of the show for the next few days. Mom and sis. Today and tomorrow. They showed so much love and even saved the day. Which I will save that story for tomorrow! Goodnight dear friend.

artworks.label: No. 176  —  September 30, 2023
artworks.title: Life Is Art
artworks.diary: “I think everything in life is art. What you do, how you dress, when you love someone and how you talk. Your smile and your personality. What you believe in and all your dreams. The way you drink your tea. How you decorate your home, or party. Your grocery list, the food you make. How your writing looks, and the way you feel. Life is art.”

artworks.label: No. 177  —  October 1, 2023
artworks.title: A Ballet of Green and Pink Energies
artworks.diary: We started the day at a sauna boat where you can sit in the heat and jump right into the Arctic ocean to take a cold plunge. It was invigorating to start the day this way, as the locals do! Max showed us around his wonderful town, the northern most city, in Norway. Where every night you can witness the glory of the Northern Lights. This was my third try to be enamored by the green lights in the sky. The first time was in Iceland at the beginning of this project, it was too cloudy. The second was in Alaska, and we were too South. Now, here we are! A place where you are guaranteed to see the dancing beams in the heavens at dawn. Before it got dark out, Max took us on a hike to forage for magic mushrooms. It was the season for it and it had just rained so it was ripe for them to pop up. We went into a cow field where he would usually find them. But to no luck for us we could not find any fresh liberty caps. However, he had a nice bag of little brown mushrooms he foraged weeks prior. We snacked on those along with his deer meat and Norwegian cheese. It was like sweet little charcuterie board with a bit of honey combs. As we were fumbling around and started to peak up in the hills looking for more magic on the ground we started to see the magic in the sky. It was dark out now and the city lights illuminated the lake that reflected a mirrored reality. It was quite beautiful to see from that vantage point. And as we walked the path back to the trail we were lead by Amanitas they were liked lanterns on a landing strip or in a dark movie theater. They were shining a bright red with their white fuzzy spots. These caps were all over the place and were massive! I had never seen one before today, and we saw more than a hundred. It felt like we came out of a Super Mario video game. Those red Amanitas as beautiful as they were like flowers growing from mycelium network underground. we did not eat them. They are toxic and take you to a psychedelic place you may not come back from, unless of course you drank it from a deer or boiled the toxins off. We teleported back to Max’s house by the lake. While the guys were smoking cigarettes. I was in the parked car on the lawn. Unfortunately, my trip was was spiraling as I was arguing with the hired editor of the film since he was holding my undeveloped film hostage while extorting me and it was quite upsetting while I was tripping out. Ethan called out to me to come join them and so I “let it go” for now… I stood outside and looked up and was blown away by what I had seen. The mood had shifted instantaneously. It was like a ballet of green and pink energies circling around us above our heads. Shimmering and glimmering on a clear night sky while healing our souls. It was scary at first, scary beautiful. Then a calm cam over me, it brought me to tours and joy to see a mesmerizing light flicker for over an hour! Then it was gone into the night like it was never there. The suns plasma evaporated into the magnetic field of our planet. Cosmic forces at odds and in sync with a chaotic harmony that creates a spectrum of wonder and beauty.

artworks.label: No. 178  —  October 2, 2023
artworks.title: Date with a Vampire
artworks.diary: We had arrived in to the night at a meeting place by the Sibelius monument. Jenni met us there and it was all closed off for construction. Gates surrounded the place. The light had vanished. We saw a break in the chainlink fence and went through undiscovered. I used the night film to see if that would reveal anything at all. But, ironically, Jenni had said to me that she was a vampire and her image would not show up. She was right because when I developed the film I could barely see through the grain, even though she was there and we used two cameras in two locations. In the dark by this pixelated organ we were playing under. Then by the water under the tungsten lights with the day time film. This caused an abstraction in the film and I decided to shift back and forth from both scenes to represent Jenni for this shot. Expressing the figure and what can be seen or couldn’t. A painterly improvisation. To make the best of the film that we had. To see through the veil of a vampires reflection and shadow. A trace without being invisible anymore. To see even if she cannot be seen. Fragments of herself as her paintings reveal a profound depth to this womans’ psyche. Jenni my friend, the muse from Finland. In this project the only failure is not making the art. The result is the art. Wether it is perfectly clear, absolutely blurry, or incredibly dark. The proof is in the journey, the ups and downs. The perfections and imperfections. As is life in its ebbs and flows. The art is the journey through the process, to be seen not as fragments, but as the whole.

artworks.label: No. 179  —  October 3, 2023
artworks.title: Moss People
artworks.diary: Drove east to Fiskars, a small artist town, to meet a great artist that I’ve looked up to for quite some time. His name is Kim Simonsson, a legendary ceramicist. He makes this beautiful life size sculptures called moss people. Kim invented a way by electrolysis to create the fiber like structures on his ceramic children. He mirrors and imagines the moss people as his own kin which represent his son and daughter. He shared that with me when I met him at his studio. Surrounded by various forms and styles of his mythical beings covered in moss, flowers, and nostalgia They say sometimes to never meet your heroes. Kim is a humble and kind man, a gem of an artist in Finland. Grateful to become his friend through his captivating art that makes you feel the innocence, playfulness, and wonder of a child again. All I had to do was reach out. Reaching out to those who inspire you and connect with intention is easy when you have the right intention and purpose. My intention was to make art with a great artist, to include him and his art in this film to represent his home country. By the time I left his studio I ended up collecting one of his smaller sized out of 3D print editions of a green moss boy in a fox hoodie to carry that energy with me. A totem of protection and guidance. Wandering around Europe in a rental for the rest of the road trip alone through all 27 EU countries. Ethan had flown home on this day and I continued to drive around like a mad man in Europe by myself, like we did in the USA for three months, on a creative quest to connect with all sorts of people along the path and respect their traditions across cultures for the next month and a half. It was a beautiful solitude. Like therapy. Time to spend with myself and process my conscience on 4-8 hour drives. To get to know who I am, what I am becoming, and how my dreams are manifesting into reality each mile.

artworks.label: No. 180  —  October 4, 2023
artworks.title: Timing Is Everything
artworks.diary: On my way to Portugal I had a 6 hour layover in Amsterdam. It was risky but I thought I could go out of the airport to meet Futuradora and her daughter Novæ at this tennis court to make the video of the day and reunite with my friend from earlier in the project and honor her family this way. When I stepped out of the airport I met a kind taxi driver who promised to take me where I had to go and more. For those 6 hours we drove in traffic, there and back, to meet the mom and daughter. The driver sat in the car and watched my luggage while I was waiting for Novæ to finish her Tennis lessons. So Futuradora and I were talking and reminiscing about our shoot we did early on and how we came full circle. The uncanny cycles of life that keep us coming back to where we went to and from, and when we do return something changed, something is different, yet we feel the same. I did not know Futuradora was a mom until she had told me the day I landed so it was a surprise to see that side of her and to be able to gift her a vision of motherhood, from when we last met in the depths of the red light district reading slam poetry to the familial boundaries of a community tennis court in their backyard. Novæ finally joined us after her lesson and showed me her swing that knocked us out of the park! We shot this portrait then It was time to go as they had more errands to run. Timing is everything and we made it their at the perfect in between state. Before heading back to the airport, the taxi driver and I stopped off to the local head shop to roll up a couple Amnesia haze and Afghani hash joints, where I wandered into the nearest park for some privacy, which opened me up to nature but the haze really clouded my brain, then we grabbed a juice and bolted back to the airport without skipping a beat. It was pure synchronization on how we managed our precious time. Once I got to the airport I was way too stoned you can tell that the staff knew by the looks and smells of me and they were laughing at and making fun of me during the security transit. Kind of like how you would fuck with a friend when you are coming up on psychedelics “I’m freaking out man…” They were being playful and I was being paranoid, what else is new? The taxi driver did say my demeanour had changed from before to after smoking. I have to admit I did smoke 2 fat hash joints and it had me silenced, slow, and stunned for the flight to the next city. I learned my lesson, again. And did not pick up smoking for the rest of the time in Europe. To be clear minded and focused. To let the art lead the way and guide my direction. When you think you need something and it backfires, to only teach you that you were better off without it. What is that curiosity, or perhaps old pattern that keeps you thinking it is a good idea until you try it and then you wish you didn’t? For me that is what smoking has turned into. When do you realize you outgrow something you once loved, and thought you identified with? Does that change happen suddenly, or over a long period of time. How do you know when something stops serving you and becomes a poison to your growth? Or is life like a tennis match where you have to balance the ball between the net as you and a friend pass the ball to each other. Where no one wins, and the fun of it is just playing the game and hitting the ball over the net until you strike out. Balance, mediation, centeredness. Striving for that perfect harmony, practice a better serve.

artworks.label: No. 181  —  October 5, 2023
artworks.title: Night Fell Over Us
artworks.diary: Camila met me at the train station through a mutual friend from the NFT community. She is a digital illustrator and was showing me some of her animations. At the time we met she was just wrapping up her meme card. We spent the day together walking around her home city. Starting from the famous blue tiles that were elaborately designed as a mural for municipal buildings, churches, and train stations. There is something about that blue and white color combination that stops you in your tracks and takes your breath away. The same feeling when you first step foot into Portugal urban areas and you see the levels of details and patience that makes up the road and sidewalks. Millions of tiny tiles that make up the roadways and walkways in their intricate designs mapped out all around the city. Everywhere you look is art, the masonry is exquisite when you start to take notice of the little things that bring joy to the city. Camila brought me to her favorite street art areas with murals and graffiti. We climbed up on a ledge overlooking the main train station to catch the sunsetting slowly. The light was hitting her so beautifully, it felt like a movie scene. In fact, it was since we were making an unconventional film through portraits of people in their places! Light and flare creates this heavenly glow. You can taste the light without being blinded by the sun. The lens of the camera is protection where as the film takes the heat from the exposure. A perfect balance and harmony between glass and chemistry. How ever did scientists and artists figure this out hundreds of years ago? A mirrored reality, and one that is in motion. Cinema is magic. It shows us what happens over time through light and action. Is that why they are called actors? Camila and I continued on our way to watch the sunset from a higher perspective, one of the most beautiful views in the city. It was what felt like a dilapidated castle that turned into an urban garden by the locals. Recycling and reusing the space in new ones while honoring the old architectures. We watched the flowers bloom and the food grow while the light was descending from the sky. Boats passing by and seeing from an eagles eye, what was on the other side? Night fell over us. We descended down the spiralling roads to find a fork in the road where each of us started to head home. But before we did, Camila and I walked across what I like to call, Eiffel’s bridge. A massive landmark that connects two side of the city designed and constructed by Eiffel’s team. The guy who built the vertical Eiffel tower. Built a horizontal bridge that stretches into two parts of the city. The locals call it, Maria Pia Bridge. Camilla was getting annoyed I kept calling it Eiffel’s bridge. The one thing I noticed about Portugal that I truly admire is the cities adopt and integrate elements from other cities. Such as Eiffel’s bridge from Paris, Cristo sculpture from Brazil, and the Golden Gate bridge from San Francisco. To share ideas and implement them. There is something honorable about bringing home a piece of another place or culture. To make you feel like the world is one through what people have built all over the globe. The brink of a city inadvertently creating world peace through architecture? I like to think so. Let’s keep sharing ideas and honoring each others visions. Where we all feel like home anywhere you go.

artworks.label: No. 182  —  October 6, 2023
artworks.title: A Beautiful Mystery
artworks.diary: Joel and the kids brought me along on their family trip to Sintra to wander through the exquisite Quinta da Regaleira. A unique artistic palace with caves, lakes, underground passageways, and mystical initiation well, resembling underground tower. Starting at the pits of the stone spiral staircase. Where you look up and see the leaves and sky. It feels like some sort of portal where mystic rituals took place. Down in the lantern lit caverns an eerie ghostly presence with a bit of a malevolent residue stuck on to you. As beautiful as it was built, it felt like something nefarious had happened here. A sacrificial chamber. Right out of an Aleister Crowley Occult advent in the dead of night. One can imagine a slew of people in red robes carrying torches and trinkets. Does energy stay in one place, if so, then how long? Why do places make you feel this way, is it something we can pick up on, smell in the air? Or, the feeling of goosebumps. Where our Subconscious knows before we even understand why? Intuition. Something to trust in that gut feeling. Because our body knows before our mind can process. But how? One can only ask questions and experience for themselves what their feelings mean. We channeled awe and innocence. Is that enough to cleanse a space, to replace what may have happened there. How can a place be spiritually renewed in a sense? I believe anything can be healed if the attention and intention is brought to it. Praying and calling in the beings of light and goodness. Not just in the physical space, but within ourselves. To remember to be good simply by asking to become it. It is a choice, a decision to start or stop something. For this adventure with Joel’s family I asked them to hangout at the top of the stone well while I sat at the bottom in the star tiled center. Channeling their light. their blur, their presence through the camera to create a beautiful mystery. In the between states they stood at the top of the castello. Together as one. A father and his sons. Joel inspired me to be a dad like him. Showing them beauty and masonry that is still intact. It felt like we were in a giant chess match. The structure they were standing on were in the shape of a rook. The bishops took their place in the wishing well. The king and queen at their thrones in the palace. The pawns the tourists wandering about taking selfies and making memories. And then there is the knight, which is me, the knight of staffs. The responsibility and nobility to protect, scout, and create the path forward for the rest of the team.

artworks.label: No. 183  —  October 7, 2023
artworks.title: Okay, That Was 10 Seconds
artworks.diary: Yael asked me to tag along with her and the family to meet one of the most important living artists of our time, Ai Weiwei. She curated a show with him a few years ago in Los Angeles and his bronze Chinese zodiac sculptures are on public display at the LACMA. I first learned about this legendary artist while I was in art school at SVA early on in 2010 in contemporary photo history class. He is a renegade artist that fights for human rights and political activism to fight censorship and thwart authoritarian governments with his powerful vision and voice. His photography work was a big “fuck you” to the man, throwing up the middle finger in beautifully printed black and white photographs of historical landmarks like the Capitol building in DC or Tiananmen square in China. Ai works between all the mediums available to channel his critical and whimsical voice. Criticizing control, capitalism, culture through his subtle yet impactful touch. When we rolled up to his compound I was nervous. Not so much starstruck as I do have deep respect for this important artist. I spoke only when spoken to and was present for every word. It was not my meeting, since Yael was talking business about the next curation. I was there to hold space, and to hopefully make art with the most legendary artist alive. I sat quietly and was intimidated by his strong presence. He served us all tea, which was an admirable and kind gesture. I had my Rollieflex strapped to my chest and walked to his pool to give them space and make a few photos in his garden with his assistant. They called me over as it was time to walk to the construction site of his next major project. The wooden architecture, something like a grandeur theater. All made and put together by hand. Yael suggested now was the time to ask him to make his portrait. I did a big gulp and walked over to Ai Weiwei and shared a bit about the project I was working on. Hoping he would grant me 10 seconds to make his portrait. He nodded yes and started counting in his head. I did not waste any time and started shooting. As soon as we began it concluded; Ai said, okay that was 10 seconds. I held the shutter down as long as I could before he walked away. It was a funny and dreamlike moment for me. To include Ai in this project is a miracle to me and a testament to where I am on this creative path and even belong in the art world. To do what is right, to follow in the footsteps of someone like Ai Weiwei and make meaningful work about humanity. We spent the afternoon as a group and shortly after this video we departed back to the city. Unbeknownst to us all this day way change the world forever. A war had broke out in the middle east. How symbolic to make art with one of the most prolific, on this day, a political catastrophe. Halfway into the project exactly. Now is the time to start. To rise up and make the message clear. How can we create something that brings everyone together than tear us all apart? To learn from the best and to create something that unites our shared humanity. To end the conflicts and control, and move into a paradigm of truth and connection. This is the dream, that someday we can manifest into reality. Peace at last. Love forever. Working together to make the human race evolve into the universe than fighting on this beautiful Earth. I have faith that someday. We will overcome.

artworks.label: No. 184  —  October 8, 2023
artworks.title: A King and His Prince
artworks.diary: Father and son, is one. A man to be the hero of his boy. To show him the world as he grows old. When the boy becomes a man and takes care of his father as he once did. The cycle of life and love continue. From birth to death, yet never alone. Family is the truth, the origins, the trusted ones. The blood you share connects you, no matter how same or different you are to them. Did we choose our parents, these lessons, in the “before life.” The karmic cycle plays out and we all do our best. Is there a destiny, or a will to decide our fate? I have been thinking a lot about having a child these days. Who will carry the family name, is that ego or evolution? To have a child before my father goes to another world beyond this one. Thankfully, I found her. A loving partner in divine alignment for a sacred union to bring life back to Earth. To find true love in this life is a blessing and does not come fast or easy, especially when time is moving faster as you grow older. Decades become years, and years become days. Does the simulation of life accelerate when it comes to its end? For when its time to have my son, I pray to be like thee. A king and his prince, for one day to take up the family name for all its honor. From my dad to I, and I to my son. To create a lineage of Aversano’s, which may otherwise go extinct without me. Then what was it all for if I die before giving birth? It is human nature and perhaps our purpose to create more love in this world and bring forth the next generation of humanity. Will that future generation of humanity reach the stars outside of Earth? Were we destined to leave home or embrace the supernova?

artworks.label: No. 185  —  October 9, 2023
artworks.title: When You Do What You Love, You Will Find True Love
artworks.diary: When you do what you love, you will find true love.

artworks.label: No. 186  —  October 10, 2023
artworks.title: Flâneur
artworks.diary: It was an early morning meeting with my photographer friend, Omar. He has been living in Barcelona with his wonderful wife for work. We took in the morning golden glow to make art together on a flaneur walk of the city. Before breakfast we strolled down a some alleyways and happened on a well lit intersection People pushing strollers, walking by, biking through, as Omar stands and shoots those same people passing out of frame and turns his lens to make a portrait of me between the edits. When a street photographer walks the town we are looking for the constant unfolding of action with harmony of light and composition in the frame. Where it all comes together. Life in that 1/125th of a second, like no other. Henri Cartier Bresson once said, “Light does not hit the same wall twice.” As the Earth spins around the sun, it is true that no moment will ever be the same again. With a camera we have the ability to make symbolic sense of the ensuing chaos of spontaneity. Omar captures this type of presence, this sort of street magic in his work. Seeing him work in his hyper-focused presence while engaged in conversation as we walk through the city. He knows the shot he is looking for, he knows his target and like an archer, calls the shot, draws back the arrow, and fire as they move closer to his frame. Photography is the transition between past and future. Does the present truly exist if it continues onward? The photo is the stillness, a fragment of something that once was for somewhere beyond to ponder. Photography is an expression, not just how you see the world but how you feel it too. The click of the shutter releases some small part of satisfaction in the brain. A chance to remember, a choice to become a mirror. They say the moment you make a photograph of something it dies, but perhaps it provides an eternal life?

artworks.label: No. 187  —  October 11, 2023
artworks.title: Romeo and Juliet
artworks.diary: How does love grow between two people? In the garden of eden as the warmth of the human touch beneath the golden sun beaming down on the brows of couple in love like Romeo and Juliet was in Verona. Where two people become a family. A connection that deepens over time and experience. To grow old together, to love another even into the afterlife of the sacred altar. We are brought into this life through mystic union, through love and the making of it. Romance and care, excitement and wonder fills the air between two loving doves. Drunk in love like a drug that hits the brain so deep that it makes the body fuzzy with butterflies. What is love than an attraction and a belonging to one another? The type of love we all crave and dream for. To be wanted and to want. The dance to find your partner in a crowd of a billion others roaming this earth. Yet we find each other, every time. In every life, like a magnetic field. Gravity brings us together, beyond our control perhaps the will of the universe, something greater than us. It is the power, the force of love that unites the hearts to beat together. To love each other no matter what or where. There will always be room for love. We are made of it, as is the universe. God is love and love is good. It is our purpose, and art is an extension of love. It is how we dream and how we see the world. To love it so much that we need to express it. Bleeding love until the day we die. Another dimension, astral planes to explore new ways to love again. In this life or next, love is the way into the light.

artworks.label: No. 188  —  October 12, 2023
artworks.title: Terribly Beautiful
artworks.diary: This time in Italy was a one way ride from the north to south. Starting in Venice and ending where my family is from, my fathers side of the Aversano fisherman heritage on the coast of Napoli. A self discovery into familial roots. To understand the nature and culture of where my father, Alfonso, is from. Diving into the country that my dad grew up. There are many Aversanos scattered across the Amalfi coast. There is a small town near Napoli called Averso. Is this a common link? Often last names were of people and the villages they were from. On my way to the south I stopped into the romantic city of Florence. Wandered through the night down different alleyways and plazas. In the morning I came across a watery dam that scattered droplets over a wall. I was suffering deeply at this place, the tears poured down my face as they water was running down the slope. The sun mirrored on the surface. It was terribly beautiful. What broke me down? My project being held hostage without any light at the end of the tunnel. How would you feel if the work you were bleeding, sweating, and working towards was held against you at ransom? Someone who was meant to help, turned to hurt. Why? It is not clear, greed and misfortune. I called my friend who helped me retrieve the film a few days later. Thankfully, it was saved by the angels. But, in that short time, it was hell with no way out. After wiping away my tears and got right up. My phone rang and it was my photography friend Giulio who was local to Florence. I drove to meet with him outside of the main city at this beautiful garden with a serene fountain. We walked and talked and made art at the fountain. From water to water, from Heaven to Hell, down from the bottom to the top of the hill. The water is carried from the Earth to our souls an back. A cycle of life, the motion of water moves fluidly, each drop in the ocean travels the world and back around. We are made of this water, as is our home planet. Water, just like love is our life force.

artworks.label: No. 189  —  October 13, 2023
artworks.title: The Queen’s Quarters
artworks.diary: Once I left Florence I drove to the wests coast to visit Pisa. There was a pizza shop before entering the grounds of the leaning tower. I grabbed a slice and headed into the landmark. It felt right to have a piece of pizza at the leaning tower of pisa. Made some photographs and wondered how this is sinking over time and leaning. A distortion of reality to see a building falling yet standing in place. My next stop was an artists dream. The public art garden based on all 78 of the tarot archetypes. Mosaics of tiles and mirrors to create massive surreal figures. I went from card to card following the looping paths around the art park. Once I saw all the characters and making double exposures I knew I had to make a portrait of the person of the day at this beautiful site. There were a handful of visitors and was waiting for the right moment. I circled the park to revisit a few tarot cards considered to be the location for the shoot. I visited the sun, then the hermit, back to the ace and finally ending at the Queen’s quarters. I walked into a makeshift kitchen and bedroom and it was covered in tiles and mirrors reflecting the objects in a home. I saw this woman in a rainbow dress and her colors matched the shimmering tiles outside the palace. She was with her husband and did not speak any english. This was the moment I knew she was the one! The person to represent this colorful place on this sunny day. A gut feeling, as there was no one else in that space made me feel this way, this vision. You have to trust that feeling because that is harmony with the universe. It is reading the signs outside and signals within. So, I walked outside to wait for them to come out of the hierophants heart. It was just Deborah and I approached her nervously, she couldn’t understand what I was saying in english so I started to speak Italian, since my father spoke it at home and I studied it in high-school. I said her outfit was so wonderful and it matches the rainbows in the park. She was dancing like a disco in the outdoor atrium. Her husband came along smiling and shook my hand then spoke to me in bits of broken English and I spoke to him in broken Italian. I made a Polaroid of them as a gift when the sun had set and I jetted off to the ancient city of Rome.

artworks.label: No. 190  —  October 14, 2023
artworks.title: All Empires Do Fall
artworks.diary: Here we are at the Roman Colosseum. The first time I ever visited was back in 2016 with my father and sister on the first family trip since my childhood. This place is a totem in time, of greatness and preservation. And a reminder that all empires do fall to the wayside to make room for the new generations. Just as everyone dies, companies die, civilizations change. The traces are still here in stone. To learn and study. What went wrong, and what traditions remained? What will come of us and our great cities in a thousand years, let alone the next 100? Mirko met me further away from all the tourists and con artists. He sat on a stone in a garden where you can see the stadium and the gateway. He was going in depth of a project he was working on to expose the mafia. Mirko knew the danger he was in, and he still went deeper into the rabbit hole. For his work, for justice. What is the right thing when those in charge are corrupted? What is the answer when things are controlled by superior powers? Where is the truth and whose narrative are we living obediently by. When a man is given power, it corrupts. Like a white lie that turns into pathology. It is not suddenly, it is over time. Standards deviate, and there are no consequences. Where does the journalist, the artist make his name? To confront those dangers and give the people the truth to set them free of fear and rule. He thought of himself as a martyr for taking on this assignment. There is always a balance of forces, causes and effects that maintain perfect harmony; equilibrium. When chaos fits into order and broken again. Creation and destruction. Selflessness and selfishness. It is merely a dance on the grey line that separates both sides. Even though they exist on the same plane and made up from the same origins. It is all one under a Jungian sun.

artworks.label: No. 191  —  October 15, 2023
artworks.title: To Live Without Fear
artworks.diary: Finally, after a long drive, I arrived at the walkway beside the sea of my father’s home town in Napoli! Walked from one end to another during a morning walk to feel the fresh breeze and smell the salt in the air. Sat by the water on the ledge to meditate and listen to the sounds. Tapping into what my dad grew up with, spreading down the roots again. Made my way past the large castles and barracks to an Italian flag directly in front of Mount Vesuvius. A live Volcano that casted the city, people, and pets of Pompeii in ash when it last devastating eruption. When I look from afar at this giant red ant hill awaiting to erupt again, one can think of their mortality as they are hiking up to the rim to see what is inside. You never know when your last day will be, to be afraid and not do something or be free and die doing what you love. Those are the risks of taking a chance, or not. Where the reward is to see beauty in its purest form. To live without fear is to have trust in the moment and on the path you decide to be; Timing and energy. As I stood thinking these thoughts looking out to living mountain, Dominika and her husband found me. She was all dressed up in red, matching her hair too. Parts of the flag and the symbol of hot magma. Everything fell into place without any planning, it was trusting the moment and the timing where all the pieces to make an artwork or an image perfectly aligned. Dominika became the life force, the lava that spills from the heart of the volcano. The wind blowing the flag behind her honoring Italy in all her beauty where the all the elements come together. The water of the sea, the fire of the heart, the soil of the volcanic land, and the air that blows invisibly until the grey smoke fills the sky.

artworks.label: No. 192  —  October 16, 2023
artworks.title: La Famiglia
artworks.diary: La famiglia Italiana.

artworks.label: No. 193  —  October 17, 2023
artworks.title: Oracle
artworks.diary: When I arrived in Athens, Greece my friend Nickos, who is a photographer, picked me up and was with his dear friend, Florencia. She was a fashion model. It was perfect harmony to be riding in the car with a portrait photographer and Grecian super model to a surprise location Nickos had in mind for sunset. After an hour, as the sun was nearing a set, we arrived at the Temple of Poseidon; The great god of the oceans. His temple ruins from the 5th Century BCE were set on top of the hill with panoramic perspectives of the sea. There were a few people there and the sunlight was thinning quick. There were golden rays illuminating the Doric columns. Florencia jumped on a sitting rock and we started to create her portrait. Without any direction, she started to move. Like an oracle in Delphi summoning prophecies, or an Athenian goddess calling upon her soldiers for might in the Homeric battles of the Trojan wars. She moved with the beauty of the sun and wind at this ancient site. Honoring the ancestors and gods that came before. The dancing rituals by the fire lighthouse for navigating the sailors in the night. As the red streaked across the sky and mirrors on the surface of the sea. Waves rippling across shimmering specks of crystalline lights from the sky reflected above. Where you can see the rainbow through the angles of the star and the dust in the atmosphere. She stopped dancing and we sat and watched this sublime sunset until all the colors disappeared into the speckled cosmic rain of the galaxies in the starry night. We departed this ancient place and made our way back home. Where a gyro was waiting for me. Reminding me of the Greek restaurant my mother used to work at and take me, Athens Square. A slice of my childhood brought back to life through where I was because when in Greece is like when I was in Rome.

artworks.label: No. 194  —  October 18, 2023
artworks.title: Columns from Afar
artworks.diary: In the afternoon I walked to visit the Parthenon, up the hill and through the olive groves. It is a glorious building, even surrounded by scaffolding to keep it upright while rebuilding for over 20 years. Imagine a once in a lifetime chance to see a sacred site and to see it covered. Though the beauty shined through at the top of the hill, where one can see a 360 degree view of the entire city of Athens. I met a man and his family while I was making double exposures. I tend to make portraits of anyone who compliments me while walking by, as it is a nod of noticing and some sort of approval. To co-create with those who reach out, as if the universe itself is lending a hand of connection. We shot a few portraits and moved on to the next temple besides the main. I was waiting for Nickos to arrive, but he was delayed to our meeting time. So I scurried over to the hill nearby as the park officials started to close down the site. There was this rock at the bottom of the stairs where people were taking selfies, reading books, and taking a second to meditate. I sat with my cameras and watched the sky changing colors, facetimed my dad, and then got the call from Nickos saying he was here. We found each other at the halfway mark. I originally wanted to shoot him with the Parthenon up close, and since he was late we could not re-enter. Even though the building was under construction it would have looked off anyway. The blessing was meeting in the middle, where you can see the exquisite columns from afar, with no scaffolding in site. The idea shifted scales and perspectives, but the original idea remained. To honor him, his home, and the sacred that coveted their fair city. It was perfect. In the end, we can imagine the perfect shot, or the perfect scene. And when the moment presents itself, it still happens but in a different way than we could ever think. It is how we can adapt and still achieve the same wishes or results. To be an artist is to be a great improviser when things don’t go your way, reframe, and use what you have in front of you.

artworks.label: No. 195  —  October 19, 2023
artworks.title: PFP
artworks.diary: It was the first time meeting my internet friend, who remains anonymous. We first met a a park where he grew up in Athens with fond memories from his childhood. He was smoking a cigarette and wore his hoodie of his pfp of his hoodie smoking his cigarette. When does your digital identity become your real one and vice versa? It is a symbol of being one with representation where the worlds of digital and analog connect as one. My anon friend brought me to his home and showed me his iconic art collection as he and another collector from the NFT space started a digital art museum together. He was just getting into collecting physical pieces for his walls and digital art history and conceptual books from this art movement. Giannis is someone to follow along if you are interested in art focused collecting and innovation. He packed me up a bowl of local hash and rolled cigars of weed mixed in for the evening. Until the end of the night in Psycho we brought our online friendship into real life and cemented that bond. The best of both worlds in a burgeoning digital art movement. It feels like only once in your life time will you see a monumental art movement during a decade or generation and we are the artists and collectors advocating for this blockchain future. For truth, transparency, and authenticity.

artworks.label: No. 196  —  October 20, 2023
artworks.title: Just Keep Going
artworks.diary: From Greece to Bulgaria I made my way through into the Baltic states. I met a young woman named Liliyana in Sofia. An online friends daughter was from there and was going through the process of studying to become a lawyer. After her final exam, we met outside in the evening on the side of the road nearby her school by an illuminated billboard that lit her during our video shoot, as well as the ambient light from the headlights of passing cars. An odd place to make a portrait but also a challenge well accepted. It was late after landing in Bulgaria and did not have much time until the next day to find someone. It was a long day of travel since I had left Athens and drove up the coast towards Thessaloniki where I dropped off the rental car and boarded a flight over the boarder. I would’ve drove but I wasn’t allowed to enter the country with a car due to their policies so had to impromptu fly to the capital. It was a long and lovely drive though, beside the sea the whole way north. Liliyana met with me for a few minutes before she had to meet her husband for dinner. It was a quick meeting, a quick shoot. And all I needed was ten seconds to create: the beauty of this project was the people who chose to be involved understood the premise and trusted me almost instantly. I believe the camera has that power, a film camera, and a pure intention can go a long way. It’s like the universe sets up the pitch for you to hit a grand slam when you take on a project with a theme or a story. The pieces and people fall together as you make your way through all the moments and all of the unknown, the uncertainty is not scary, it’s exciting with a scoop of vision and a teaspoon of faith, and a pinch of trust in the process. The recipe to success is simple. Just keep going. Even when you don’t know, just create with what you have in front of you to make the shot, to make that painting, to write that song, to code that machine. We are the authors of our destiny. What is the story you want to tell? Who are the people you want to honor, and share that with? To realize a big dream is to take the first baby step towards getting there. And as you keep going. Day by day, work to work, you’ll be further along than whence you started. Whatever that project is, or idea you have, and even the person you want to forgive, now is the time to start. Because there is no better time than the present moment!

artworks.label: No. 197  —  October 21, 2023
artworks.title: Twins
artworks.diary: A morning drive from Bulgaria to Romania. On my way through one of the borders, the maps led me to a bridge that was facing a drought. Right before the border was a gas station and this woman in broken english told me it was closed and had to go a different way. She recommended me go to the other border pass that was 2 more hours away north, I called my artist friend named, None, and broke him the news it would take longer than expected to get to Craiova. Once I finally pulled into town hopped in the car at the parking lot and surprised me with good news. Originally, we planned for him to be in the portrait series. An hour before I arrived, None serendipitously met a mother with her twin daughters at the gallery exhibition he was curating. He said that they will meet us at the church in the center of the village to be part of the project! The girls played a ring-go-around in the holy presence of the towns sanctity. Their mother standing by watching the photoshoot taking place. None, speaking in Romanian, telling the mother Denisa, about my Twin Flames project. Throughout all of my projects I tend to return to the same people, or the same location years later. When completing older projects and starting new ones, I hide some easter eggs; like including Twins from the Birthday project into Twin Flames 6 years later. Or, A set of twins, or twins shot separately in the same project. Such as Twins from Twin flames in Smoke and Mirrors, and twins I did not shoot for Twin Flames to be included in Smoke to honor the past ideas and communities I have created with. In this current series, Moments of the Unknown. Some may notice the traits of, Everyday is a Gift, Twin Flames, or Smoke and Mirrors. As they represent the people who were involved in the past. And those who embody that idea who were not in past projects. Happy Birthdays, Twins and Mystics. Weaving stories from past to future. How do we age, and how do places look different, and sometimes the same. An exploration into repetition. Where does change happen? The present is the place that almost never happened. Only once, then forever shifting and fleeting, awaiting our awakening and noticing of awe.

artworks.label: No. 198  —  October 22, 2023
artworks.title: Dracula’s Castle
artworks.diary: Samo met me all the way from Bucharest at Transylvania. It was the dead of night with not a soul around. The Castle clinging to the mountain was illuminated by a strange orange glow. The town was dark and the castle was reflecting tungsten light. The evening before the adventure to count Dracula’s castle we had a proper Romanian meal from the Baltics. Samo and I feasted like kings. We have known one another for a few years and this was our first meeting. He was working with me as a moderator and protected the community of our discord chatroom. It was nice to meet someone i’ve only known online. It is funny how we can trust someone we never met in real life, and spend so much time working together online. Ironic, yet efficient. Samo and I went to our hotels before waking up for sunrise to tour Dracula’s castle. Since it was close to Halloween this place really felt perfect for the holiday. The village was prepping for the Hallow eve festival that was coming next week. We walked around in the field before ascending into the interior. We were scoping out the garden to find the right place to shoot. As we waited for the light to pass from the clouds we observed a group of women making selfies, a few children playing and climbing, a couple of lovers reflecting in the pond. Everyone was enjoying themselves in their own sweet way. We watched and made photos at the passing of the day, The sun shined through softly and we outlined the royal contours against Samos brave face. The shoot was done and the film had run out. We walked into the chambers and halls of the stone towers. The legend of Dracula, Vladimir. A fierce warrior that drank the blood of his enemies. Became a nightmare in these wooded parts. The vampiric archetype was born here between the stone mason. Urban legends said he lived for a thousand years whence returned from the dead. Bats are his minions, and blood is his food. They say that you should not invite a vampire in your home or you’ll be struck, but what if you entered the home of the vampire? And subvert their power and danger. How to heal a vampire before it’s too late and they eat the stake? With love. Because there is no more powerful force than the ancient resonance of the highest frequency. Negative to positive. A life renewed to be pure again.

artworks.label: No. 199  —  October 23, 2023
artworks.title: Living Sundial
artworks.diary: It just so happened to be the anniversary of the Hungarian revolution in Budapest when I drove to the city from a meeting from the author of “Atlas of Beauty” in western Romania. My buddy Andrew and a couple of his friends and I walked around the city at some of the memorial sites and sculptures. He pointed out a few bullet holes in the cement walls as we headed to the water. You can feel the heaviness in the air, yet it is a city with rich culture and sovereignty. It has great potential. It is somewhere I feel like I could live. Felt like living in a Baltic Berlin. Andrew stood in the street during our history lesson walkthrough the city. His black solar flared silhouette and his silver shadow reflected on the cement; Like a clock ticking as the cars pass, an hourglass, a human living sundial marked by the light through the street. A balance in the frame of a man and his shadow. Plato’s allegory of the cave became the theater of the street. Wherever the light hits, is revealed in the real. And the shadows are but an age old attachment, a fixture made of the dark. So according to Socrates, which one is the real? As both are true to the eye and mind of the beholder. Reliant on experience, perception, and subjectivity.

artworks.label: No. 200  —  October 24, 2023
artworks.title: Crypto Valley
artworks.diary: The team at 1 of 1 hosted me in Zug for a couple days to take rest and regroup at their office. Zug is a wonderful place to focus on work and hit up the occasional swiss bagna with the bros at the end or middle of a work day. They call it the “Crypto Valley.” Perhaps because Ethereum and other early Bitcoin business man adopted it here in this sophisticated little German town off the mountainous lake. I hung around the office smoking hash pipes with The digital art connoisseurs, Lukas and Ozan. They rang the gong to bring in the team for uplifting boost to carry through the work day on zoom calls, meetings, and audits. Deals are always being made in these glass hallways. Always close the deal. The future of art guided by the conversations in their conference rooms. A passionate team of art lovers and believers in this movement. Verifying nodes for the NFTs and validating the art in major institutions. From the MoMa in the big apple to the Serpentine across the pond, this team, is at the helm of the boards. And this office is the safe haven for artists. To relax, to make new art, to get the job done. When working together. Art and business. Creative and Collector. We are one. We are writing the new chapter.,Together.

artworks.label: No. 201  —  October 25, 2023
artworks.title: Meditations
artworks.diary: Excerpts by the great Marcus Aurelius from the book, Meditations. A book of wisdom and lessons that sir Ryan Zurrer gifts to all of his friends and allies. These quotes are from Book 1. Ryan’s preferred section on Gratitude for the teachers and elders. For that is how we got to where we are today, as we build for tomorrow. A man with his beloved wife and children playing in their garden. “To the gods I am indebted for having good grandfathers, good parents, good teachers, good friends — and that I was preserved from the path of pride and folly.” “From my adoptive father: gentleness and unshakable adherence to decisions once deliberated upon. Never to be content with mere appearances, but to act from reason and justice; to show no sign of anger or passion, yet to be full of humanity.” “From my grandfather Verus I learned good morals and the government of my temper. From the reputation and remembrance of my father, modesty and a manly character. From my mother, piety and beneficence, and abstinence, not only from evil deeds, but even from evil thoughts; and further, simplicity in my way of living, far removed from the habits of the rich.”

artworks.label: No. 202  —  October 26, 2023
artworks.title: Where Is Home When You Leave Town?
artworks.diary: At the clock tower in the center of the stone city of Zurich with the daughter and granddaughter of the Shamans from Peru. Lesley. She moved to Switzerland from her home in Cusco for university. She wanted to become a photographer, and became a model. Met her husband and became a Swiss citizen. We first met in 2016 when she was a young girl at the San Pedro sanctuary at the Temple of the Moon. While in a ceremony of the grandfather plant medicine, I made a portrait of her face with a double exposure of the sky. It was her blue head in the blue sky turned into a Cyanotype print for the Cactus Diaries. I once gifted her a twin reflex camera to give her a film camera for school. It’s nice to see someone you met since they were young grow up through your artwork, through the timeline of life, and every stage as we learn and grow. Her family is my spirit family. The tribe of the cactus have green hearts, like the chakra. Where is home when you leave town? How is family formed through love and connection? Being a kid in your village and becoming an adult in a big city for school or work. A lifetime that becomes longer than where you once was.

artworks.label: No. 203  —  October 27, 2023
artworks.title: Another Brick in the Wall
artworks.diary: In the morning I arrived into Tallinn from Zurich. Found myself in a beautiful airport heading toward the next rental car to begin the next leg of visiting the remaining countries of the EU on my solo road trip. From Estonia to Croatia and everything in between. My buddy Ian’s family resides in Tallinn so I asked if he knew some friends I should meet with. Therefore he connected me with Herkki & his daughter Lillian. Through Herkki I met a mysterious red headed woman who was an actress and a model. She had shown me around her studio while Herkki took a call, we talked for a while then she left her studio to go to a dinner party and took down my digits to meet another day to shoot. Herkki offered me tea after his call and showed me his studio sauna and some of his original artworks from the 90’s. I made portraits of Herkki, and he made portraits of me. That is what photographers do when they get together. They turn there lens on the other. I believe it is to connect. To see, and acknowledge the light inside and that lands on you. To see you, truly. To find something beautiful about the person and accentuate it to make them feel good. To be loved. He is a prolific photographer and even took me to a restaurant and then a bar which were showing his photographs on the walls. He is a legend in this stone and cold city. I originally made a portrait of just Herkki. Then seconds later his daughter, Lillian finally arrived. So I did a shot with both of them together. I blended his solo part, then she magically appears as he sits down. Is like a metaphor for having children. Once you are done and relaxed, they appear! A family portrait, of a father and his daughter Where the apple does not fall far from the tree in the orchard of a castle of trust. Unconditional love is just like another brick in the wall that is the cement that holds the fortress of fortitude together.

artworks.label: No. 204  —  October 28, 2023
artworks.title: Under a Blue Glow
artworks.diary: A cold kiss is bittersweet in the grey clouds of snow. You walk towards me, then away just as soon. For a moment there, we were awake at night in the dark under a blue glow listening to Cave’s tunes. A potent mushroom melted my brain as it met your sparkling eyes above the champagne glass. From the party down the road, a friend’s going away. It’s late now, and time doesn’t even exist. So, I leave to live close by up in the sky to my temporary home. A thump and a thud walking down the stairs. The heart awakens yet the trust is still new and broken. I see her red hair, red lipstick in the mirror. I go this way, and you go yours. Then I will see you in the morning to shoot at 11:11. No, she says, I’ll come with you.

artworks.label: No. 205  —  October 29, 2023
artworks.title: Peace Treaty
artworks.diary: A peace treaty between 3D Cryptopunks and Bored Ape Yacht Club in the center of a Latvian farmers market. Made with a pair of enlarged lego masks. To represent digital PFPs in real life as their identity. There is an old saying In the NFT community, we are all going to make it (WAGMI!) And if we do come together as Yuga did with these pixelated juggernauts, we will ride into the Ether of Valhalla.

artworks.label: No. 206  —  October 30, 2023
artworks.title: Live Forever
artworks.diary: I met up with a couple of punks in Warsaw at one of the most historic hotels for a meeting for lunch. When we wrapped up, Jakob and I walked around old town. We bought some Labradorite crystals and expressionist art by local street art vendors selling their beautiful paintings of the town. As we walked and talked around his hometown looking for the perfect place to make a portrait. He was telling me how he was the “next” Steve Jobs. In health tech, life extension to be exact. His goal was to create technology so we do not die, and can live forever. As advantageous as it sounded I asked him how humans can achieve immortality, and also asked even though death is natural. Don’t humans, at some point, “need” to die? If we fear the unknown and the beyond. How do we know what we are missing because just like life, death is part of the process. Whatever dimensions await our consciousness, or the oneness of the universe upon the moment of our death. As one would hear from common stories during near death experiences. Are humans supposed to live forever? Is life now in the eye of the beholder. If we had the choice to decide how long to live. To grow younger as we age. A perfect median for a man like Benjamin Button. Genetically engineering what age you want to be, as we decide the genders and amount of offspring you want before the zygote is formed? It sound like a sci-fi dream, but can it be a reality at some point? Can humans map out DNA and manipulate it to live forever? What is forever, how much life is enough before you long for death? What then becomes of time if you can live continuously? What about expanding populations and limited material resources? So many questions with no answers but ideas, Finally, Are living things supposed to die, or live in this dimension forever? Do we traverse the cosmos as long as light years, since we can live as long to reach the stars? Jakob, our new and improved Steve Jobs, says we can and he is working on the tech to do so.

artworks.label: No. 207  —  October 31, 2023
artworks.title: Stalemate
artworks.diary: Early in the morning, the clerk at the hotel lobby helped me devise a plan to reach the border of Poland and Ukraine. The team showed me the closest entry that I can park the car and walk across the immigration on foot leaving the rental in a strange lot. After a few hours I found the location and called my photography friend, Shcheglova, to plan the meeting in Ivano-Frankivsk. Her twin friends Tania and Ann set me up with a driver from the border to their artist compound. He was a young Ukranian gentleman who did not speak any english, yet we spoke through a phone translator app the entire drive. This went on for about 4 hours, as we drove through the farmlands and passed the cities till the sunset and we reached the city with the sirens and planes overhead. Tania, one of the twins greeted me with a big hug. We had been talking online for a month before I arrived. She was the mastermind to help me visit to Ukraine. Her and her sister Ann with her black puppy walked me up and around their artist compound filled with a large community of young people getting together in a time of war. I learned that it is safer in numbers. To be together and work toward a common goal. Protection and unity. Why be home alone and hear the bombs fall, when you can gather together, rise up, and build a solution. It was inspiring seeing so many young people working together in this building. From creating supplies to innovating lamps made of Kombucha, Coming together under the roof from the conditions of life and death and war was the catalyst. Maybe it’s true, something bad needs to be happening so we have no choice but to come together for the greater good and turn the traumatizing and terrible into great strength. We are all in this together. The twins showed me around their art studio and sat them down with a chess set with the match conveying a stalemate. To represent the conflict of Russia and Ukraine. Does anyone really win in a war? It is a blockage, a blockade. How do imaginary borders make us different even if we look the same? As the war continues, they are up against the odds. The board game and pieces are black and white, but life is made of color. The twins tower over the game holding one another. Happy Halloween to some, but the only day that exists to others. Tania and I went to her home and told me some of her war stories of how her and her twin Ann were interviewed by Vogue because of the incredible support to the elders and animals in Ukraine. Protecting these families from the rubble and giving them new homes. Building cement and solutions for their citizens to continue to thrive and survive. The night ended with Tania burning Russian literature and her friend busting through the door with a German Shepard because her phone was off. The taxi man pulled up for me and I took this sign to leave in the middle of the night. He jetted back to the border after getting stopped by Police a couple of times. I crossed again with my cameras and my heart beating in my chest. I made it back to Poland and drove through the night thinking about what just fucking happened.

artworks.label: No. 208  —  November 1, 2023
artworks.title: Nightmare Before Christmas
artworks.diary: I drove through the night to meet my twin friends, Katerina & Marie. We met in 2018 when I was shooting Twin Flames. We were all vegan and bonded over good food and art. They called themselves witches and practiced dark arts and magic. When I arrived I noticed they had shaved their heads clean to an orange fuzz. We smoked a few joints of their fathers weed plants and drank some tea over a tarot reading. Sitting in the kitchen was their vegan model friend Adenike. We all hung out and had lunch in the kitchen. We went on a walk into their garden, then their backyard which lead to a small stream and a nature trail. The twins brought their orange locks to be part of the shoot. They wore matching orange Nightmare Before Christmas Jack Skellington hoodies and swung their dreads from side to side. It was the day after Hallow’s eve, but today really felt like a Halloween treat. Adenike was hiding in the shot behind the leaves of the tree. This was the shot the twins asked me to shoot. Their hair as the portal to connecting two projects across a decades time. How do characters appear and re-appear over time in different ideas and projects? Is art the life we live and the evidence we show of it? Photography and video are the tools I use. Like a time traveler decoding the present moment through light and beauty. The present moment never died, it was extended into infinity. When we integrate and interweave projects. It is like a Quantum leap through time and space. The thing that changes are the people and their features, how we grow and how we age. What does a memory become if it can be updated? The twins led me back to their art room waving their dreads like a air traffic control signaler on a runway guiding a plane to land amidst the fog on the turmak. Right to the couch. They saw how exhausted and unslept I was so offered me to stay the night and take a nap. They tucked me in and put me to bed. I was laying in the dark for 5 hours surrounded by their art. When I awoken it was time for me to go on towards Austria. So the twins packed me up a vegan lunch and a couple of joints for the road and off I went into the night going from rest stop to rest stop taking breaks to cool down my fatigue. Then arrived in Austria and crashed out until the morning shined through the windows.

artworks.label: No. 209  —  November 2, 2023
artworks.title: Level 30 Unlocked
artworks.diary: Level 30 Unlocked. Life is like a video game. As we age we level up. We gain experience when learning new skills and going to new parts of the globe that are unmapped. Is this a simulation, a dream, or a dream inside of a simulation? Perhaps none. Life is as it is. We all start at level 1. As we go along we forge friendships that last for long. We play this game together. Some higher, some lower. Yet we play by the same rules of physics. What character are you in this server called Earth? and what is your main mission. I am the type of player who likes to complete all the side quests and leveling up my skills and gear before I take on the main game. 100% completion. What does that mean here? Level 30 unlocked; now. How much further to go? From World of Warcraft to living in the real world. Creating art breaks us out of the game, like a neo in the matrix, immersed into a whole nother universe outside our head.

artworks.label: No. 210  —  November 3, 2023
artworks.title: Dancing with Her Shadow
artworks.diary: From Vienna I drove into the night. Faced a fierce purple thunderstorm and flood from the sky that I could not see the road. I stopped at a rest stop to nap every couple hours as I was falling asleep. It was raining heavily on my way to Croatia. Then the downpour stopped though the clouds remained grey. Diana met me at night to help me get settled in. The next day we met up in the village in the hills of Split. She was generous to have her cousin house me during my overnight stay. We walked around the city with her friend and her son. Seeing and smelling the ancient city. A castle made of stone and sand. Home of the Game of Thrones even though I have never seen the show. I found this beautifully lit dome where tourists take selfies. Observed the angles of the light and asked Diana to play in the illuminated path dancing with her shadow. It was pure poetry of feeling in the frame. The tour continued and we saw more ancient relics like sun clocks and mysterious structures. We marched upwards for a tea to watch sunset at the top of the hill overlooking the majesty of the view and medieval architecture. There was an old cemetery nearby and went through to notice the star of david on the graves and that it was all people buried from the Jewish community. I immediately thought about my Jewish mother and prayed to the family of the ancestors above and below. We continued into the night and parted ways after the art show at the hotel by the water. I walked home alone enjoying the winding castle paths back to my house to get some rest for flight to Berlin to finish the remaining countries of the EU tour.

artworks.label: No. 211  —  November 4, 2023
artworks.title: Algorithms and Plotters
artworks.diary: Back in Berlin I revisited my gallerist, Anika from when we made her portrait during my exhibition. Now, next door at the gallery inside the mall, was her boyfriend Andre surrounded by a group exhibition of Anikas expansive artist roster. One name in particular, Herbert Franke, whose artwork Drakula graced the walll. Herbert was a pioneer and recently passed away. When I was running Quantum Art we curated his original computer artwork from the 80s minted as NFTs. It was one of the most successful drops on the platform. It was also the first time he saw massive appreciation and success from the art he has been innovating all of his life. His artwork is cemented on the blockchain and will always honor the legacy he created with algorithms and plotters. He was one of the first and best to do it. It is a great honor to have helped him while he was still alive and bring the love and awareness to his work. He got to see people fawning over his historic work. So, I ended up collecting that very work that was hanging on the wall to represent that connection, that bond we shared through his art and helping him mint it on the blockchain. This piece is like a relic of supporting other artists and having a piece to carry the past into the future. Rest in Peace Herbert, and thank you Anika for bringing us together to make his dreams come true and his family a foundation to preserve his memory and work.

artworks.label: No. 212  —  November 5, 2023
artworks.title: The Moment It Takes on a New Life
artworks.diary: In the middle of the day I met my friend Lily at the C/O Berlin photography museum. She brought her friend Christina along to see a Mary Ellen Mark retrospective exhibition. I always thought this german museum had some of the best contemporary and conceptual photography shows in the world. A place I would aspire to show my photography someday. Mary had passed away a few years ago and was an icon in the photography world in the class of Arbus with a photojournalistic eye. From the South to the psych wards of the US in black and white to the slums and brothels of India in color she documented the fringes of societal norms. There were some amazing photographs of Mother Teresa with a shining cross tending to the sick and poor. There was one large room that really struck me deeply. It was her large format polaroids. Two projects together. 20x24 Polaroids of high schoolers and their prom dates in black and white. The other in divine alignment with my photography was her twin portraits at twinsburg, ohio during the twins festival in color. I loved how Mary played with the same medium with different projects in different tones as if expressing the inner and outer worlds of intimacy and connection. Conditional and Unconditional love in a way. Conditional as an agreement in black and white like pen and ink on paper, unconditional as a rainbow expressing and exposing the world rich and colorfully. You would rarely see her color photography until later in her work. What makes the shift over time? From light and shadow to color compliments? How does an idea reflect the way you convey it through saturation or not. Lily and I had a long conversation about the prom portraits. Who was the stronger person in the frame in the relationship. Who was the leader and the lover. She said the women held all the power in the pictures by the way they were standing and looking into the camera. The man was happy and proud, the woman full of questions. It was a heated debate. Then there was one picture of a man with a few women which made us laugh and found our agreement that he was just a player at the prom. Christina found a delicate portrait of a woman by herself. It was the only one like that. The woman in the picture looked just like her. When she put on the headphones to listen to the story of the girl, as this was part of the exhibition, she learned that she was battling cancer and was bald because of chemotherapy. Christina too had battled and defeated cancer and lost her hair just as the girl in the picture. It was a powerful encounter not just for her but for us in the room. So we made this portrait to honor them both, to honor Mary Ellen Marks legacy and influence on my work. How do we interpret the works and create a connection to the person in the photo, their story, their gaze? We are all humans on this little rock around the sun standing in front of a glass lens then a part of ourselves is left until developed and hung on a wall for others to see years away. How then does someone feel or respond to that image of yourself or myself? Do they see what we see or is it different because time went along and things changed except what’s in the photograph. When you see a portrait today, then 10 years later. Is it still the same picture? Are you still the same person? Maybe, just maybe, every moment you have with an artwork is precious. Because the next time you will feel differently, based on the food you ate, the company you are with, the state of mind you are in or the world is. The beauty of art is the encounter, and the re-encounter will never be the same. The photograph keeps time frozen, while everything around it changes constantly. Even in death, the photographs live on. What kind of pictures do you want to make and hang on the wall? For me, its pictures of people. Because we are all so alike, yet so different. We all are alive, and we die. Being human is beautiful and painful. The art is what connects us across the world and generations past and future. We are all human, we are all the same type of animal. It’s funny what some light, glass, and chemistry can do to our self-awareness and understanding of time itself. The invention that changed the world. Like a mirror, yet the silver nitrate is fixed forever. It does not disappear like our reflections do when we walk away from the surface. Roland Barthes said when you photography something it dies, though I believe that when you photograph something that is actually the moment it takes on a new life.

artworks.label: No. 213  —  November 6, 2023
artworks.title: Drums in the Darkness
artworks.diary: To fill yourself with light you must beat the drums in the darkness. Break open the fears by embracing the shadows of yourself. Empty the void of sorrows to grow without them. Unattached and unscathed by pain. Release what does not serve you and let in what does. Give back what does not belong to you and call in what aligns, now. A ritual of healing, a ceremony to come back to self. Sometimes we stray along the path, just to be grateful with what you have and get back on track. Here, in this moment, you have everything you need. You have enough, and you are enough. We are worthy of our greatest aspirations. Let them come. Let yourself receive the grace of god. The light is within. The love is inside. Nothing external can validate your existence. You must do that for yourself. Like the Buddha, we must all walk the path to enlightenment on our own. We will get there, in our own funny little way. Nirvana awaits, yet not a place. But a feeling of peace. Inner peace to create the peace in the world around us. The journey to love, is loving ourselves first.

artworks.label: No. 214  —  November 7, 2023
artworks.title: Family Is Forever
artworks.diary: Family is forever. We grow up and old together. Our parents give us a home, and when we become parents we give our parents hope. For the future, for the namesake. Brother and sister made from the same blood. How far do we go from home? Do we go, or do we stay. Sooner or later we end up back where we came. Father gave us everything we need, and mother gave us the life we have. A happy family is to love each other unconditionally, communicate honestly, and accept our differences no matter how triggered we become. Family is trust. It is the blood we share that makes us connected. Who else can you rely on when these are the people you came from, the first people you got to know. We did not choose our family as we choose our friends. The ultimate lesson is to acknowledge them. They do their best with what they have, sometimes they do not know any better, and that is okay. Our traumas often occur within the family tree, and that is also where all our healings begin. To become a better person is to forge a deeper bond with the family tree, digging deeper into the roots to cultivate the fruits of friendship instead of parental control. Love goes both ways, not because you have to, but because you want to. At the end of the day, all you have left is the family you met when you were born. Until the day you meet someone and create your own, they will always be with you in this life and the ever after. As our ancestors came before us, what we contribute to the world and what we leave behind. A loving family, cherished memories, and stories to carry with you into the end of time.

artworks.label: No. 215  —  November 8, 2023
artworks.title: A French Surrealist Dream
artworks.diary: Lovers in Paris. My dear friend Ian and his beloved Hedvig dancing in their dining room. Ian puts on a smooth sounding vinyl from his outstanding collection of gems he has been collecting over the years. The man knows how to set the tune and the mood for his woman and his guests. He is a legend in the music industry and leaving his legacy in the crypto business. From Beats to Ledger he is hardlined in the hardware. So much love and care for his companies and his friends. Even when we first met he always treated me like a brother. Sharing his home, a sacred creative space. Lending a room when there is no where else to go, or rather, where you would want to be. A second home, cozy, because you are welcomed in like family. Ian makes you feel like part of the tribe. Knows how to uplift his friends and family. I have learned a lot from this gentle man. How to be kind and gracious. Good karma comes from good action and vibrations. I am grateful to be his friend, to create art with him in his home. A little gesture to leave a gift of love between he and Hedvig. Something I hope they cherish and remember. How much fun we all have together. Being ourselves and for them, being in love. This moment lasts forever, their hugging and kissing into infinity in the city of love itself like a French surrealist dream.

artworks.label: No. 216  —  November 9, 2023
artworks.title: Major Arcana
artworks.diary: A year before this video was created I dreamed to exhibit my photography at Paris Photo. It was my first time visiting Paris for this acclaimed photo fair, where all the historical legends and contemporary icons showed and sold their work through prominent and emerging galleries. I walked down the halls in awe of all the artists I had studied and am now learning about. Manifesting, saying to myself. This time next year, I will exhibit my photography, my tarot scrolls! A few months later a wonderful French woman approached me at NFT Paris. Her name was Marlene. She had asked if I would like to work together and show my work at Paris photo in 2023. I was ecstatic. Could this be the wish I had asked for? She had so much faith and trust in my work. I mentioned the tarot scrolls and she was more than thrilled to show this work with La Collection. My final stop in Europe for this solo Eurotrip was in Paris. To celebrate the opening of the fair, and the exhibition of my work. Originally, we wanted to showcase all 78 tarot scrolls. Marlene made the curatorial decision to include other outstanding artists in the booth, like Operator. Therefore, we decided to only show the 22 Major Arcana pieces from the series. The booth was located at the entrance of the book fair, where everyone would be walking by. It was the perfect placement. Apparently, the French minister of culture took a fancy to our booth.
