Out of the hundreds of works exhibited, she showed up for us. During our show I sat with the artwork and the passersby to read Polaroid tarot cards to museum heads and intrigued fair-goers. I am an artist that stands by his work when it is shown. To meet the people and patrons who take the time to understand what the work is about. After all, the artist is the best person to speak with about the art! It was the final day of the fair and Marlene had caught a cold from working so hard this week. I made her portrait in front of the art, as we did once before in Berlin with Anika. To intertwine the artists past work within the new work was sort of like an easter egg for me. To tell a bit of my story diaristically and what was happening in my professional life within the travels around the world meeting and connecting with people. The inner and outer worlds come together. Since the tarot scrolls were silkscreened on Egyptian papyrus paper I gave Marlene my clear crystal quartz Ankh that I picked up in Ireland from the king himself. Held it to her heart and breathed deeply the power of creation. A symbol of unity of man and woman; Of life beginning. The journey ahead. For the next time you see this sacred tool will be in Egypt and it’s ancient hieroglyphs on the stone temple walls.

artworks.label: No. 217  —  November 10, 2023
artworks.title: Tourists in Their Home City
artworks.diary: Every time I visit Paris I see my pal Jean-Michel. For his portrait we met outside of Paris Photo in front of the Eiffel Tower. To me he represents this city so I wanted to be a tourist in the park and showcase him with the architectural symbol of the city. At night it twinkles, and I remember the first time I saw that sparkle. Paris is a bit like New York, it feels like home. A feminine city, a romantic place to sit in the parks with baguettes to feed the crows or walk alongside the Cien at night with the tungsten street glow. Jean was with his daughter Constance. I thought it would be a special gift to make a portrait of them together to remember this day, this time they have together while she is growing up. A father and his beloved daughter. Tourists in their home city with me. Have you ever been a tourist in yours? To see a place with fresh eyes, for the first time. As if you have not walked through it a thousand times. It is a simple state of mind. In the video he asked to make a portrait of me, so we turned the camera on each other and I show up for a millisecond with a faint smile. Jean and I always see art together whatever city we are in. He held space during a tough time for me last summer as we went through the life of Van Gogh in all the places he made his paintings. It was a semi-artist retreat. It felt like a walk through history, repeating it, only this time with a camera instead of a brush. A house filled with artists. Building friendships. A week of deep connection and fun, and a bit of healing. I love my friend Jean-Michel, who believes in me and my art. The kind man in the blue cap at grail capital.

artworks.label: No. 218  —  November 11, 2023
artworks.title: Love Carried Forward
artworks.diary: It was the last day in Europe for the entire project. After all the 27 EU countries on a solo road trip I made it! The final destination was Paris. To exhibit artwork and rest in the city I consider my second home for the long journey ahead in Asia and Australia. Martina asked to meet me at a cafe she used to work at while she was studying at the university. It was been a long time since she revisited her old stomping grounds. Now, older, she is a very successful businesswoman in the arts sector. We waited outside the cafe with her Italian friend until they opened. The staff noticed it was Martina so they let us in early as they were setting up. They offered us drinks and cappuccinos. She was reminiscing on her time her when she was young and broke. A humbling time for her that brought back fond memories. The woman behind the counter was none other than Fatouma! They had a sisterly bond and she was still working here since Martinas days. It brought her right back down memory lane and they hugged for a very long time, and even shed a few tears. It was beautiful to be in their presence, and an honor to make their portrait together. We did not intend to make this together, but it was what the moment revealed to us. Sometimes you cannot plan authenticity and just have to go with the flow. Sometimes that is the medicine we need, and to remember where we came from to be grateful for what we have now, and ready for whatever is to come. It was 11/11 at 11:11 when we made this portrait. Spiritually and numerically charged with divine alignment, and as you can see an extraordinary connection between friends, co-workers, and sisters who love one another. No matter how much time has passed or distance is traveled. The love always remains, and it is how we touch people’s hearts and lives is how we are remembered. So when we see each other again, it doesn’t feel like years or decades that pass, but days and minutes where we had left off our last conversation. Have you ever had a friend like that? You can go a very long time without talking to them, and when you do it is as if nothing has changed. That’s love carried forward and respect buried deep.

artworks.label: No. 219  —  November 12, 2023
artworks.title: Happy Diwali
artworks.diary: Traveling on a very long flight from Paris to Kathmandu there was a layover in Delhi. All of the staff at the airport were dressed up in ceremonial outfits. I had asked the passport gate attendant why everyone was dressed in such beautiful clothes, was it some holiday? They shared that it was Diwali! I always found myself somewhere on a special holiday or sacred alignment with celestial portals opening up. Another signifier that I was on the right track making this project and I was exactly where I needed to be. They called out on a loudspeaker that there was a big delay and passengers had to wait before getting their passport stamped. I made friends with the young crew of airport staff and shared about the project I was working on. They were about to goto lunch and mentioned it would be special to create their portrait as a team on this special holiday in these colorful clothes, whereas normally they would be in uniform. They all came back smiling from lunch and welcomed me over to make their portrait in front of a mural near their desks. The security was looking at me obscurely with my pelican case and photographic gear. Honestly, it is a strange place to ask permission to make a portrait, especially at an airport where you are not allowed to film. But they let me get away with it and we made a special moment at work together. I gifted them a polaroid for them to remember this experience and holiday. They stamped my passport and allowed me through since they got to know me a bit better. The armed guard at the security checkpoint was investigating my film and was opening all the boxes, and tried to open my camera. I told him there was film in there and please not to do that. He snarled at me and gestured me past the gate. An odd place indeed to make art, yet it was the perfect time to create. For me, creating is a feeling and knowing when is right. It is the process of the journey and the kindness of the people along the ride you meet. I never thought I would make art at an airport security gate, yet here we are. The lesson is you really can make art anywhere you go, with anyone you meet. It is all about the motivation and intention, the honoring and the irony. You can plan and envision what you want, but are you receptive to what you get? As I work on a timeline with a 24 hour clock countdown. I count the moments like I do blessings that fall right in front of my face. Being open and observant. Sure sometimes there is missed opportunities, and maybe you will get a second chance if you hesitate. But there will always be another moment as life is full of them and people creating memories, Look around and you will see. The world is full of people and each person is a universe to connect with. Sometimes all it takes is reaching out, saying hello, and asking a question by leading with intention. Happy Diwali to my new friends in India!

artworks.label: No. 220  —  November 13, 2023
artworks.title: The Happiest Place on Earth
artworks.diary: How did I end up in Bhutan? It is kind of a funny story. A place I always wanted to visit as it is supposedly the happiest place on Earth with a carbon footprint that regenerates the planet! The king is ruling with Bitcoin and walks the streets amongst his people. It was said they once got rid of the “robots” aka stoplights just because it costed people their traffic controller jobs. A man for his people. A collector from my discord group suggested I come to Bhutan. I said, lets do it! and I was dead serious. This country requires an invitation by a local in order to get a visa to visit. Well my online friend hooked me up with his local friend who was also a travel guide and helped me get permission to enter the kingdom. It was a synchronistic call to come visit a special country with an orange dragon on its flag. The flight in is also precarious as you are inside a massive dome shaped mountain range, the pilots are extremely skilled. It was one big yes to a strange adventure to a Buddhist paradise of happy people. Rinzin was my guide and taught me stories and brought me to many sacred places. I made his portrait at the Punakha Dzong by the river. He told me stories about why there are so many Phalluses around the city. It represented a Lama named Drukpa Kunley. He who lived at the turn of the 16th century and who was popularly known as the “Divine Madman” Rinzin made me laugh with his sexualized jokes and shared with me Kunleys reproductive organ, is called the “Thunderbolt of Flaming Wisdom” as it unnerved demons and demonesses and he subdued them with his magic stick. It is also said that he is “perhaps the only saint in the religions of the world who is almost exclusively identified with phallus and its creative power.” I had a great time with Rinzin and his funny dick jokes. He even took me to a special temple for fertility that many women from around the world visit to help them with their pregnancy. The stories of the Divine Madman are comical, yet also teach wise lessons in a strange unconventional Buddhist way. He fought many demons and struck them down with his Thunderbolt. Rinzin and I fed the ducks off the bridge that leads inside the Dzong and we ran into his long lost uncle. It was a trip! We carried on back to town to meet my online friend, Clinton, who manifested me to arrive in Bhutan. He moved there years ago with his wife and kids to teach at an elementary school with the children. We hoped in the van and the final stop for the night was a handmade paper mill! I love paper because its such an intimate process with pulp that becomes an instrument to scribe on. They used hemp leaves and flower to create viscerally embossed papers that are unique to anything I have ever seen before. I had no idea what I would use this paper for but I ended up buying out the shop of 100 different sheets for a future project, You just can’t pass up an opportunity like this when you meet the people making the paper and the paper itself is art. The last time I was trigger happy buying paper was in Egypt a year prior when I visited a papyrus mill and was taught how they make paper out of the papyrus plant and instantly bought almost 800 sheets to send back to the US. That inevitably was used to create my Smoke and Mirrors Tarot Scrolls. And come to think of it, the paper I received in Bhutan ended up creating the Omega Arcana with artificial intelligent prints derived from Smoke and Mirrors. I love to travel the world and discover different types of paper, because each paper tells a story from where its from and transforms how it is utilized. Ultimately, to make art and tell a new story.

artworks.label: No. 221  —  November 14, 2023
artworks.title: The King’s Bodyguard
artworks.diary: Rinzin, Kaito, and I hiked up the steps to the golden Buddha of Dordenma. It is a massive sculpture sitting amongst the trees with a heavenly glow you can see from miles away. A godlike man in the lotus position sitting atop the mountain gently hovering over the trees. It is truly surreal up close and afar. Kaito was telling us stories from his time as the kings trusted bodyguard. It was like being in the presence of royalty himself. A man with a gentle heart and loves to make you laugh. Buddha was not a god, he was a man named Siddhartha. Born as a prince and left his royalty behind to experience the suffering and enlightenment that life has on both ends of the spectrum. His journey his one of self reflection and realization. Nirvana is not sitting under a tree in the lotus position till your legs go numb with a blood clot, it is a state of mind. Heaven on Earth. Disciplined focus where nothing around you. Not a serpent in the grass slithering up your legs, tantric women dancing around you with temptation, the drums and sirens of war, nothing can stop the focus. Not even death’s blade. It is all an illusion of the mind. Nirvana is the realization that you have the power to activate this peace and silence at any moment. To remember that you have the will to change your life in an instant. It is not the after life, it is living for the first time for the rest of your life! Without fear, without suffering. Breathing brings us back to the moment. When meditating you focus on the breath. It is the prana, the energy of life. When you focus on your breathing you become the most present you can be. You let go of all your thoughts just to fill your lungs. That is love, that is living in harmony. Remember to breathe, you can do it right now as you sit here reading this passage. Four seconds breathing in, four seconds breathing out. Do that four times. Welcome to your Nirvana. Welcome to your peace in the inner sanctum. Sometimes we forget as we go about this thing called life. Just remember to breathe to come right back to yourself. This is the way of the Buddha, and no one can teach you, except the lessons you learn on the path you walk by yourself.

artworks.label: No. 222  —  November 15, 2023
artworks.title: Art Is the Bridge
artworks.diary: When two strangers come together what is the friction between us? The first impression, the first meeting point. How does the ice truly break so we can connect. Imagine if humans were like ants and communicated through our antennas and sync into harmony. What keeps us apart, why does it take time to earn trust and become friends over similar interests and going on adventures? Art creates the sympathy to forge an even playing field of interpretation and discussion. When creating it, we are equal, and when looking at it we have our own subjective ideas. To communicate those ideas is to share wisdom, perhaps that is how we can truly connect. By sharing our perspective with one another. Not to argue or to say who is right or wrong, but to learn something new. Life is about learning and growing. In the age of AI we are evolving at a rapid rate due to the information we are exposed and processing: like an organic computer we filter data as stimuli. What makes us so different you and I. What makes us even different from the machines we are building to mimic human behavior and work? To create a consciousness outside of the one we harness within. Externalizing our pain, our problems to another. When we could be looking within and appreciate those who are right in front of us. A family member, a friend, and even a stranger on the street with a smile. Learning to connect with ourselves so we can connect with the world. Art is the bridge. The unspoken truth that needs no language, just a feeling of hope or loss. A feeling we all feel that makes us human after all. Our job on this Earth is to take care of her, to take care of one another. Then, we can truly evolve into something greater, leading with our hearts and empathizing with each other. To slow down and see the world instead of speeding up to destroy it.

artworks.label: No. 223  —  November 16, 2023
artworks.title: Om Mani Padme Hum
artworks.diary: Om Mani Padme Hum

artworks.label: No. 224  —  November 17, 2023
artworks.title: Not Black or White, but Grey
artworks.diary: We circled the Buddha Stupa in the middle of Kathmandu. Ringing the bells and circling a few times with all the people who come far and wide to pray at this special place. Some bring offerings of fruits or incense, sometimes money too. As you circle the dome that watches you with those Buddha eyes, you run your hands through these spinning columns for karmic cleansing. Each spin represents an Om Mani Padme Hum. You get double the points every time you spin one, up to infinity! We come to these places to pray and heal our souls. To pray to always do the right thing. To be forgiven, to be healed, to make your dreams come true. To manifest a better life, or at least try and be grateful for the one you have now. It was a time of letting go. John and I found this barber while waiting for Ethan to arrive. I decided to go full on Eat, Pray, Love and shave my head for a new beginning. I never did it before and wanted a cold hard reset atop my head. Also to regrow lost hairs as I age the natural way. I took one last look in the mirror and closed my eyes and when I opened them it was freshly shaven. I could hardly recognize myself, for the better. Sometimes all you need is a new haircut to feel better and start fresh. As the haircut ended and the man was slapping sense into my noggin with his knuckles Ethan arrived. With him were two young boys who grew up in these parts and they hung out by the Stupa everyday to meet tourists and foreigners. They were students of the Thangka painting school in the center next to the Stupa. We were enamored by their work and picked up a few paintings. Then treated the boys to some hot chai and veggie momos in this sweet little cafe with a great view of the eyes of Buddha. After lunch I made a portrait of them and then we played some snooker at their local pool hall. They took us further into their stone homes in the alleyways to meet their family. They cooked us dinner in a small room where they all slept. John gifted the boys baby brother a skateboard and taught him how to skate. It was a touching memory that we all carry and learned that art, humility, and food can bring people together from all sorts of backgrounds. It is simply a matter of reaching out and saying hello and not being afraid to see what is behind the doors that open before you. At the very least, a lesson or realization about yourself awaits. This is the path to Buddhahood. Where all people have a gift, you will always learn something new from everyone. For better or worse, it helps you grow with experience. After all, it’s only human to experience the full spectrum then find yourself on to the middle way. Not black or white, but grey. As you sway towards love and fear, the middle path creates harmony between earthly desires and delight. Follow the path of knowing to set yourself free from worry and doubt. See with eyes of love and compassion to make the world feel round.

artworks.label: No. 225  —  November 18, 2023
artworks.title: The Sheriff
artworks.diary: It was around sunrise at Nagarkot geodetic survey tower we drank some street chai and had some breakfast with the locals before hiking to the top when the sun shined over the Himalayas behind us. Overlooking the rice fields and Kathmandu in the distance. Ice on the snowy caps of the legendary mountains in all of its peaceful and subtle glory. There was a rickety old metal tower that people were climbing. My friend John climbed up first and waved us up. I followed him and it was a tight squeeze as people were eager to see higher into the distance from this birds eye view of this rusty mechanical structure. A man in a cowboy hat came up to me and we started talking. He called himself the Sheriff. He asked me to take a picture of him and his new friend from Chicago. I thought they were a couple and complimented them being cute together and she laughed and said her boyfriend was under us watching the sunrise. We all laughed and she got close and made a photo with the sheriff. I asked the Sheriff if he would like to be in my art project. He nodded and did not say a word as I made his portrait as the golden dawn sunlight landed on his face. We climbed down and he followed us for some more chai. We treated him to a cup of course. Then he got into this long monologue of being a warrior of some sort. A karate master. I think he was trying to intimidate me but I was looking him in the eye just listening to what he said, then went into another tangent about the movie he was starring in and directing. He was happy we made photos of him on his camera. I’ll never forget meeting the sheriff at the top of the mountain, but there was no deputy. They guys and I chugged along a 10 mile hike around the rice fields and were chased down by children asking us for money, i’m not sure what they would do with it but they saw us as piggy banks. We smelled some side of the road hemp growing and our noses perked up. Ethan busted out the golden hash ball that Vansh gave us the day before and enjoyed some of the best hashish in the world. It is so good that you can roll a joint with it without any flower. Thankfully the sheriff was not on our tail anymore and we gleefully walked around until we made it back to the town. I remember losing a lapis lazuli ring I picked up a few days prior on this journey, but thankfully we did not lose our heads! When we got back to town we went to a few temples in the old town and sipped some more chai until the evening ceremonies. Monkeys took the streets and we were escorted by a random monk being foreigners to sit front and center to the water ceremony they had hosted. The fire dances were psychedelic and mesmerizing. The crowd cheered and prayed. It was indeed a special day from sunrise to sunset. Amen and Namaste.

artworks.label: No. 226  —  November 19, 2023
artworks.title: Happy Birthday!
artworks.diary: Maya was the shopkeeper under our apartment in the Stupa circle. She had warned us about local scammers trying to take advantage of foreigners like ourselves. She was a good one and it was her birthday! We bought some Ganesha and Hanuman gifts from her shop to celebrate and support her business. We sang her happy birthday and gifted her a Polaroid with her husband who runs the store with her. John, Ethan, Eli, and I packed our bags and set out for India. Eli had forgot to get his visa so he had to stay behind once we got to the airport for a couple days. John, Ethan, and I trekked onward to Bodhgaya to meet the children Ethan had worked with ten years prior and meditate under the Bodhi tree.

artworks.label: No. 227  —  November 20, 2023
artworks.title: Bodhisattva
artworks.diary: We arrived in Bodh Gayā. Which is a religious site and place of pilgrimage associated with the Mahabodhi Temple complex, situated in the Gaya district in the Indian state of Bihar. It is famous for being the place where Gautama Buddha is said to have attained enlightenment (bodhi) under what became known as the Bodhi Tree. Bodh Gayā has remained the object of pilgrimage and veneration for Buddhists. Ethan’s friend Dhirendra who runs an orphanage brought us around the city. After feeding us potato fritters he took us in a broken down ambulance to meet with a lama that is close to the dali. We set with him for an hour as he just started spitting wisdom the moment we arrived. We absorbed his teachings with open ears and open hearts. As he stood before us there was a painting with an enlightened Buddha behind him. I framed the shot as if he were an Buddhist angel, like a Bodhisattva, Imparting his philosophy to us. After having a serving of tea and a polaroid portrait. He vanished back to his quarters. Dhirendra walked us through the Gaya complex to meditate under the Bodhi tree. He somehow got us into the temple as the main ceremony began. We sat there beside all the monks praying, and ironically, some counting money to give offerings to their colleagues, It was funny and sort of strange to watch spirit meet commerce inside the temple setting. We stepped outside and sat under the tree where Buddha sat. Closed our eyes and saw all the lights. Voices and sounds of the people and the prayers they carried. Until a bald man with a three Bodhi leaves appeared right in front of us once we opened our eyes. He held them out, as if for us to take a leaf, and we each did. The man nodded and smiled and walked back into the circular motion the crowd was moving around the Temple. We were in the right place at the right time. Calm amongst the chaos in the complex… like all is one with the universe.

artworks.label: No. 228  —  November 21, 2023
artworks.title: The Youngest and Smallest to the Eldest and Tallest
artworks.diary: Dhirendra picked us up in a broken down ambulance to Dungeshwari Cave Temples. Where Buddha was meditating in the caves for nearly 6 years without eating and moving from his lotus position. He became emaciated and forgot to take care of his body as he had been developing his mind and third eye. At some point he came to a realization of the middle way. Not extreme gluttony or malnourishment. To create a balance, this is where you will find enlightenment. To take care of oneself. He left the cave and walked away with this wisdom. We trekked up the mountain to see where he had sat. To meditate there ourselves for a few moments. There was a bronze cast of what he had looked like, sitting in the lotus position. There were people praying and tourists making pictures. We sat in silence, observing. We came down the mountain and were met with hungry monkeys and begging children. Dhirendra gave the monkeys cookies, and the children water. We all sat together with a monk before entering the cave at the top to pray and be in silence. To pay our respects to the elders and the history of our hero. Buddha is just a man, not a God. It gave us hope on what we can become, as we are just men. Simply human. We got back into the ambulance and drove on over to the school that Dhirendra manages. Hundreds of children. They greeted us with flowers and open arms. Had a dance competition that Ethan joined with them too. I taught the kids how to make Polaroids to the point where they went nuts and started ripping the pictures and camera away from me and the teachers had to step in. Then Ethan, John, and I served all the children Dal. Starting with the youngest and smallest to the eldest and tallest. There was plenty of food for all the children, even to have seconds and thirds. It was a big lesson for me. I found my joy serving food to others. Food is gratitude. It is nourishment. It is what the Buddha had forgotten on his path. Not all earthly pleasures are poison. Food is a gift. Food is life. Food gives energy to continue the practice to reach higher states of consciousness. To serve food to others is the best medicine for the soul. Enrichment and humility. It opens the heart to more love in the world.

artworks.label: No. 229  —  November 22, 2023
artworks.title: Him and His Rickshaw
artworks.diary: We had driven from the sacred city of Bodh Gaya to the ancient city of Varanasi. Driving on the highway in India is different from anywhere else I had ever visited, though Cairo was close. In India the people speak with their beeps. To say hello, to pass by, to communicate a message to other drivers or riders. There were even some instances where on a separated two lane highway, cars would still be coming in your direction on your side going to opposite way! It was pure chaos, yet a divine order to the rules of the road here. There were none. Everyone is hyper aware, and people are coming from all directions and buses and trucks filled with people where they started pouring onto the roofs! Our driver made it safely to Varanasi. Found a random street corner in the Middle Eastern neighborhoods and dropped us off there. We were far away from where we needed to be dropped off. We walked for awhile until we realized we could flag down a rickshaw. There we met Dhiraj. He saved us from bring lost and brought us home to the hotel that used to be and old palace quarters right off the docks of Ganges river. He was a kind and gentle man and was thrilled to meet us Americans. We told him about the project and once we got out of the car I made a portrait of him and his Rickshaw. Thank you, Dhiraj. Inside the hotel we regrouped with Eli, Ethans brother again.

artworks.label: No. 230  —  November 23, 2023
artworks.title: In This Life, and the Next
artworks.diary: Our group woke up early for a sunrise boat ride to drift along the Ganges. There was a smokey orange glow in the ashey sky. You can look directly at the sun without getting blinded or burned. A faint red dot lingered over the grey and green water. People bathing with the blessings from the ancient river. Some cleaning, others pilgrammed, mostly praying. Cremations happening 24/7 along the piers. You can see the fires burning from each dock at the burning gahts. There was a peaceful silence in the air, the only noise was the water as we gently rowed down the stream. The light of the sky brightened to a hazy white and the day broke. We got off the waters and headed into the city. Visiting Hanuman temples on rickshaws. Then meeting tailors and other vendors in the narrow corridors. We learned how to sing from a master who sung with The Beatles. Raising octaves from our sacral chakra up to the throat. It was not just singing, it was calibration where the soul meet the voice. We followed the path down the alley and at the corner of the evening we found what we were looking for. A delicious bhaang lassi at the famous Baba Lassi. What makes Babas so special? A special plant protein. A half ounce ball of dark green almost a darkened amber color of hashish. Somehow he had mixed this much material to match the milk dessert drink taste. Without realizing you are getting extremely high, because it tastes so damn good. Like melted ice cream with fresh pomegranates topping the terra citta bowl of heaven. It sure takes you to heaven… until you realize you are in hell. It stated with laughing with our friends and Baba before he closed. We walked the wrong way to the Ghats and met with kids who were skateboarding. My friend John is a pro skater and saw an unconventional gap between the stairs and borrowed the kids board. He gave it a try and we were walking with a saint and a sadu as they walked us through the night ghats safely, which felt like being protected by spirits. The saint said to stop skating. John continued to skate and almost landed his trick. The boy wanted to impress his friends and took the board to try too. He instantly hurt his ankle and carried him off to a bench. They stopped skating and he was hurt. His friends cared to him and the saint lead us on. We arrived at the gates of the burning Ghats stoned out of our minds. Past midnight, peak lassi. There were people carrying bodies and placing them on the fire. They chanted, Ram Ram, Ram Ram, Ram Ram, in harmony. Honoring the dead, remembering their family, and completing the final wish to release them in the Ganges. We were surrounded by death and fire. Only a few men were still working. The police almost stopped us entering this area this late but the saints nodded to him. We were in good company. They were teaching us foreigners something valuable; Teaching us how to respect. I was freaking out, like a bad acid trip on repeat. Paranoia booming in my brain and nerves. This place felt demonic for a second. It’s a different energy from the day to it is night. It felt like we were going to be stabbed, killed, burned and sacrificed. I watched the people working. For some reason I felt safety when I was standing next to the saint who led us here. A divine protection of some sort. The anxiety left my body and started feeling confident. Starting to feel unafraid. The fear of death had left and started to reveal itself deeper. It’s about family and grieving those we love. Believing in something that will free them of their suffering. In this life, and the next.

artworks.label: No. 231  —  November 24, 2023
artworks.title: A String and a Brass Hoop
artworks.diary: The Sadu was showing us his magic tricks with a string and a brass hoop in the middle of the ghat drawing an audience then busted out a box of Rudrakshas. He handed each of us a different Mukhi with different faces. He gave me the double, which looked like the shape of a walnut but it was a sacred prayer ornamental bead meant for meditation. After his performance, He walked us to the saints home and he welcomed us in to the doorless temple. It was an empty space crawling with fuzzy centipedes and swarms of ants covered on the tiles under a large metal caged room. Inside was a statue with a million eyes in the shape of a ganesha. It was terrifying yet a holy idol at the same time. He had us sit in the cage and meditate with the sculpture. He sat in silence and watched. The guys closed their eyes and started to hum. It was hard for me to calm and meditate because it felt like at any moment he would shut the gate on us and lock us in. This paranoia flared up. Red flags and bells whistling. I could not meditate or sit still. Bugs crawling up my arm and around us. It felt a bit like trying to meditate in hell. My third and two eyes open and could not take anymore so excused myself out. I waited outside till the guys were done. How to trust the universe and keep a calm mind while in the dangers of the unknown in a strange place? The men lead us on to the ghats and the saint was preparing his home for his next students. Eli had a place in mind that we go enjoy a meal thinking of our families for thanksgiving since we were together in India as brothers, as family.

artworks.label: No. 232  —  November 25, 2023
artworks.title: Ram Ram
artworks.diary: Ram Ram.

artworks.label: No. 233  —  November 26, 2023
artworks.title: Blessings
artworks.diary: After 6 hours on a bumpy mountain road from the airport to Nainital. We stopped for some hashish since we were close to where the hash in India is grown. Our friend John was losing his patience in the back seat getting smushed around by the luggage. At nightfall we made it to our lodge that was off the beaten path and our driver helped us off in the middle of the road. Our host found us and walked us on a hike to the house. We crossed a broken path and jump wired fence with our luggage to make it to our rooms. The guys were bbqing and playing music and all we wanted to do was rest before going to Kainchi Dham for Neem Karoli Baba blessing. He was a Hindu guru and a devotee of the Hindu deity Hanuman.. The same teacher of Steve jobs and Ram Das. We too sought out the wisdom of the importance of living in the present moment and transformative impact of kindness and compassion. Our host Paras served us Dal and Roti and off we went to bed. He said he would join us and take us to the Ashram in the morning to pray. We arrived to the temple and stood in line. Surrounded by all the locals we were the only westerners for kilometers. Observing the people in their prayers, receiving blessings from gurus and statues we participated in the rituals. There was a moment where we all sat down on the steps to meditate and close our eyes. Sitting in the sun. Illuminated… Becoming enlightened in such a sacred space for so many people around the world. Everything inside my eyes turned to a supersonic gold vibration from a source of white light. A vortex of energy was rushing up inside me like a kundalini awakening. To the point where my whole world was spinning. An overwhelming force as if you can feel the axis spin of the Earth. It was an intense 30 minutes of purifying the mind and body till everything became crystal clear. Third eye wide opened. We left the temple and stopped meditating at the same moment. Got in line to leave, and as you walk out the temple gates they give you a single chickpea as an offering. You eat it and it is the most delicious single garbanzo bean you’ll ever taste. The taste of heaven being fed by the angels themselves. To teach us compassion. To feed people who are hungry. To answer their prayers when they need help or guidance.

artworks.label: No. 234  —  November 27, 2023
artworks.title: Big Beautiful Family
artworks.diary: It was our first evening in Rishikesh. At sundown every day they host an Arti on the docks of the Ganges river. Where the entire community and Ashram gather with their families and with fire to pray together. Its quite a beautiful and connective ritual. You all share the same experience and it becomes an event that everyone is included in the transcendental meditation of singing as one big family from all walks of life. When you keep coming back every night, its not just a novelty. It is a way of life, a way to deepen connections with oneself, the spirit, and the people all around you. Everything becomes more familiar. The fire dances as the songs blend together. We me this big beautiful family in the Ashram who welcomed us to goto their cousins wedding in Rajasthan. Kindness is all around you, you just have to open your eyes to see them, and be open to the hearts of others inviting you in. Then all of your prayers will be answered.

artworks.label: No. 235  —  November 28, 2023
artworks.title: The Sacred Women of the Sacred River
artworks.diary: From Hollywood to the Himalayas. Eli’s friend who leads the Parmarth Niketan Ashram, Sadhvi Bhagawati Saraswati, welcomed us in to the spiritual campus and provided warm meals with a place to sleep every evening as long as we wished to stay. Daily Satsongs and Nightly Arti’s we were looped into the rituals here. Rishikesh had its hooks on us. Even when we tried to leave or wanted to continue. Something held us back, the city wanted us to stay. We prayed by the water and learned yoga by a street teacher on the rooftops by Mother Ganga at sunrise. I felt like the karate kid learning how to defend the sacred temple, the body itself. For the fire ceremonies in the morning you walk past more than 20 deities. Some Hindu spirits I never seen but connected with. The gemini twins of shiva. Blue angels together. We met Sadhvi with her daughter Shivani and devotee Pooja by where she hosts the daily Arti’s beside the Shiva statue. The sacred women of the sacred river chanting love to Mother Ganga. Rishikesh; A city of divine feminine energy as the body moves like the fluidity of the river flowing. Namaste.

artworks.label: No. 236  —  November 29, 2023
artworks.title: Releasing Guilt, Releasing Grief
artworks.diary: Ethan, Eli and I visited the location where Ethan had a near death experience in the rapids of the Ganges. His raft flipped and a couple of riders he was with fell out of the boat when they went over a waterfall. Ethan was pulled under by the currents. Descended to the cold dark and silent depths. Accepting his fate quietly, Accepting his death as apparitions of his families faces swung around him. Saying goodbye to each of his loved ones. A light touched him and he let go. Miraculously broke the tide and floated to the surface as he let out his last breath. An arm from above the waters, which looked like an angels arm stretching from heaven grabbed hold of him and lifted him out of the waters. It was his friend who saved his life. Unfortunately there was one soul who lost their life on this day, his name was Nico. Ethan carried his photo of him to honor him and heal this wound that he has been carried for over a decade. Dunking in the water to face his fear, to take his power back from the water that almost took him away, to heal with his brother and create stronger bonds as Eli extends his hand in safety like an anchor in the sand. To pray to the portrait of Nico and remember his smile. The water cleansed our souls, purged our fears, and let go of all the weight we carry. Releasing guilt, releasing grief, releasing parts of our old selves that do not serve us anymore. After the baptism we sat on the rocks to meditate and glaze at the sun while it sparkles across the surface of the calm ripples carrying us away. God bless you Nico.

artworks.label: No. 237  —  November 30, 2023
artworks.title: Om Namah Shivaya
artworks.diary: Om Namah Shivaya

artworks.label: No. 238  —  December 1, 2023
artworks.title: The Woman of the Water, the Man of the Rock
artworks.diary: Lily was waiting for me at the cafe. She was in Rishikesh mastering yoga learning new forms. We decided to take a walk to the water as she brought a special white scarf as a prop to pray in the water with. We found a crowded small beach and was about to begin the shoot until a holy man dressed in orange came right up to us from the bushes. It seemed like he appeared out of nowhere like a ghost and asked if he could guide us to a better place on the beach to make the portrait. He gestured to follow him and we did. We walked through a small forest and climbed over massive rocks. We found ourselves arriving on a quiet patch of land grey with rocks and sands; the water gently flowing in this pocket. This was the spot, and he was right. I asked if he also would like to be in the video, as our spirit guide. From the time we met to where we sat he was sharing us wisdom and anecdotes. About the present moment, about prayer, about meditation. All you have to do is ask the right question. He sat atop the boulders in the lotus position. Divine masculine holding space for the divine feminine to express. Lily changed out of her clothes and stepped into the water with her handmade silk white robe scarf. Action! She began to stretch and release into the sky. Twisting her bodily form as she would in yoga. Using her body as a totem for liberation and connection to the gods in the heavens; Like Artemis reaching her arms and bow out to the mountains of Olympus. Man and woman channeling the energy of nature. Fluidity and grounding. The woman of the water, the man of the rock. The two pray in different ways, yet its the same.

artworks.label: No. 239  —  December 2, 2023
artworks.title: The Fire Keeper
artworks.diary: Ashutosh was the fire keeper of the Hanuman temple at the Ashram we were staying at. Every morning he would light the fire and pray, and every night he would ring the bell before arti and close the temple. He had a huge following on instagram and tik tok just from the songs and prayers he sings for the divine monkey god with tearing apart his chest to reveal Ram and Sita in his Heart. This deity can move mountains as gifts to other divine lords. There was a very large statue outside of the temple that embodies the story and strength of this visceral description. A giant red heart emerging from a giant monkeys body. All is love, all is one. We sat for one last prayer, a Hanuman Chalisa, before we packed our bags and rode off to Agra from the Ashram. We were supposed to fly to Goa that day but the energy did not feel right and we set off to see the marble temple of love, the great structure of the Taj Mahal. We broke loose from Rishikesh hold and tore out of town with a trusted driver and felt the tug of the city’s gravitational force with a great escape velocity. It was time to continue on as much as we would have loved to stay and were welcomed to, we had more work to do!

artworks.label: No. 240  —  December 3, 2023
artworks.title: Love That Builds Buildings
artworks.diary: The temple of love, the great Taj Mahal. We arrived to the palace after an 8 hour car ride to see one of the great wonders of the world. In the name of love from a king to his wife he built this ornate sanctuary to display his affection. It was said, the king was preparing to build another palace exactly the same but in black right across the river. The king’s son locked him away to protect his family’s wealth as this would have made them go bankrupt. Little did the little prince know this would become a global landmark, A UNESCO site where millions of visitors come marvel at the scale of the magnificent landscape and near perfection in the engineering of the alignment with the quartzite building mounted with semi-precious stones along the walkways. At the entrance to the majestic view of the pool stood two couples. It was the perfect moment for a picture to represent the love that carried over from monarchs to modern day lovers. Each man laid a kiss on the head of his beloved. There hearts were full of joy and laughter. The way love moves through you, the way love should make you feel. Like the butterflies that never die and lift you to new heights when you are together. Love that is eternal, the type of love that builds buildings and lasts a century for other lovers to fall in love on its doorstep.

artworks.label: No. 241  —  December 4, 2023
artworks.title: The New Chef
artworks.diary: Aekakshara was the new chef, straight out of university, at a hotel near the Taj Mahal we had visited. Ethan gifted her a large pink flower from the lobby vase and we asked the manager if she can step outside with us to make her portrait. During her lunch break she joined us outside on the steps by the pool in the rain. I made her portrait then we went back inside to enjoy a breakfast with her and the staff. We went back outside in the rain and wandered around the venue chasing the sounds of brilliant blue and green birds squawking. A thousand eyes of the peacock’s tail greeted us in the small wooded area of the hotel. It walked us into a bush where we snuck a toke then returned to our rooms to enjoy the sounds hitting the terracotta ceilings like drums making music on the windowsill. We rested before preparing our next impromptu road trip to Jaipur, the colorful and rich city, with castles made of pink sands.

artworks.label: No. 242  —  December 5, 2023
artworks.title: Keeper of the Monkey Village
artworks.diary: We met Hanuman at his temple in Jaipur. A city of monkeys feasting on bananas scattered across the sacred ape landscape. A man named Kanhaiya Sharma was the keeper of the monkey village. He knew how to communicate with them; He feeds them, he plays with them, he cares for them. Kanhaiya said they made a documentary on him and how he connects with the monkey kingdom and how they call this place their home. At the top of the hill are two temples. We prayed and were banded with an orange bracelet tied by the monks. He dotted our heads with red pigment and we sat inside by the statues to meditate in silence till the sky turned as pink as the city walls.

artworks.label: No. 243  —  December 6, 2023
artworks.title: Jain Temple
artworks.diary: Sreenivasulu showed us around the Jain temple an hour right outside the Bangalore airport on the way to Sunils familys village in the north. We wandered the temples from left to right. Each pillar had a different deity in Jainism. I clearly remember a black ganesha somewhere in between the 100 gods we met in stone and bronze. We climbed up a dilapidated building across from the temple entrance. The staircase was still intact so we wen to the top floor. We had to be very careful because there were massive sinkholes from the building destructive state and was easy to fall in. Sreenivasulu posed atop the pillar in front of Jain before we rode off for 6 hours more to the family compound in Madanapali.

artworks.label: No. 244  —  December 7, 2023
artworks.title: Jai Ganesha!
artworks.diary: Jai Ganesha! Praise to the elephant-headed remover of obstacles and patron of wisdom.

artworks.label: No. 245  —  December 8, 2023
artworks.title: Beloved
artworks.diary: A mother and her beloved son at the Veerabhadra Temple.

artworks.label: No. 246  —  December 9, 2023
artworks.title: Prayed with the Holy Mountain
artworks.diary: Adinarayana in front of the sacred mountain in Tamil Nadu, Arunachala. We visited the Annamalaiyar Temple, A Hindu temple dedicated to Shiva and Parvati, located at the foothills of the Arunachala. The entrance was packed of people trying to pray and make worship to their guardian angels. Adinarayana grabbed our hands and pulled us past the metal gate. We quickly scurried through the labyrinth inside that constantly guides you through the walkways. A never ending circuit of meeting gods and gifting flowers. Hindu priests pressing their fingers on your forehead of pigments; oranges, yellows, pinks, and reds dots to mark the third eye blessings. We waited, we sweated, we prayed, and we gave sacrament to the temple. It felt like being inside the heart of the pyramids of giza. How were these temples made of stone? Who built them!? We walked to another ashram for Sri Ramana. It was said that the Arunachala mountain was his guru. Therefore his ashram sits at the foothills. When you visit this place it’s important you walk counterclockwise around the entire mountain to pay respect. In our case, we drove the car around a couple of times around the mountain. We stopped at a pull off that took us into a smaller village. Adinarayana parked the car and we found a building that was under construction. We walked up the hollow stairs in the cement hallway with metal bars sticking out and made our way to the roof. This was the place, and we did not have much time as the neighbors were looking at us from below and the workers inside were wondering who we were but shrugged it off and continued working. Adinarayana put his hands together and prayed with the holy mountain. A bird flies by and symbolizes spiritual freedom and transformation. It’s time to take flight!

artworks.label: No. 247  —  December 10, 2023
artworks.title: The Orange Grove
artworks.diary: How do people become family? Those who are with you since as long as you can remember. Who always show up and serve with a smile on their face. Family is a feeling. A knowing; Some sort of belonging together. We are born with our biological family, but choose the family we spend all our time with. Even if its for hire. They become not only a part of our extended family, but a part of ourselves. These two lovers known each other for their whole lives and have been together ever since. Soulmates. They live and work at Sunil’s family compound. The people who are caretakers for the people and the land of this home to the point where the become a part of what home is. It was a blessing to meet Ananda & Parvati in the orange grove, to touch and taste their south Indian recipes. We sat with them and Sunil with his mother and shared so much love of what a family feels like. When you eat together, you bond. When you eat great home cooked food together made with love, you are in bliss! They are the miracle workers. The invisible force that combs through the home and make sure the gears are turning even when you are not knowing. Mindful of their help and their presence. Always grateful for the help we receive and reciprocate. Family is a loving presence, an acknowledgement of those who spend their time with you. At the end of the day, family is all we have.

artworks.label: No. 248  —  December 11, 2023
artworks.title: Resting in Paradise
artworks.diary: A son and with his beloved father, NagaRathnamma, resting in paradise.

artworks.label: No. 249  —  December 12, 2023
artworks.title: She Held a Fire
artworks.diary: On the final day in Madanapalli we visited Sunils guru at the local temple. They have all the Hindu gods around the religious compound. In one of the bunkers was a giant Hanuman carved out of stone laying on the ground for the finishing touches before it gets installed and becomes the largest Hanuman idol in the country! There was a dome like chamber on the other end of the property. You go inside and see a massive shiva lingam in the center of the room wrapped with healing crystals. On the walls around the 360 degree room are different phases of a human-like Shiva character and twelve of his different forms. From nude to blue. We sat on the ground and started chanting Aum. It echoed through the halls and through our hearts. The sonic healing acoustic sound vibrated across the room. I recorded an hour of it as it felt like a sound healing chamber. Activating the blue throat chakra. After an hour we went outside and met the gurus volunteer, Chandra Durga. She held a fire in front of the Hindu Goddess Durga for her daily prayers.

artworks.label: No. 250  —  December 13, 2023
artworks.title: Wood, Brass, Copper, and Stone
artworks.diary: The blessings and teachings of all the Hindu Gods and Goddesses in one shop in the far corners of a strip mall in Bangalore. Following the flow of divination to illumination. Wood, brass, copper, and stone idols waiting for you to choose who will to protect your home and guide your spirit? I chose a copper Vishnu. God of preservation; Restorer of Dharma and the protector of good bestower of Karma.

artworks.label: No. 251  —  December 14, 2023
artworks.title: Phoenix Tears
artworks.diary: Gumpoong invited me to her parents home in Chang Mai to meet her mom and dad to drink some red Thai tea and have a very spicy meal. It was a family affair! For their family portrait I asked Gumpoong to take a photo of her parents as a way to honor her art as a photographer. To integrate creativity with the meaning of being together as a family, and that energy that brings us all together. The shooter becomes the subject and the viewer became the shooter. Before we left, her father noticed I loved his special tea from his neighbor so much that he gifted me a big bag of tea leaves which was the best tasting tea I ever drank. It almost felt illegal how good it was. They called it phoenix tears. And I cried when it was all gone. Gumpoongs cousin picked us up and drove us all around the village until nightfall to visit the temples scattered across the town and have a couple of coconuts and tom yum soup at the local night street market before taking me back to their families hotel.

artworks.label: No. 252  —  December 15, 2023
artworks.title: Silhouettes of Shapes and Shadows
artworks.diary: It was sunrise at the golden Buddhist temple of Wat Phra Doi Kham on the mountain top with a giant white Buddha sitting on the edge. It is 2023, the year of the dragon. We entered the gold plated walkway with 2 dragon rails that coil up towards the ornate opening of the sacred space to pray and meditate. The light at the temple was blinding so bright as the walls and grounds are white and details shining gold. All you can see are the silhouettes of shapes and shadows if you make photos. A piercing light that cleanses the soul.

artworks.label: No. 253  —  December 16, 2023
artworks.title: Gentle Giants
artworks.diary: Nonthawit & Wannisa picked me up in the morning to go meet a family of elephants in the forest outside of town. Just like horseback riding you can ride an Elephant. We fed them and met the baby elephant that was born earlier in the year. I paid for the lovely couple to ride together while I stood on the ground below walking beside them with the elephants to make their portraits. It was a calming and peaceful ride, and I was able to make a ton of photographs and the perfect shot of the couple in different perspectives. Even though the ride was over the place was empty so the elephants owner let me sit on top of the elephant. I pet her head and felt the thick skin and strong hairs on top of its skull. I deeply connect with the elephant spirit as I am an admirer of Ganesha, the remover of obstacles. And even though I smoked a lot of weed in my life from an early age, I have a memory like an elephant. Elephants are gentle and they are like humans in a way. When one of their pack dies they grieve their loss. They revisit the place that the elephant died or is buried. The way animals think and behave seem foreign to us, but really they feel what we feel. Love, pain, anger, dare I say hope? We too are animals, just the dumb ones who think they are smarter than the rest of the animal kingdom. Perhaps we need to remove the ego, step out of time, and look deeply into the eyes and hearts of other living creatures. Sure we may be smarter than a chicken or a goat, but are we sweeter than those animals? In Buddhism, they teach us to be vegetarian because we do not want to consume or create suffering of another living thing. How do we create empathy if we do not look at these souls with eyes of understanding? We are not better or worse, we are just different. We think differently, we see ourselves and think we know ourselves. But do we? We are, humans. And humans are part of the animal kingdom. Top of the food chain, right? We built tools and weapons to hunt and kill to eat and live; but we too can also create farms and agriculture. There are animals with bigger brains like dolphins, and stronger than us like elephants. Yet, they are kind. How can humans become kinder to other species. Kinder to ourselves? To see an animal not as food but as a friend. On Earth, in the garden of Eden we are all equal life forces with a soul and a heart that beats. The elephants teach us humility, in a way they can teach us how to be even more human on how they look out for one another, and for their offspring. Elephants are gentle giants. What does that make us?

artworks.label: No. 254  —  December 17, 2023
artworks.title: The Night Market
artworks.diary: At the night market with my friend Hean, I met up with Rathanak and Lynna. We all shared the local foods, some bugs, and lots of noodles! We talked about earlier in the day where Hean brought me to half of the archaeological sites and temples at Angkor Wat. There were mighty jungle trees growing through parts of the temple at Ta Prohm. There is an iconic relief in one of the walls of the monastery. It’s called the Dinosaur of Ta Prohm. “Built by the epic builder king Jayavarman VII in the late 1100s, a small carving on a crumbling temple wall seems to show a dinosaur. a stegosaurus, to be exact.” How could they have known the exact look or even existence of dinosaurs at that time period? Did they discover dinosaur bones then, if they had existed for millions of years I guess they can be dug up, or sticking out of the ground after geological events at any point in the past? Fragments and fossils of the past. As inspiration, weapons and tools, or decoration? It’s fun to think about. Visiting these ancient sites makes me wonder. How are they built so well so long ago? How are they perfectly harmonious with the path of the rising sun and full lunar cycles? To the exact degree the corners are made with tools we don’t have today. Facing the same direction and coordinates as the constellations that reflects the weight and measurements. Like a mathematical golden ratio that shifts the resonance and frequency of those who visit the site. A portal of healing and prayer. It is like time stops when you visit the past and its ancient mysteries. Where does our curiosity lead? Thoughts and ideas on how this could be. Who they could have been. How can this all be made. Where did they all go? And, how did we forget how to build or remember?

artworks.label: No. 255  —  December 18, 2023
artworks.title: Where Vishnu Met Buddha
artworks.diary: The portal gate was opened to another dimension. There stood two star crossed lovers observing a sunrise on the Winter Solstice at Angkor Wat. A temple complex with a complex history that carries the wisdom of Hinduism and Buddhism traditions. A meditation station; Where Vishnu met Buddha.

artworks.label: No. 256  —  December 19, 2023
artworks.title: Nature Truly Is Our Mother and Healer
artworks.diary: On the last day before heading to Australia, Hean brought me to the Pink, Banteay Srei, and Bayon temples starting at sunrise because I had a sunset flight out. We drove a couple hours outside of town to reach the further temples and stopped for snacks on the way. The tastiest and largest, unique style of Cashews I had ever seen. Do you know how a Cashew is grown? It will blow your mind. Every single Cashew grows from a mango looking apple. So it requires tons of food waste and mango-apples to fill a bag of nuts. Every time you eat a Cashew nut! Remember how much energy went into that single food source. We carried on the journey with a handful of coconuts, cashew apples, and honey from the jungle. Hean was telling me horror stories about tourists who had visited these temples back in the 80s or 90s. Until we made it to his favorite place, a surprise he was waiting to show me. Another temple? No! It was the most majestic Waterfall system. We hopped into rented bathing suits and took a cold plunge into the strong force of the falls. I planted on top of one of the rocks and let the water beat down on my back like a massage. It was releasing so much tension and saturating me with life force like blood in the veins and vessels. Adrenaline pumping and awe as wondering. Nature truly is our mother and healer. We swam for an hour then dried up to head home. I remember buying a few stones of Amethysts and Smokey Quartz geodes as a gift to my guide and friends back home. I collected crystals everywhere I had gone till my bag of rocks got heavy. The sun was setting and I had arrived to the airport a few hours early. I tried to check in and the man ate the gate said I needed a visa. I was dumbfounded and sweating with anxiety as my flight was in 3 hours. He said to download the app and enter my information. Sometimes it works instantly, sometimes it takes 24 hours. I hurried over to park my things down and searched for wifi in the airport. A bar of service was my only hope. Entered my info and prayed for help which felt like a late weekend for someone to be approving my visa so soon. Yet, alas! 10 minutes later I received an email with an approval and my stress broke free from me. I was in the clear and went back up to the gate to get my ticket printed. All was good, so I decided to download New Zealand visa too, It also took a few minutes to process and approve. Things were in flow. Now I am off to another continent, Oceania, to the world down under.

artworks.label: No. 257  —  December 20, 2023
artworks.title: Right-Click Save as Guy
artworks.diary: My first day in Australia I was welcome with open arms and an open heart by Jane and GT. They run Oshi Gallery that supports emerging and established local artists. Within the first ten minutes I met them we shot this acrobatic portrait of them out front their gallery beside the CCO Xcopy mural of Right-click save as guy. I hung out there every day while I was in town and was even invited to stay an extra few days at their house on the big hill with their wonderful pup. Every day we went to go see art in different parts of the city. We began right in the heart, their space. It felt a lot like being home. Somewhere I feel like I belong, and with help I met many new friends just by being at their space.

artworks.label: No. 258  —  December 21, 2023
artworks.title: Banana Zone
artworks.diary: Banana Zone

artworks.label: No. 259  —  December 22, 2023
artworks.title: Caterpillars and Computers
artworks.diary: Marka & Steve hanging out with the Caterpillars and Computers mural by Keith Haring, made in 1984. “The distinctive artwork has been visible from Johnston Street, Collingwood, ever since. The mural was added to the Victorian Heritage Register in 2004. Restoration and conservation work was undertaken in 2013 with financial support from the Victorian Government.” Keith Haring wrote: “I am interested in making art to be experienced and explored by as many individuals as possible with as many individual ideas about the given piece with no final meaning attached. The viewer creates the reality, the meaning, the conception of the piece. I am merely the middleman, trying to bring ideas together.” - Keith Haring Journals, 1996

artworks.label: No. 260  —  December 23, 2023
artworks.title: Him Protecting It, and Me Absorbing It
artworks.diary: The plan today was to meet my friend Claudia’s son at AC/DC Lane, where all the street art is living and breathing from bricks to walls. There were many alleys in that area with different stories being told through spray paint. So much so they host street art tours in the neighborhood. Reminded me a bit of home back in Bushwick, Brooklyn. The artists are close! As this was a week in Melbourne to get cultured through art I thought this was a great location to convey in the film. I got a call and he was not going to make it, even though I was waiting there for 2 hours. He had to go buy Christmas gifts. I get it! So, I strolled into the museum and took my time to breathe and think. Deep in the unknown. Going from knowing who I will photograph to looking for a new subject. I paused in the Aboriginal arts museum nearby. A man was following me around in the empty halls of the museum. I met the security guard named, Chee Leong Cheong, at the National Gallery of Victoria in the Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Galleries. He said he liked my tattoos and asked me more questions than you think a security guard at in a gallery should be asking. Since it was just he and I, I think he felt a warm presence and opened up. We started walking and talking about the art and gave me a tour of the place since he was just going on break. Chee told me about his boxing life outside of the walls of art and showed me pictures of winning matches on a phone. Then it hit me! Chee is the one. So I showed him the camera and asked to make his portrait with his favorite artworks. He had two, so we went over to this large abstract work and stood there and started smiling a lot. Then we walked over to another sculpture piece and made his polaroid there. We rode the escalators down to the lobby and he opened the doors for me. It’s funny how things can change so fast when you think you know what is going to happen, then something even more special occurs out of the nothingness. And it is simply by being open, open to possibilities, and open to others when they approach you in a safe place with a kind pace. We became friends over the love of art. Him protecting it, and me absorbing it. In that gallery, the art brought us together. As I believe, art will always lead the way. A symbol, a path, a beacon of hope.

artworks.label: No. 261  —  December 24, 2023
artworks.title: I Know a Place
artworks.diary: We woke up at sunrise before our flight to Uluru. Dundo drove from the city to where GT lives an hour in the countryside. I was asking GT where we may find the kangaroos and he said they’re all over the fucking place! “You’ll see. I know a place.” So we drove in his truck to the misty golf course at the country club. No security, no problem! We drove up on the green and there they were eating the grass like natural lawn mowers. I even had this theory that kangaroos evolved as bunnies when they first arrived by ship and ate up all the grass across the continent to become big boxing marsupials. Anyway, there were hordes of them gently grazing. We walked carefully to not scare them off. Some peaked there eye up and hopped away. Especially the babies. So we scouted the area and calmly walked around while they were eating and the gents were hitting golf balls in our direction. Then we found an open green and a swarm of Roos. This was the last chance before the sun came up and they go back into the forest. We made this portrait and GT started to talk to them to get their attention and we recorded them hopping away as Dundo stood there by the tree. As soon as the shot was done they took drove me to the airport and met with Lambie from the Banana shot and Gursh, a new friend of GTs that I met at Oshi gallery, to join me for Christmas in Uluru!

artworks.label: No. 262  —  December 25, 2023
artworks.title: A Christmas Miracle
artworks.diary: When I first got down in Uluru with Lambie and Gersh, I was manifesting a portrait with the locals. To honor them and their land. The second we got into town I ran into Lance & Julie Peck. Lance stood in the entrance to the town square with his wife who is a prolific aboriginal painter in these parts. She’s even in a few museums around the country. Lance and I hit it off and started talking about the paintings she was making. He said he would take me to Uluru on Christmas tomorrow and was happy to be a part of the art project with his family to respect and represent his culture and heritage. It was an early Christmas morning and Lance was waiting for me where we had originally met. He was with his daughter and granddaughter. Before we drove to the sacred site. Lance showed me a few of Julie’s paintings. I had a gut instinct to buy their incredible work. On this holiday, I was dressed in red and felt like old Saint Nick in this small town as I walked around the square and continued to buy more paintings from each family. Lance says they are all cousins. So, I was happy to be collecting their artwork and helping out as much as I could. I left with around 11 pieces. Some to keep and some to gift to family and friends. The canvases were covered in their ancient cosmological lore and myths of creation. The Seven Sisters make up the stars in the sky at night. Where we all stem from. I rolled up the canvases into one big cylinder, threw it in the trunk, and packed out the car with the locals. We rode over to Uluru rock and there was no one in sight; it was just the family and I. I chose a specific painting that Julie painted which struck so deeply at my core. I asked Lance and Julie to hold the artwork up together in front of the holy mountain while I made my artwork with their permission and grace. It was a Christmas miracle to make this special portrait. It was the art energy that brought us together!

artworks.label: No. 263  —  December 26, 2023
artworks.title: Jester to the Ancient Kingdom
artworks.diary: Before heading to the airport to Sydney. Lambie, Gersh, and I rode over to Kata Tjuta, the sister site to Ayers Rock for sunrise. There were many scattered mounds of ancient rock in this region. We arrived 30 minutes before sunrise watching the sky go from a dark blue hue to a glowing orange sun. We were the only people there at the time. The birds were chirping and watching us as we watched them. Three little birds whistling their happy tune. Three little humans catching a smile in the eyes of a sunrise burning through the sky. The orange sun, the red sand, and the blue sky all as one. Piercing the heart of Sir Gersh and his whacky fit. A shaman in his own right, a jester to the ancient kingdom we stood on. Somewhere out here in the middle of the desert, in the center of Australia. Empty lands with road runners and racing red kangaroos.

artworks.label: No. 264  —  December 27, 2023
artworks.title: A Sunday Afternoon
artworks.diary: After, “A Sunday Afternoon on the Island of La Grande Jatte.”

artworks.label: No. 265  —  December 28, 2023
artworks.title: Sacrifice to the Water Gods
artworks.diary: My buddy Onil connected me to his artist friend Ryan. His studio was facing directly onto Tamarama beach, where all the dogs go to play. Where you can walk on the rocks like it’s an aquatic planet, or a water ride at Disney Land. Ryan runs a pottery studio right above the beach. A dream of paradise. Art and Ocean together like that. Ryan asked if I ever made pottery before, “I did not but I always wanted to!” So he sat me down at a clay station, wet my hands, and threw down some clay for me to play with. It felt natural making the gentle grooves of the tea cup we were making. I busted up a thick cup for tea ceremonies and felt proud of myself. Now we had to wait! So we ran down to the water with Sarah and Zena, who were also playing with clay in the studio. Ryan brought down to the low tide a half broken and still wet pot, after we smoked a bit of pots. While we were in the ocean to make an artistic sacrifice to the water gods the tide started to rise and the coral pond flooded our friends. Looking back it’s one of those things that push you forward. For years while living in NYC I would always walk past a pottery studio called Mano on 26th street on my way to the photo studio. And every day I would tell myself I would take a class. Ten years later, in the middle of a strangers garage, Far out in the corners of Australia I found myself, getting in touch with an ancient art and a doorway I always wanted to walk through. Now that the window is open the fear if trying, or doing something new, no longer exists. It no longer limits the infinite possibilities of fun. Because now, I know how true it is for me. Just like surfing in Peru. You learn how to do things in other places that you normally overlook at home. Then you begin to appreciate how close to home it always was, and start to go. I just had to get out of my comfort zone and try something new, that I always knew would make joy come true.

artworks.label: No. 266  —  December 29, 2023
artworks.title: A Talking Tropical Parrot
artworks.diary: A man with a talking tropical Parrot magically appeared on the walkway as we were looking for a place to shoot the family portrait. The old man placed the bird on the boys head and turned our walk into a circus. The bird was balanced and still. Even when the boy was practicing his free throws. The old man turned back around and started getting mad. He took the bird back into his hand and walked off. We observed the architecture from afar of the iconic Opera House. While Onil son shoots for the invisible hoop in the air right at the buzzer. Then… Swoosh; It’s all over when the fat lady sings.

artworks.label: No. 267  —  December 30, 2023
artworks.title: Surf’s Up
artworks.diary: Surfs Up in Bondi. When you are in the barrel of a wave it is pure bliss. The ultimate high in life. An impeding presence that carries you forward. Nature’s energy harnessed by the board. Somewhere in between motion and stillness since the wave you the force pushing you. The balance between air and water, from riding on top of the board until you go below the water. A push and pull like the tides themselves. It intuition that teaches you when to start to swim to take upon the wave. Sitting in the water waiting for the right wave, the right moment to move. You can’t catch all the waves, and the right ones will find you. Surfing is a game of patience, then thrill. That feeling when you catch a wave is the dopamine I wish to feel every day in my brain. Perhaps because it is the feeling of harmony with nature, with the universe and her invisible forces.

artworks.label: No. 268  —  December 31, 2023
artworks.title: I Now Pronounce You Man and Wife
artworks.diary: I now pronounce you man and wife… is what they say for the kiss that forges a marriage. I met this man and woman on the top of a hill at a park in the windiest city in the world. They were making wedding portraits. Throughout the entire project I was seeking a couple, an image of a wedding. To represent the love in the world. Between two different people. Love leads the way to Peace on Earth. The closest I got to a real wedding ceremony was in India when we crashed a wedding. I had made the portrait of the day earlier that day so will remain true to the moment. Although at the Indian wedding I met the bride and groom and gifted them a Polaroid of their special night in between the two photographers they officially hired. So in a way you can say I photographed two newly weds in this project. One as a gift in the perfect setting at the wrong time, and the other as a blessing to be in the right place at the right time with the right people in their aura of love that shone like a lighthouse in their fair city.

artworks.label: No. 269  —  January 1, 2024
artworks.title: The Celestine Prophecy
artworks.diary: Em met me at Mount Victoria. She brought a copy of Harry Potter and the Sorcerer’s Stone. The tree that we met at was from the film Lord of the Rings: The Fellowship of the Rings. I found that quite uncanny and ironic. Both worlds are made of Magic and adventure telling similar stories and life lessons.

artworks.label: No. 270  —  January 2, 2024
artworks.title: Pet Rock Kiwi
artworks.diary: The misty morning welcomed my day on the farmland at the retired police officers guest house below his balcony where I stayed at. The officer told me he became a farmer. As he just retired right before the pandemic. He was thrilled to show me around with all of his domesticated animals in their play pens, including his precious oxen with a sprained foot. We got along real fast, he and I. Then started to think how ironic it was the night I had arrived I finished the rest of my weed smokes right under his nose before I found out he was the law man. The universe is a comedy and likes to play jokes on us. On my drive from Wellington to New Plymouth I passed a volcano called, Te Papakura O Taranaki. I wondered which Lord of the Rings movie that mountain was filmed in, perhaps Mordor, where the precious ring falleth to restore the order in the land? The clouds covered her softly as I passed by on the back side checking the rear view as stories of her height disappearing into the light grey sky. The sun was coming down in New Plymouth, when I had arrived to meet John and his pet rock Kiwi. A native flightless bird, which is a national symbol of New Zealand. He was a professional photographer and showed me all his works. While the sun was setting golden on his yard we made portraits of one another till the gold light also disappeared. Where does the light go when the day turns to night?

artworks.label: No. 271  —  January 3, 2024
artworks.title: Cosmic Light Beings
artworks.diary: We are all cosmic light beings living on planet Earth.

artworks.label: No. 272  —  January 4, 2024
artworks.title: Punks, Love, and Family
artworks.diary: Auckland was the final stop for the road trip across the upper island of New Zealand. It just happened to be that Danny, aka Seed Phrase, was in town visiting family for the holidays. We had not had a proper hangout in real life as much as we had spoke online over the years. The universe aligned for us in the strangest place of the smallest and coolest corner of the world. We sat by the wharf with his new fiance. Spoke about Punks, Love, and Family. Once we finished our meals we took a stroll by the water where the Yachts were parked. I jokingly asked Danny where his Yacht was on the harbour. He didn’t have one but the Bored Ape Yacht Club that he held in one of his various wallets. We all laughed and then I saw a picture perfect moment stirring up. The drawbridge was rising, the yachts were passing, the wind was blowing, and then these two love birds looked each other in their eyes and kissed. When you do what you love and live your truth, its real that you will find that true love, whether its inside of you, or in someone else. Art will always lead the way to more love in life.

artworks.label: No. 273  —  January 5, 2024
artworks.title: Her Thinking Place
artworks.diary: Originally, I was supposed to fly out to Vietnam on this day. Perhaps the weight of all the nonstop travel and carrying so much on my back had broken something in me. It was painful to move and to even stand up. It was my bodies way of telling me to STOP! So, I listened. I missed my flight to a country I always wanted to visit to take care of my health. To see a chiropractor and they simply told me to rest. Once I left their office, I mustered up all my strength to meet with Sarah.
