We met at a parking lot at her favorite place to shoot, since she too was a photographer. You can see the cloudy city between these pillars where the water was gently flowing. This was her thinking place, where she came to make her abstract art. She stopped me in my tracks and said, this is the place I would like you to photograph me. I squeezed her into the frame to compose this shot of alignment and stillness. For a minute there, while we were creating art, I forgot I had any pain at all. It was like a moment of clarity. Letting go of any distress I was consumed by. One minute it felt like I was Atlas carrying the world, the next I was free of all the pain and sorrows my back had accumulated on 100 flights and nonstop motion like Io in the myth of Prometheus. It started to rain and we went for breakfast. In the car she was telling me about her past life as a pilot, and I had many questions about aviation and safety. She answered them all with a smile. We had arrived to a place which took a while to seat us, then the server never came as we sat for an hour so decide to leave. My back was starting to inflame again like the healing spell had wore off and it was excruciating. It was time for me to go home to rest to give my back a break. It was the first and only time in the project this had happened. Perhaps a sign from the universe to stay in New Zealand for a few more days before going to Asia. I was bummed to miss out on Vietnam, but some things you have to accept just don’t work out when you are not feeling right. And that’s okay! We carry on to where we are now and make sure we take care of our only body, the temple, the vessel, we have. To not over do it because of obligation, and to be flexible and adapt when the plan has to change.

artworks.label: No. 274  —  January 6, 2024
artworks.title: Stairway to Heaven
artworks.diary: Instead of heading to Southeast Asia as planned I hopped over to the southern island of New Zealand to a city called, Christchurch. A photographer named Richie came to pick me up at the airport then we drove into the middle of his home city. He showed me around the artsy part of town and walked me through parts that were destroyed by a devastating earthquake years ago. There was a set of stairs wrapped up by a shabby chain link fence that was easy to climb over, and he did. This was the remnants of the building that once stood there. Covered in Graffiti it is now an archeological site of the force of mother nature when her heart beats onto the land through tectonic plates shifting under us. Richie climbed the stairway to heaven and I recorded him as passersby walked their dogs across my lens. He hopped back over the fence when we wrapped up his portrait and headed to the parking garage. I hopped in his car again and we took a ride to the beach house that my shaman and her witchy friend were staying at for the month on their healing quest. On the ride to the mystic home he was telling me stories about his photography and indigenous community and rituals. Once we arrived at my healers house, we all walked barefoot by the water and hung out on the beach for sunset. When the sun rested beneath the sky Richie drove on home to meet with his son for supper. The magic of photography not only freezes the moment we live and see, but forges friendships you never knew you’d meet. We became buds instantly. Starting with camera conversations, and simply bonding over stories and common life experiences. It’s easy to make friends when you love the same things and come from the same cloth. Art and music; Culture and traditions.

artworks.label: No. 275  —  January 7, 2024
artworks.title: Your Tears Are the Prayers
artworks.diary: Sibylle & Claudia were chanting all day preparing for a healing ceremony with me on the beach. They laid down shells and trinkets and prayed to the spirits of the land, sea, and air. It was nearing sunset and the mystic women laid me down on the beach to help me release and cleanse somatic blockages in my back. Releasing guilt and shame that I have been carrying from a past life. Screaming into the sand with no one else in sight, I was freed from this grief. This went on for an hour until I ran towards the ocean and purged my soul from their healing witchcraft. I felt lighter, it felt like purification. The part of my back that ached was gone and loosened. We carry stress and trauma in our bodies for lifetimes. Sometimes it turns into dis-ease if you don’t caretake the issues when it happens. It gets stored and forgotten and blocking life force energy moving up and down your spine. Until one day a kundalini awakening breaks your heart and mind open. We often forget what we carry and its still inside us waiting to be released. Finding the right tools to set us free. Nature is the remedy. Silence to listen to our bodies and feel where we need to bring attention to it. Quieting down from the external noise and traveling within. It does not take long if you listen, as you will feel where it is wrong. To self heal you need the space to do so. Stop the rat race and give yourself that love you desire. True love comes from within, not from without. The ocean waves crashing down are the melody to my salvation. Jumping up and down on the sand, activating all parts of my body. Moving along the lymph nodes and detoxing old emotional wounds. Now, is the time to look at what parts of you need that attention and care. Be present with yourself. Cry and laugh, as your tears are the prayers and laughter is the medicine for your heart to keep the beats flowing.

artworks.label: No. 276  —  January 8, 2024
artworks.title: Robotic Planters
artworks.diary: Shavonne introduced me to the Sky Garden in Singapore. It is a futuristic botanical garden in the south marina. It was tropically foggy in the atmosphere of the city during this time of year. Everywhere was hot and humid. The climate complimented the attraction, which made it feel like an otherworldly planet with robotic planters. We found a perfect pink ground spotlight that lit Shavonne for the video shoot. It was getting dark and she recommended we visit a night market for yummy food to eat the local cuisines. I trusted her to do all the ordering as I could not read the menus and she was the local that knew the best spots. All she said was to get a table and she’ll handle the rest. After ten minutes passed she came back with trays of foods from different vendors. Talking about digital art as we ate amazing noodles and soups. We were both stuffed and felt like we gained 20 lbs each by the end of it. The journey continued, after I found a fruit stall with bags filled with jackfruit, we walked towards a foot massage spot that she goes to every week with her husband. She sat me down in a chair and the parlor folks worked their magic. They were beating the shit out of my feet to the point where it hurt, yet relieved so much tension and pressure in the body. Its funny how that works. I was cringing in pain and the staff just kept laughing at me like a silly American. Shavonne showed no signs of pain, as she was laughing too. I was snacking on the Jackfruit trying to cope with the hour long endurance test. Though when we left I felt pretty amazing and my pot belly had calmed down a bit. We parted ways as it was time for her to go to bed, and time for me to head to the hotel. We planned to meet again tomorrow to meet with Clara at her gallery show.

artworks.label: No. 277  —  January 9, 2024
artworks.title: Everything Comes Full Circle
artworks.diary: Shavonne and I met with our friend and curator, Clara. We met at Claras favorite ice cream parlor before walking over to the Gillman Barracks. A year prior, Clara included in an art exhibition showcasing my Doppelganger work, The museum was closed so we decided to make outside of the doors on the same floor where the art was shown. A symbolic gesture to honor our connection and our past that brought us together through art, and now making art in the same place. Everything comes full circle. From online to real life, and back online again. There are no borders when working in digital art, and there are friends all over the world. We are all just nodes looking to connect with one another. What makes the world a smaller place over time but meeting people everywhere you go. After traveling you get a sense of space and gain a sense of self and how the world works as you navigate it. All it takes is time to get from one place to another, time you have to commit to the journey. You can literally go anywhere, and all you need is the time to get there. Sometimes, right where you are is right where you need to be. Art lead the way to more art. Always say yes to an art show. To be part of something bigger than yourself so the work can live on its own.

artworks.label: No. 278  —  January 10, 2024
artworks.title: The Dragon Playground
artworks.diary: Kevin invited me to breakfast at his part of town where he grew up called, Toa Payoh. When I arrived I was greeted by a kind smile and a big bowl of noodles and eggs. He was with his shy girlfriend who did not like to be photographed. While we were eating we were discussing digital art and the future of NFT technology. We both came to an agreement that we are at the right place at the right time in this art movement. After we had finished eating we walked over to his apartment complex. Kev wanted us to do the video shoot at the Dragon playground where he used to play as a kid. It was a sense of nostalgia and connecting to roots of childhood. It took a few tries asking his beloved girlfriend to be a part of the shoot. She reluctantly agreed and faced the opposite way on the horsie seesaw. It was her way of being in the shot, without being in the shot. When you make portraits of people your job is to make them feel seen and beautiful. Honoring the subject always with deep respect. Find the light that lands on them to make them look and FEEL good about themselves. Our superpower is making people fall in love with themselves in how you see them and see the world; It’s beauty. To see the light in others. The dragon is the protector. A symbol of flight fantasy. 2024 was the year of the Dragon, and we all rode in on the royal red dragon right through the town. Bringing in the year with an ancient cosmic force. Do dragons still exist? The fire they breathe, the wings they flap, and the treasure they guard is all real. Representations and states of emotions. Like passion, flow, and wisdom.

artworks.label: No. 279  —  January 11, 2024
artworks.title: The Concrete Jungle
artworks.diary: Singapore is a city that’s buildings are covered in plants. To make us feel back in touch with our roots in the concrete jungle with the illusion of green grass that covers the walls teeming with life and cleansing the air. A futuristic city that shows the potentials of what a place can be like when nature comes first and pollution an afterthought. To create a future that integrates nature than dominates her for all her beauty and resources until forests are turned into dwellings and there is no longer air to breathe. Plant more trees, more green in the red and grey cities. Developers, bring us back home as we yearn to return to the goddess that gave us air and fruit. We just want to play with the leaves and leave this city. Where did nature go, and why cant she be a part of our future as she was the one who gave us life to our past? Imaginary lines are more important than the air we breathe, so be it. Profit shares overrides the prophets words. When did we lose sight of what’s right and necessary for our survival as a species? Is there time left to turn a new leaf and make the world go green for a climate collapse? Does mother Earth have plans of her own with or without our choice. We can only adapt, to become symbiotic than a parasite feeding on her blood and oil till she dries up and the waves come crashing down again as they have twice before. With Noah and Gilgamesh as our heroes of the great floods, who will be the champions of tomorrow?

artworks.label: No. 280  —  January 12, 2024
artworks.title: Tuancheng Fortress
artworks.diary: It was a cold and snowy evening at the Tuancheng Fortress. Wang Fei is a student of the Ip Man school of kung fu and self defense. Scarlet brought us together. She flew from Cheng Du and set me up with a ride from the airport to one of the most legendary Peking duck in the city where I met her and Wang Fei. We walked over to the fortress where he showed us some of his moves kicking snowflakes in mid air with precision and discipline. He is a spiritual warrior in the cold air of the empty night. There were only guards and us. I was worried that the video wouldn’t come out as there was barely any light illuminating him. Scarlet held two phones up to light him while he was making his moves. The film grain feels like the white snow, and the fortress from the past subtly fills the background in all of its red and gold glory and majesty of the dynasty of ancient Chinese emperors who built this Forbidden city.

artworks.label: No. 281  —  January 13, 2024
artworks.title: Through the Arctic Mist
artworks.diary: Scarlet and I adventured to the Great Wall of China. We rode in the gondola that glided us up over the mountains to the top of the wall. It was snowing and the wall was a frozen tundra. People were slipping and sliding down the stones like skaters in a hockey rink. You needed to grab hold of a busy rope to go up and down the steeper slopes. We made it to a soft patch that overlooks the landscape even though you could not see anything outside the wall. The wind was howling as the icy crystals were gently sweeping through the arctic mist. Scarlet with her royal red fan, fanning fabric through the cool winter air.

artworks.label: No. 282  —  January 14, 2024
artworks.title: May You Live with Ease
artworks.diary: May you be happy May you be healthy May you be peaceful May you live with ease

artworks.label: No. 283  —  January 15, 2024
artworks.title: Art and Healing
artworks.diary: Art and Healing on Venice beach with Sheila Darcey. We first met on Clubhouse when we started a room together where artists got together to share their personal stories and created a safe space online to be vulnerable and honest. To share your heart and be heard. Art brought us all together, it was our vehicle to heal our souls from past trauma. When you share your story you let it all go. The pain, the grief, the great release. The talking cure is real. When you speak of what is difficult you’ve been through, you overcome it by owning it in that moment. Clean out the skeletons in your closet and set them free. Set yourself free from unexcavated grief. Of loss, of hurt, of all the pain that never belonged to us. We give it back to mother Earth. Where the waves take them from us like fruit plucked from a tree. For her to eat and nourish from our wounds to be made into energy for the sea. A transmutation from our bodies to the ocean floor. Where new life can grow from within us, and more.

artworks.label: No. 284  —  January 16, 2024
artworks.title: The Mechanical Bird
artworks.diary: We ride the mechanical bird to take us from land over water. To reach the other side of what exists beyond what we know. The world is connected by flight and sounds. All it takes is 24 hours to navigate the world. Home is not where you are from. It is where you are.

artworks.label: No. 285  —  January 17, 2024
artworks.title: Until Next Time
artworks.diary: The last stop at the end of the Earth before taking a ship to the arctic walls that lay ahead the Drakes passage. From the thick white clouds in the sky to the rough grey waters in the ocean, we fly and sail into infinity. Dreadfully shaking from the bumpy air. There is no end, when you travel around. We say our hellos and our goodbyes, until next time. Heading to the south pole to reach a part of the world that is rare to be. Where the sun does not go down in the midst of night. Just pure silence with crystal blues and clear whites. Cities of penguins and gangs of leopard seals. Birds that flew many miles without rest, and orcas that hideout from the west. This place is a sanctuary. The purest place on Earth. We head to Antarctica from here. Ushuaia, with one last letter to mail at the post office at the bottom of the world.

artworks.label: No. 286  —  January 18, 2024
artworks.title: Captain’s Log
artworks.diary: Captains log. We are in the heart of the Drakes Passage. The ocean is clear as glass and placid like a lake without wind hovering over its surface. Sometimes you hear 2 day horror stories about this merciless glacial strait. Rogue waves can strike from any side by the unstoppable forces while the ship is already rocking wildly from bow to stern through violent waters. We got really lucky. The captain of the vessel invited us onto the holodeck. The captain was a humble Argentinian man in a throne-like chair surrounded by sailors and sonar instruments keeping us on track and right on time. The floating automaton was doing all the heavy lifting. We just had to sit back and relax with the best view on the ship. The driver’s seat. At one point the captain let me steer the ship, or so I thought… We lived on the water for 2 days before seeing a single Emperor penguin. We anchored near the beachy remnants of the Andes still protruding out of the ocean, which make up most of the land masses in the Antarctic. Nothing but snow white and blue glaciers with a golden sun that never sets or rises. Lots of whale activity in these parts. This is where they go this season when escaping the peril of the humans above. The ship was our home. Most of the people on the boat were over 50 except the crew. It was our mission to meet every single person on the ship. We made a pact to say hi and talk to every soul on board. We might as well, while we are all stuck on this hunk of luxurious metal together for the next two weeks! And, it’s more fun when you know everyone.

artworks.label: No. 287  —  January 19, 2024
artworks.title: Happy Feet
artworks.diary: Happy Feet, Happy Family.

artworks.label: No. 288  —  January 20, 2024
artworks.title: No Other Blue
artworks.diary: We made it through the Drakes Passage and onto the land. We stepped foot onto the Neko Harbour and climbed up the glacier. We helped our new friend, Christine, who was visiting from Jamaica walk step by step as far as she could climb and back again. It was a great reminder to slow down and appreciate the beauty around us. That deep aquatic blue that is almost gem-like between the cracks of the ice that envelopes the landscape. There is no other blue that exists this way, and it only lasts for a second when the light hits the edges and turns it inside out to a calm shade of grey. I remember reaching the top and then having an asthma attack. My inhaler was inside the boat and was doing my best to make it to the ship with tight lungs and thin cold air. At some point I started seeing stars and colors in my vision and held on, focused on breathing techniques. Sweating with anxiety and overcoming with slow stepping and deep breathing. It’s funny because when you focus so much on how you cant breathe, that is all your mind can reflect to you. But when you start to focus on how to breathe, then you can stop the asthmatic panic. You almost need to let go and forget its happening and calm down for it to stop. In the case if you do not have the medicine, this is what saved my life a few times. Even running to a yoga class, which in itself is an ironic instance, having an asthma attack in the middle if hot yoga. Where all you can do is breathe as the teacher guides you. By the end of the class it was gone, when the mind lets it go. It is scary, and makes me more mindful to remember to breathe every moment, in the middle of the day, where your body autonomously functions even if we don’t perceive while it is happening as we speak.

artworks.label: No. 289  —  January 21, 2024
artworks.title: The Last Place We Were Ever Meant to Be
artworks.diary: When you think of Antarctica you think of ice. Where is the land that exists that makes this place the 7th continent? Under the ice that took millions of years to compact. There are pink sandy beaches and metamorphic rocks that are teeming with animal and plant life. Emperor penguins come here to nest their young. They dont leave their side until they are grown. Sometimes their eggs get picked off by other species of birds hunting from the sky. There were towns of penguins gathered together. Swimming, sliding, squawking around. They are the true citizens of this continent. All dressed up in their tuxedos for every occasion. Civilized creatures, unlike their mortal enemy. The Leopard seal. Those seals eat penguins for breakfast, lunch, and dinner. Sometimes the orca whales come out to play and find their prey, penguins and seals. Outside of the animal food chain there is peace on Earth. Antarctica is where peace exists. All countries working together in the name of science. No one has claim to any territory, as like the moon in space. On this ice planet, can we truly get along? Maybe peace begins in the last place we were ever meant to be. In harsh conditions, create cooperation. I really wonder what goes on down there. Ancient aliens bases, the entrance to hollow earth, the ice walls that house us. or simply the south pole covered with ice. There must be something to discover, after all Pangea broke apart with tectonic plates drifted over millions of years. Our history buried in deep snow, somewhere deep in a base underground. How many people live on Antarctica year round? Other than the penguins who inhabit the South pole raising their young. They are the rulers of this land, the Emperor penguins reign to covet their offspring for generations after generations. The safest place on Earth, away from all the humans who bring them bird flus. So do not touch the birds, don’t get too close. Respect the flightless bird and laugh at their jokes. They are funny little critters slipping and sliding around their towns. They just want to live in peace as we do when we are home too.

artworks.label: No. 290  —  January 22, 2024
artworks.title: Voyage Leader
artworks.diary: Voyage leader, Jonathan Zaccaria, took us out in the morning sun for a private ride on the Zodiac to create adventurous portraits of him in action by the Antarctic peninsula. Surrounded by snow capped Andes mountains and icy glaciers breaking off into the ocean. You can hear the crackling miles away like an echo of the Earth shattering. The water a crystalline blue that exists nowhere else. The purest place on Earth. Untapped by human traces, other than the boats that traverse through the landscape every once in a while. Does that add to the pollution and co2 in the atmosphere? Visiting this sacred place that only the animals dwell and thrive. Is it right for us to be there? Is there a corner of the Earth we can let go and let live without controlling the outcome. A peace treaty written by all nations that no nation can claim Antarctica for its own. Only inhabited for science, to understand the planet better; its history and future. Where did the land arrive from, and where did all the snow fall? How will the snow melt and what will that do for us all? Can we control the rate of the rising tides, or is that hubris thinking us humans can change the world? Our actions polluting from industrialization. When will we as a species think through regeneration. Long term lifespan rather than short term gains. What is more important wealth, or our life on Earth? Will we ever become a symbiotic species that heals the world than drains her oil and blood. WIth the right leadership and values. Thinking for the next 10,000 years instead of the next 10 months. Shifting our mindset from survival to caretaking. Humans were born to be the custodians of mother Earth. She provides all our needs for free. Where did money come and trick us into this system of greed? It is time for us to be freed from the illusion and share in the abundance. Where each tree bears a hundred fruits, and each fruit a hundred seeds. That is true abundance, that which multiplies from the original. A fractalized system that was here before we were born and evolved into this thinking being in which we became. Will we return to nature, integrate before it’s too late, or destroy ourselves and the ice in the Antarctic before it’s too late and the coasts are flooded again like Noah and Gilgamesh? I have faith in humanity, we can overcome as we have for the last 10,000 years of written history. Passing the wisdoms across new generations, teaching our woes and mistakes, to create a future for humanity to reach the stars and bear fruits on other planets just like Earth.

artworks.label: No. 291  —  January 23, 2024
artworks.title: I Will Meet You at the Ends of the Earth
artworks.diary: I will meet you at the ends of the Earth

artworks.label: No. 292  —  January 24, 2024
artworks.title: Reach Out
artworks.diary: When you reach out to the universe, the universe reaches back to you.

artworks.label: No. 293  —  January 25, 2024
artworks.title: In Another Life
artworks.diary: We will see each other in another life, where we are both cats.

artworks.label: No. 294  —  January 26, 2024
artworks.title: I Dream of You Kissing Me in the Light
artworks.diary: she found me dancing in the streets. I dream of you kissing me in the light. Walking beside me each and every day. In our home city. We play, we work, we love and cook. Through out the seasons as they change. Do we stay the same? Our connection grows like a tree when it bears its leaves, to when they fall to soil the earth. Seeds get buried into our minds. From a whisper to her laughter the love grows inside of me. I found her dancing in the streets. We kissed again in the dark in the shade, where life as one became the fulfilled dream. Together, the two hearts sing and beat. Two bees buzzing, then comes the ring.

artworks.label: No. 295  —  January 27, 2024
artworks.title: Self Reflection
artworks.diary: How do we see ourselves in a world of people who see us differently? You are a different person to everyone else than you are to yourself. What is the space between where the shadow meets the self reflection? We are all just apparitions of emotions dressed in light called human.

artworks.label: No. 296  —  January 28, 2024
artworks.title: Cold Drinks on a Hot Day
artworks.diary: Today opened my eyes more deeply and my heart more felty. I was obsessed with looking for dancers in Bueno Aires to do the Tango for the shoot while we are in town. I was so blinded by this idea and was seeking something that was not happening. So we rested in the park to sit and chill, sip on Mate and smoke some weed. There was a man zipping around in his electric wheelchair selling drinks out of a cooler. Buzzing around the park. Ethan went to go get a drink from him and as he was talking to him I observed. And suddenly it hit me, wait… Why am I seeking dancers when there is this man, this person who cannot move his feet. Something in me shifted, an awareness arose out of this simple interaction. I walked up to the man and bought all of his drinks to share with my friends and even the man to quench his thirst on a hot day. We made a portrait together and he was the best model and loved being part of the project. I realized this was the magic. The connection, the realization that it’s all right in front of our eyes if we look deeply and feel more intuitively to what’s happening around us. It’s about appreciating what this man taught us. You don’t have to have legs to dance, the dance is simply how you move around in your own way. One of the most impactful lessons I’ve learned on this project. Set a goal, but don’t seek it out. Let it happen, and be patient and mindful as this energy can show up in any form at any time. Even as a man in a wheelchair making a living selling his cold drinks on a hot day. Life is simple, so why complicate it? It’s all about love anyway. To see instead of seek.

artworks.label: No. 297  —  January 29, 2024
artworks.title: The Thinking Man Meets the Thinking Man
artworks.diary: The thinking man meets the thinking man.

artworks.label: No. 298  —  January 30, 2024
artworks.title: Rano Kau
artworks.diary: There is an ecosystem inside of Cráter volcanico. An extinct volcano that became fertile land. Home to plants and animals below sea level; Bees, pink pineapples, and bananas. Oh, how the Earth transforms and changes over the ages. Around the corner is Petroglifos Rano Kau. A stone carved symbol of the bird man who was inhabited the island that we came to know as “Easter Island.” Where did all the trees go on this island, and how did they carve such large structures in the shapes of human forms? That is the great mystery of this small and remote island. An ancient unknown. With only glyphs and statues that litter the island of a lasting legacy of those who dwelled once before, and the families of them who still remain.

artworks.label: No. 299  —  January 31, 2024
artworks.title: Giants Frozen in Time
artworks.diary: “The Moai are monolithic human figures carved from stone by the Rapa Nui people, on Rapa Nui in eastern Polynesia between the years 1250 and 1500. Nearly half are still at Rano Raraku, the main moai quarry.” How did these people carve these figures from the quarry and what were they used for; Offerings? Prayers? Gifts to the elders for a hand to marry? To prove who which clan was more superior? Buried and forgotten for ages until they surfaced again as a mystery. A civilization bent on crafting art. Sculptures that mimic those who dwell on this small remote island paradise. Stone armies of the native people resting for almost a century. Ornate eyes of obsidian and back tattoos of paint and pearls. Why do some face down and others still uncut shapes in the quarry? Was there a battle, or was there lost hope because the resources dwindled where casting stone relics did not matter any more, and survival was the focus. The world may never know, but will always wonder. Though, the people who are descendants of the ancestors of the Rapa Nui people never left and may be the wisdom keepers of the stories passed down to modern times. Maybe there is no mystery after all. Their history is now a part of the landscape, burial mounds protected by the giants. But, how did they get all across the islands; Did they walk, or were they moved? The giants frozen in time melting into the ground. Will this ancient art project ever be completed; Which was the last one before they stopped? and, why?

artworks.label: No. 300  —  February 1, 2024
artworks.title: We Dance to Remember
artworks.diary: We dance to honor the ancestors. We dance to respect the land and those who came before us. We dance to connect to the Earth. We dance to move our bodies. We dance to shift the energies inside and out. We dance in synchronization to be one with each other. We dance beneath ancient stone figures that have watched over centuries. We dance as a prayer made from our bodies to the altar where spirit meets Earth. We dance where memory becomes muscle in motion. We dance with each step as we carry the weight of those who danced before us. We dance to remember. We dance because we know that we are not separate from the stone, the sky, the soil. We dance to break the silence that settles over forgotten places. We dance to resurrect the songs that live in our bones. We dance to prove that the human body is a language more honest than words. We dance because standing still in the face of so much beauty and sorrow would be a betrayal. We dance to heal what was broken. We dance to become the bridge between what was and what will be. We dance as the living heartbeat that connects the distant past to an uncertain future. We dance because we are human and that’s how humans move.

artworks.label: No. 301  —  February 2, 2024
artworks.title: Respect the Elders
artworks.diary: Respect the elders, honor the ancestors, protect mother nature, and enjoy your life.

artworks.label: No. 302  —  February 3, 2024
artworks.title: What Goes Around Comes Around
artworks.diary: Esteban met with me early in the morning before the flight to Rio, Brazil. Right when Santa Lucía Hill park opened we took a stroll inside. We walked and talked to get to know each other better. He too was a fellow photographer from the NFT space. There was a fountain we found and I noticed there was a San Pedro cactus growing above it. I asked if he knew what that cactus symbolized, and he responded, you mean Huachuma? Yes! We bonded over the sacred medicine and it was the first time I realized it was common outside of California and Peru. Chile too has rituals and practices for this sacred plant medicine. In that moment I decided to create Estabans portrait, with the cactus as a cameo, and playing around with framing with the steel circles that were the boundaries in the circular garden. He did not know what to do at first so I directed him to walk up to me and reach his hand out to grab the camera. It was the first time doing something like this in the project and had a really neat effect. Always try something new, and what goes around comes around, especially when your in a circular park!

artworks.label: No. 303  —  February 4, 2024
artworks.title: Rasta Beach
artworks.diary: It was the week before carnival in Rio. I got to the hotel elevator and characters busted out laughing and were all dressed up in feathery angel wings and sparkling devil horns. It felt more like a fashion show than it did a festival. People were already drinking and dancing in the street. There was a sense of magic and mystery in the air. Angels and Demons took over the city and the party had not even started yet. It was a pre game. Marcus met me at the hotel in the morning and we took a long, long walk over to “Rasta Beach.” He brought the joints and we found a nice spot on the beach and sparked up. The name is true to its roots. Lots of Rastas and marijuana smoke. People playing football like hackey sack and kids running around playing in the water. The views were incredible. Where the mountains meet the sea. It was truly breathtaking, and even more inspiring since I was pretty high. The energy was immaculate, the vibes were great, and we made art in the beach. Then a rainstorm came and you can see lightning in the distance out at sea. Nobody moved, everyone kept on playing and chilling like the sun was shining in our hearts and souls. The weather didn’t matter. We adjusted to the flow, like the water crashing on the beach and falling from the sky onto the sand.

artworks.label: No. 304  —  February 5, 2024
artworks.title: God Bless You
artworks.diary: God Bless You.

artworks.label: No. 305  —  February 6, 2024
artworks.title: Floating on a Ledge
artworks.diary: We take flight to Lima, Peru. To stay a couple days before the wings to the city in the sky, Cusco. In the meantime, we roamed around this city by the sea. Heading to the beach to remind myself where I learned to surf 8 years ago. For the first ride I rented a board and paddled out with my host. A wave came up and up I went, for the first time on the first try. I rode it all the way back to the beach. A feeling of peace came over me. This is what I want to do the rest of my life. Riding on the waves, at the in between of air and water. Exhilarating stillness in motion. On the walk down from the overview a man named, Henry Jipi, who was floating on a ledge with his mini chute greeting the passersby, like me. We talked and I invited him to be in the project, and he invited me down to go surf by the beach. It was fate, it was friendship! From the sky towards the sea, we took flight in the air and on top of the water.

artworks.label: No. 306  —  February 7, 2024
artworks.title: Cusco
artworks.diary: The Quechuan weaver women of Cusco. An ancient city in the Andes. Built by the Incans. A living archeological site.

artworks.label: No. 307  —  February 8, 2024
artworks.title: Messenger Between Two Worlds
artworks.diary: I visited the Cochahuasi Animal Sanctuary in Pisac to meet the largest flying bird in the world native to the Andes Mountains, the Condor. Their wingspan is as large as a human. They can can glide hundreds of miles with almost no wing flapping. A curious and kind bird when you get up close. It was my muse for the day. Alongside some small monkeys and other critters being rehabilitated to rejoin the wild once they heal up. The condor is a messenger between two worlds. The sky in its divinity & the Earth in its humanity. There is a story about a hummingbird and a condor that I learned on my travels and thought it was a beautiful lesson. “Long ago, when the sky and the earth were closer than they are now, a great imbalance came over the Andes. The winds grew confused. Seasons arrived late. Humans forgot how to listen. The Condor, guardian of the high world, was called to carry a message from the mountains to the heavens. But the journey was long, and the sky had become dangerous— storms, ice, and silence thicker than stone. The Hummingbird, small but relentless, insisted on coming too. The Condor laughed. “You are too tiny,” he said. “The cold will break you. The distance will erase you.” The Hummingbird answered: “Then let me fly where you do not look.” As the Condor rose into the thin air, the winds began to tear at everything light and fragile. At the first great storm, the Hummingbird vanished. The Condor thought the bird lost. But the Hummingbird had slipped beneath the vast wing of the Condor, resting close to his heart, where the wind could not reach. There, the Hummingbird listened. It felt the Condor’s slow, ancient rhythm. It heard the silence between heartbeats. It learned how the sky breathes. When the Condor finally reached the highest place—where words are too large to speak—the great beings of the sky asked: “Where is the small one who dared follow you?” The Condor searched the empty air, ashamed. Then the Hummingbird emerged from beneath the wing, alive, trembling, radiant. And the sky understood.”

artworks.label: No. 308  —  February 9, 2024
artworks.title: Everything Is Alive!
artworks.diary: In 2016 I visited Cusco, Peru for the first time. It was the first country I visited outside of the USA. My roommate, his girlfriend, and I traveled together to this ancient city at the top of the Andes. We had no idea what we were doing or why, but we went. And it was the most precious adventure I ever had. During this time I was self-medicating with psychedelic mushrooms to heal from and make sense of my mother’s passing 2 years prior. I had an unhealthy relationship coping with this plant that was supposed to help with depression, it became the poison to my unwell mind. Art was my therapy, but the medicine was my escape. Getting out of New York City and being somewhere else was the first door that opened me up to do something new, to become better; To be well. I saw a sign that said, San Pedro. It was a big cactus that was a healing plant and grown in Peru. I said to myself, I’ve always wanted to try mescaline… I read about it in the doors of perception by Aldous Huxley and Hunter S. Thompson psychedelic escapades and scientific research. I saw the sign and did not think much of it. At the time I thought I was going to try Ayahuasca because I was currently reading books like Daniel Pinchbeck’s, Breaking Open The Head, and The Cosmic Serpent. Little did I know as I traversed up towards the Sun Gate Temple at Machu Picchu, Destiny had another message for me. A whisper of wind in my inner ear telling me as the sun shined down on my body through the mist and clouds of the ancient site. “Do not do Ayahuasca.” What was that? It sent chills down my spine. The message was clear. It was not meant for me. I arrived at the sun gate and meditated for an hour. Then I opened my eyes and everything seemed different. It was time to go back to Cusco. I was waiting at the entrance for a while and realized Brian and his girlfriend must’ve headed back to the bus. It was getting late and I was running out of time. I ran down the steps from Machu Picchu to the town below. A hike that should’ve taken 2 hours, I ran with a couple of Chileans in 45 minutes to get back to where the busses were. I would’ve been stranded! Ironically, my bus had a popped tire so they could not go anywhere for a couple hours… Wow, thank you universe! We got back to Cusco later at night and I saw that sign again. I had signed up for a San Pedro ceremony for the morning. Again, little did I know, this ceremony would change my life forever. To open my heart and mind. To find inner peace, closure, and a vision forward. I sat in a circle with twelve strangers. We set our intentions and drank a goop of aloe vera juice, it was the most purest version of the plant medicine. It has a strong and bitter taste, but over the years it started to taste good as it courses through my veins. Becoming one with the plant. They call it the grandfather, he gently holds your hand and walks you through your journey. Metaphorically speaking. It is a pleasant trip. After 2 hours and a large cup I was stunned in the sun on the ground. A white light took me into the clouds of my consciousness. I heard a voice, it was my mother. It was pure love. It was the closure I needed to let go of the cope. We talked for hours, at least it felt like that in my head. Two voices communicating. A new way forward. A smile from ear to ear as I woke up from the daydream and gently touched the Earth with my feet and toes. I could see Gaia breathing. From the grass to the mountains. Everything is alive! How can we be so blind? It is a frequency we need to tune to, or tune back into. Year after year, I visit this special place at the Temple of the Moon. To detox and purify from all the shit we take in over the year. The pain, the emotions, the toxins, the stress. To recharge and let it go again. A retreat to nature, a time for thyself to think, or not. To become a better person, and integrate that experience. Processing the lessons and feelings that I may have overlooked. San Pedro is not only my guardian spirit, he is a guide to do good in the world. I pray to always do the right thing, in the eyes of God. In the heart of the Earth; A servant of God, an angel on Earth. The time after, I drank another cup in 2018. I met my twin sister who passed in the womb as my mother had 3 miscarriages, as I was a survivor in the middle of it. She went on to have ovarian cancer. It’s all starting to make sense now. The shamans who administered the medicine were also Twins, and this was during the time I was finishing up Twin Flames. This time was another path to closure, not for my mother, but for my other half. A hole in my life I had always felt. A sort of “Phantom Twin Syndrome.” This idea when you have a prenatal connection with someone before you are even born and that connection is severed as you are shot out into the world. Where did they go, other than the spirit world where they have your back in this realm. A hole in your heart, until you discover the truth. They were always with you and still are. You carry them as an ally in another world. Where the spirit meets the earth, and somewhere in between. A butterfly, was her name. It was time. To reconnect with my twin as I was finishing Twin Flames. It is all meant to be. Making art is like a spiritual path. The artist is the vehicle for the expression, even if we yet to understand the message. Like all great art, it takes time. Even time after to process what the artistic process was about and what it was all for. A natural trust of the intuition when creating. This was the power of San Pedro, this is my Huachuma shaman, Lorenzo. Again, as I come back in 2023. Not in a sense for healing, but a sense of belonging. A coming home. I Became part of this healer family in the hills of Cusco. With friends who became a family that I’ve grown with since I first stepped foot in her Garden of Eden. Lorenzo is still among us. A person who protects and holds space in the real world and spirit world. He knows and senses what you feel, or when you need help. A character who continues to show up in my artistic practice. A way to honor his gentle soul. For all the times he had my back with his condor feather and whisk of sage. Thank you Lorenzo, Thank you San Pedro. Forever, I am GRATEFUL.

artworks.label: No. 309  —  February 10, 2024
artworks.title: The Shopkeepers
artworks.diary: Katty and Alexa were the shopkeepers at a restaurant in Aguas Calientes. My friend Charlie and I were looking for a place to have lunch as we wandered through the time in preparation for tomorrow’s hike to Machu Picchu. He and I loved playing chess so we noticed they had a chess set outfront with a couple of open seats. We decided to play chess and have our lunch here. The women were very kind and the food was out of this world. We both had the Quinoa as this is harvested in Peru. It is always better when its local and for most of the trip around the world I would only eat what the locals are having to connect and learn more about their ways of living. We played 5 games and Charlie had the upper hand. I did win a couple games but I don’t think he was paying attention since he was facing the street and I was facing him. Checkmate! A knight took his Queen and a pawn made no way for his king to escape. We continued to play and have tea at the table till nightfall. Went to bed early to wake up at 4 am to hike to the top. We were the first people at the gate to have Machu Picchu to ourselves as I had done back in 2016. I always recommend the early morning hike instead of the bus. Both up and down the mountain.

artworks.label: No. 310  —  February 11, 2024
artworks.title: From Black and White to Color
artworks.diary: At the top of Machu Picchu I met an archaeologist named Williams holding a notebook up of one of the oldest photographs of the site when it was first re-discovered by a yale professor named Hiram Bingham in the early 20th century with the help of local guides who told him of the tale of an ancient Incan city in the mountains. It was overgrown and he scorched the earth with fire to reveal what was hidden underneath; Not quite a sustainable approach. This city was populated by the Incas in the 15th Century until the conquistadors invaded their territory forcing them to retreat to a final stand in another ancient city that has not yet been rediscovered, as the tale goes on. It is impressive to fathom that this city atop the mountain was built and only lived in for approximately 100 years. The mystery goes on: Where did all these large stones come from? How were they moved? How did the Incas develop sophisticated agricultural architecture that allowed them to farm and protect their land from environmental factors like landslides and run off from the misty mornings caused by the Urubamba river. Where did all these people, their rituals, and supposedly their treasures vanish too? So many questions without answers. Perhaps the locals know, as they did before when Machu Picchu was published. Its funny how the people lived with the ruins for hundreds of years, and it took an outsider, from Yale and National Geographic to make it a global phenomenon and contemporary attraction that is now the largest ancient tourist site in South America. Another question is, how does something become ancient? How much time needs to pass? 100 years? 500 years? A century? How many generations need to pass for it to become an archeological site. When no one longer lives there? When it falls into ruins, then interest arises many, many years later? To understand what happened, and why? Will we ever know? Where were the stories written, or were they passed down in by other means? When do they become truly lost in time. A place of worship. Rituals and cosmological navigation were evident here. Mirrors to the moon and sun using water and stone during equinoxes and solstices. They measured time by following the stars. Some say this civilization vanished into the stars themselves. Just as many other conspiracies of ancient cultures disappear without a trace. All we have are the stone skeletons of their homes, temples and farms. So here we are. On top of a mountain still in tact, thanks to restorative practices. A man holding a timeless photograph of the sacred site. Fractaling from the past into the present. From black and white to color. Here and now, until the future generations to come. What will the ruins we leave behind?

artworks.label: No. 311  —  February 12, 2024
artworks.title: Year of the Horse
artworks.diary: Today is the year of the Horse.

artworks.label: No. 312  —  February 13, 2024
artworks.title: Star-Crossed Lovers
artworks.diary: Up in the Sacred Valley is a throne for a King and Queen, and in between a heart shaped rock for star crossed lovers. You don’t need to be a man to sit inside the divine feminine, nor a woman to sit inside the divine masculine. We carry both energies throughout life like a dance with destiny in harmony and equilibrium. Mark, who is one of the twin cactus shamans, has been holding space for me and tons of other visitors by the Temple of the Moon for many, many years. He is with his beloved Elizabeth who he met at the gym in the center of town in Cusco. They fell in love and are bringing the healing qualities of the cactus to the local people with her help. I visited this gym during my stay at their home and it became a daily ritual to walk from the mountain house to the town and back up the long and winding trail steadily uphill, which was pitch black at night and ridiculously steep the way we chose to go back home, Charlie and I, who had joined me in the Peruvian leg of the journey. I photographed Mark and Simon for Twin Flames back in 2018 nearing the end and this is the time after the first I drank the green cactus juice which opened my heart and soul to the spirit world for a second time. I spoke to my twin sister who was lost in the womb during my mothers miscarriage, she became a butterfly. A guardian spirit on the other side. There was a Psychic also named Elizabeth who translated and spoke through her like a channel during the peak of the experience. I roared like a lion in pain with a blockage in my back, from the pain and guilt of surviving. It was as if I had absorbed her in the womb and she clutched to my back shoulder. Once I roared my friend Lindy, who was another Shaman (Sangoma) from South Africa, helped me clear this energy blockage. By screaming louder and pounding the Earth for 30 minutes, louder and louder until I let out what felt like a black bat from my throat and evaporated into thin air. A physical manifestation of the pain was released and banished to whence it came: death. Once released, I collapsed on all fours and face first into the dirt. The process was complete, and I had felt a gutteral release. I laid there for a couple hours crying into the ground, the tears seeping under like crystal seeds pouring back into the Earth. There was peace, there was no more pain. Then, I got up. Feeling grounded and inspired. Mark and Simon and I went to the front of their Casa with totem poles of San Pedro standing guard on each side like a green tree climbing to heaven. Mark was holding the thick cactus awaiting to be cut, boiled, and juiced for the next guests. This was the photograph I had imagined for months before I came to visit. It was the only Twin Flames image I had been thinking about how I would like to photograph them. The image was crystal clear in my consciousness, where as nearly all of my other portraits were shot in the moment, improvised and authentic to the light, models, and presence. They are my brothers; The family I chose up in the Andes. So here we are in 2023. Mark and his new girlfriend Elizabeth, “Twin Flames” and a lot to learn from one another. Instead of shooting Mark with his Twin, Simon. We seeked the depth of their life beyond the twindom and created a moment for their personality and lifestyle to shine through. Mark is in love, and we wanted to honor that since Valentine’s day was a day away. Later on in the project I photograph Simon by himself with a pack of Gorillas in Uganda. Sometimes twins live their own life, even though they may sometimes be together and finish their sentences. They are their own person, where their life choices make them unique. We end with a subtle kiss. Mark and Elizabeth, sitting rightfully at their throne. Coming together in the heart shaped rock at the Temple of The Moon.

artworks.label: No. 313  —  February 14, 2024
artworks.title: Two Hands Touching
artworks.diary: A new love is born From family and friendship A force that gave life to the universe An infinite energy source From within the depths of the heart To the glowing heart of the milky way A fire in the night sky Exploding suns Color thy soul Atop the mountain Back towards the Temple of the Moon Two hands touching Seeking truth Feeling connection From family and friendship to freedom Love is the way

artworks.label: No. 314  —  February 15, 2024
artworks.title: Birthplace of the Sun
artworks.diary: There are floating man made islands at Lake Titicaca. and Taquile Island is one of the natural islands in the middle of the lake. The group landed ashore and walked through the island to the other side where I collected sand to represent South America. There is a rich Inca mythology that was said “the lake was portrayed as the birthplace of the sun. The Incan sun god Inti emerged from its depths, bringing light into the world.” We made our way to meet the Uru people. I met the family living on this island and when my group boarded the ferry. I asked to make a family portrait of them where I gifted them a Polaroid and bought some of their baskets and other goods they made. They took us around on their handmade boat to get a feel for how they fish and travel. “The Uru considered themselves the owners of the lake and water. The Uru use bundles of dried Totora reeds to make reed boats (balsas), and to make the islands themselves. The islets are made of multiple natural layers harvested in Lake Titicaca. The base is made of large pallets of floating totora roots, which are tied together with ropes and covered in multiple layers of totora reeds. These dense roots that the plants develop and interweave form a natural layer called khili (about one to two meters thick), which are the main flotation and stability devices of the islands. Each island lasts about 25 years. After 25 years, water seeps through the reeds and the inhabitants build a new island and let the old one sink to the bottom of the lake. The Uru do not reject modern technology: most boats have motors, nearly all islands have shared solar panels to run appliances such as televisions, and the main island is home to an Uru-run FM radio station, which plays music for several hours a day.”

artworks.label: No. 315  —  February 16, 2024
artworks.title: The Key to the Gates of Heaven
artworks.diary: We find ourselves in the Garden of Eden of “The World” a mystical woman who we call Lesley. A healer by trade. She holds the key to the gates of heaven, the sacred cactus of San Pedro. Lesley holds space for hundreds if not thousands of people a year to assist them in their healing journey. An angelic woman who has dedicated her life to the light, and to help bring people into their own. Find their way to a higher self. Letting go of past mistakes or regret, coming to terms with deep physical or emotional trauma, in some cases healing cancer and paralysis from strokes. The medicine moves blockages in the mind and body. We deserve to be set free from what holds us back. As we hold ourselves back. Sometimes with fear, sometimes with pain. The medicine allows us to bring them up to the surface to face without repressing or hiding. To reveal it in the light, to expose the deep wounded truth will inevitably heal it. Grandfather gently holds our hand and walks us through the garden of our hopes and dreams. He helps show us the way when there are too many choices or not enough direction. The truth lives inside of us, and we are shown what to do. How to pursue our purpose on this Earth, in this lifetime. To give back to the life we were given. To heal the world, by healing ourselves first.

artworks.label: No. 316  —  February 17, 2024
artworks.title: Rainbow Mountain
artworks.diary: There is a mountain in Peru that is as colorful as a rainbow. With seven colors layered on top of each other, which are caused by its mineralogical composition. “The seven colors of the mountain are due to its mineralogical composition: the pink colour is due to red clay, mud, and sand; the whitish colouring is due to quartzose, sandstone, and marls, rich in calcium carbonate; the red is due to claystones (iron) and clays belonging to the Upper Tertiary period; the green is due to phyllites and clays rich in ferromagnesian; the earthy brown is a product of fanglomerate composed of rock with magnesium belonging to the Quaternary period; and the mustard yellow colour comes from the calcareous sandstones rich in sulphurous minerals.The mountain used to be covered by glacier caps, but these melted in 2013.” The first time I ever visited Rainbow mountain in 2018 it was covered in snow with patches of colors visible. It was a beautiful contrast. This time in 2024, I was able to see all of the colors! It was a harder hike this time around, as I was not chewing on coca leaves and charcoal that makes your steps faster and heart beating rapidly like it wants to dance out of your chest. This time was calm, cool, and slower. We arrived at a time that all the tourists had left and it was just Charlie, me, and our guide. Once we made it to the top we met an Alpaca wearing sunglasses and people selling giant ears of inca corn on the cob, a nice snack at this altitude. We sat on top of the highest point to make art. Pictures, portraits, and videos. As I had done in the past when this place was snow white. There is something about coming to a place more than once, especially on a nature hike like this one. How the world changes, how we change, how the landscape changes colors like leaves on the tree over the seasons. It is as if no moment is the same, even if you go over and over to the same place. We are different, the air is different, the clouds and sky and temperature. Always in flux. Change is the common denominator to experience. Change creates memory. We hold on to change with photography and video. A piece of existence lives forever like a time capsule. The present never existed until the shutter creates the proof. The flow of time ceases and the present instantly becomes passed. Rainbow mountain is a phenomenal phenomenon, there is only a few places in the world just like it. Layers of sand, layers of color. Nature is an artist herself.

artworks.label: No. 317  —  February 18, 2024
artworks.title: Be Here Now
artworks.diary: Remember to close your eyes. Take a deep breath in. Come back to your awareness in the eternal present. Long exhale out. Don’t attach to your thoughts, let them pass like clouds in the sky. If you find your mind straying. Gently remind yourself to breathe again. To be one with the mind, body, and spirit. To be at peace, inside and out. To come back to the infinite source of love within, to “Be Here Now.”

artworks.label: No. 318  —  February 19, 2024
artworks.title: Soul Mates
artworks.diary: From twin flames to soul mates <3

artworks.label: No. 319  —  February 20, 2024
artworks.title: From One Fruit You Can Plant a Hundred Trees
artworks.diary: We left the mountains of the Andes to make our way to the rainforest at the bottom of the mountain. Landed from a small propeller plane to Puerto Maldonado at the edges of the Amazon Jungle. It was hot and humid. The group and crew boarded a bus to the water from the inner city, then onto a boat to cruise to the lodge deeper in the jungle. The water was rising and rushing as it had been raining all week. You could see trees floating in the river flow. We stepped onto the shore and made our way into the lodge. There was a spider monkey named Jennifer who grabbed my hand and led me around the grounds. She was sweet and kind and when I laid on the bench she laid on top of me like a cat would with her tail curled up on my chest. Our host took us out to a nature walk after breakfast with his machete to pave the way. He pointed out yellow fruits in the trees that he chopped down and cracked open. We ate some and it tasted like candy. It was nature’s treat. It was raw cacao! This is the fruit that chocolate was made from. As we walked through the jungle we collected more cacao and threw the seeds around the forest to lay down new trees. From one fruit you can plant a hundred trees. Nature is abundant, it’s literally programmed into the system where 1 equals 100, all it takes is time for it to grow. These trees grow fast! And even faster under these environmental conditions. The jungle grows in all directions, and if you are not careful it will swallow you up! We walked past caiman, which are like crocodiles. Howling monkeys in the trees. All sorts of spiders and insects. Panthers hiding in the greens. Snakes and anacondas slithering nearby. Life is all around us. Even Ayahuasca growing freely. Nature has her rhythm and systems and its up to us humans to tune back in to whence we came.

artworks.label: No. 320  —  February 21, 2024
artworks.title: Extreme Fear and Extreme Bliss
artworks.diary: The canopy of the jungle was dripping wet. Every step through the forest was damp and squishy. As we walked through on our morning hike it felt like the rain forest was cleansing my body and mind. I welcomed the droplets of water all over my skin. Equipped in a soccer jersey and big muddy boots I felt alive and refreshed. Hydrated by the atmospheric breeze. We climbed trees to knock down more cacao for the walk. The sweet jungle treat. There was a swamp building from the rainfall. The light was pouring through so I asked the guide if we could make his portrait there. He said, “in there?” And I said “yes why not?!” He laughed, and said “okay and be careful.” Be careful of what? I thought. The caiman are always prowling in the water when you least expect it. Perhaps that’s what he meant. We dredged into the swampy lagoon and started rolling. I felt something was off when we finished. And then I felt something crash against my leg under the water! Holy fuck, it seemed to be a giant snake. Was this the anaconda he was telling us about earlier?! I jetted out of the water and he was laughing. I felt a snake brush up against my leg, traverse the underworld. A brief encounter with the slithering DNA strands of mother Earths lungs. We quickly made our way to a canoe that was waiting for us. Flipped it over and hopped in. The jungle was flooded and we were riding the waves, literally. We paddled and paddled for a while. Saw a few caimans eyes blinking as we passed them by. Man they are silent and slow. But really they are motionless and waiting, their trick is to be so still you forget they are even there. So when you least expect it, or forget it. They strike with their lunging force and sharp teeth. We canoed along and found a good rhythm in the flow of the river. We popped out into a nesting ground. This was the most beautiful moment I’ve ever witnessed in nature. There were thousands of blue herons feeding their newborn birds that had just hatched. It was quite marvelous. I was brought to tears. You can see blue wings flapping amongst the greenery. Squawking and chirping by the adult and baby cranes. Birds flying past your head every few minutes. It was glorious. We circled the nest a few times just to catch a glimpse of their beautiful existence. All felt so pure until you realize what lurks beneath the trees. The caiman wait for baby birds to fall into the water because they don’t know how to fly yet. Ready to catch a meal. Always waiting, always patient. The cycle of life begins and ends in the nesting grounds that become the feeding grounds. Yet it is all in perfect harmony as nature intended. All forms of life serves its purpose here in the jungle, even in death, breeds more life. The Amazon jungle is the source of abundance. Fresh air for the entire planet, food for all the critters and creatures that roam the trees freely, and water to restore and regenerate the Earth and its inhabitants. Two sets of emotions set in on this day, extreme fear and extreme bliss. Oh, how the forces push and pull us closer to our home; The ground below and the sky above.

artworks.label: No. 321  —  February 22, 2024
artworks.title: The Life Blood of the Amazon
artworks.diary: Water is the life blood of the Amazon. The waterways are the roads to get around. The boats are the cars in traffic crossing from cities to villages and back again. It is the quickest way through, yet they are always changing, always bending upon new floods and droughts. Adaption to the ever shifting landscape. Even the roads break down with landslides. The jungle eats everything. You will see trees break from the forest and float up and down the river. Panthers swimming across with their cubs, caiman hunting for their next meal. Monkeys drown and fish are caught. Families swim for fun and bathe for health. The sacred river provides everything you need. Food and water. And the trees for shelter. Basic human needs. We row in the boats or flow with the motors and engines back home. Back to the buses to take us to the planes. To fly to another place. In this case, Colombia. Where the journey takes me to the beaches of Cartagena.

artworks.label: No. 322  —  February 23, 2024
artworks.title: The Ocean’s Kiss
artworks.diary: Once landed in Colombia I took a 2 hour cab ride to a part of Cartagena that was outside the old city. I had no idea where I was going or what I was doing. But I had a trusted taxi driver thanks to my friend Ana. He took great care of me and barely spoke English. I was in Colombia for one day before heading off to Jamaica so had some time to rest on the breezy beach and enjoy the sunshine reflecting on the ocean. Idanys was working at breakfast time and her smile and bright yellow dress caught my eye. I knew deep down this was the person I had to photograph, but she was on the clock. She also did not speak english so her co-worker translated for us. Luckily, it was about to be her break in an hour so I drank a few more glasses of passion fruit juice and waited for the window of opportunity to make art with her. She walked me over to a quiet part on the beach and pointed towards the water. She walked in calmly and smiley. Held her dress and was dancing in the water for the duration of the shoot. She stood with such poise and dignity. The sun shined on her so perfectly. Everything about this moment was in harmony with nature and what felt like the universe. The broken waves even posed for us. We wrapped up the shoot after making a few portraits on my Rollie-flex while we were out here. I walked her back to the kitchen and said farewell. I packed up my camera and went back to the beach to swim and meditate on the sands. Napped in a hammock and read a book. I was alone for the first time in months. On a beach in Colombia. It was me and the sound of the waves. Mental clarity. 12 hours of freedom until the clock struck midnight. Until the new day began and groundhog day commenced. To find another person somewhere else in the world to make art with. Once the shutter clicks and the portrait is made the stress fades away. A sense of survival meets completion. Every single day. A part of my brain smooths out like kneaded dough when the work is completed. As if I can finally relax or take a deep breath. The shutter is the transition of emotions; a physical processing to the computational mind. Where the stress leaves and the mind become at ease. Just for a little while. Like sitting on the beach watching the waves gently hugging your toes before pulling back to the sea. The oceans kiss. Art is a similar feeling for the heart and mind. Transforming a thought into feeling. When finding someone to make their portrait is half the process, and seeing them to convey them is the other. Endurance and Creativity. Like a knight with his sword and shield. Or a magician with her staff and cloak.

artworks.label: No. 323  —  February 24, 2024
artworks.title: Soursop, Sweetsop, Breadfruit
artworks.diary: After Lee and I landed in Jamaica. We were riding on the freeway to meet with Chris Blackwell at his James Bond hotel. Our drive Chris ripped by on the highway and I noticed a fruit stand on the side of the road. A bag of jackfruits caught my eye, and Ackee for Lee. We asked Chris to turn around and he drifted into the lane to head back to the stop for some fruits and coconuts. The woman managing the fruit stand name is Tass. We bought up all her fruit! A laundry list of Soursop, Sweetsop, Breadfruit, Jackfruit, Pineapple, Ackee, Mangoes and Guavas too. Enough to last us the few days we were visiting the island. We thrived on fruit and Ital food. We stuffed the trunk with all the fruits and carried on to our beach bungalows. The first night we were here there was a reggae concert and drum circle. A bright yellow harvest moon illuminated the night sky, the giant fire glowing on the Earth. People dancing and singing around the fire. It was a special and soulful punky Reggae party. The music and the fire connected us deeply. Without any words shared, just the sounds of the waves crashing, the fire crackling, the crickets clicking, the people laughing and humming, while the drums beating. My soul starved for this connection; The music was working, it was healing. It was dinner time and we all sat at a table with the legend himself, the man who made this place and Island Records. Bob Marley’s record label and friend. It was an iconic night and made me feel closer to the music I grew up listening to. Bob’s songs always felt righteous and biblical. Real and human. A man of the people that brought people together through his music.

artworks.label: No. 325  —  February 26, 2024
artworks.title: Rastaman Vibration
artworks.diary: Right up the street from Bob’s home on Hope road. Lee introduced me to Bob’s cousin, Sledger. They were family. Lee spent his time on the island with the cousins making photos and music when Bob was becoming a reggae sensation. Sledger would drive them around from home to the recording studio. When I met Sledger, he would bring you in real close and hold you for a while. You can feel the Rastaman vibration coursing through his fingers and body as he hugged you. It was a whole lotta “One Love.” We pulled into Bob’s old home, which is now a museum. But did not go inside. We went over to Sledgers nephew Craigs shop and green house next door. Sledger was telling us stories about Bob, and Lee would reminisce of stories about Sledger when they were younger. I felt like I was living a in a dream. Parts of the life my musical idol, Bob Marley, had lived. His music touched my soul growing up. It helped me heal when my mom had cancer. It felt like Bobs soul, words, and energy was there for me. Like I could get through the difficult times with his music. It was soulful sounds and melodies. His music would always cheer me up. Especially, when we were smoking fat spliffs singing along to Three Little Birds and Natural Mystic. Lee told me one of Bob’s songs was about him, it was “Talkin Blues.” While I was in College, I took a course called Songs of Change. It redefined how I would “listen” and interpret music. It wasn’t just fun and games passively filling the auditory space, it was meaningful stories and symbols of connection to what was being said and how I was hearing it. It changed the way how I understand music, specifically “protest songs.” Like Woodie Guthrie folk music and 2Pac’s Changes. There were layers of depth into what they were singing for, not about. A movement in the times to change working conditions or racial prejudice. When we had to write about a song, I chose “War.” Bob Marley adapted a speech by Haile Selassie. Everytime I heard this song I would feel something deeply. It was not until I read the lyrics did I understand what this was about. Equality. Seeing each other as human. This verse struck a chord in my heart. “That until there are no longer First-class and second-class citizens of any nation Until the colour of a man’s skin Is of no more significance than the colour of his eyes Me say war” It really makes you think what the world is fighting over. We see racism and how people are treated with which religion they practice and the color of people’s skin even in America. This “otherness” or “belief systems” is what the crusades were fought over in ancient times, and the civil rights movement in the 60’s were trying to abolish in modern times. And as Bob and Haile said, “Until the colour of a man’s skin Is of no more significance than the colour of his eyes.” I have faith in humanity. We will see the day where we recognize that we are all just humans and when we can work together, we can traverse the stars than continue fighting on this Earth. That is the only way to evolve. We fought each other for so long, it’s time to come together and cooperate and do more. Society and future generations deserve better. We can go further, when we come together. True singularity is not Artificial intelligence, it is humans uniting as one, Just as ants and bees in harmony with nature and their communities. We too will overcome!

artworks.label: No. 326  —  February 27, 2024
artworks.title: Tivoli Gardens
artworks.diary: Lee and I were invited with a museum curator in Kingston to visit the garrison of Tivoli Gardens. Marlon greeted us with a warm smile. The kids who were playing football came up to us to say hello and hang out. Marlon was giving us a tour of all the murals he created and curated in the neighborhood to uplift his community. Years ago there was a terrible tragedy that brought turmoil to the people of Tivoli Gardens. Now, they have been rebuilding together. Art was the spirit of renewal. Regenerating the garden with creativity. And, it was working. He and fellow artists came together to paint beautiful images and encouraging words across the rows of building in the town square. He created a movement. Bringing artists from all over the world to paint and bring a renewed sense of life to the Gardens again. Giving back to the place he comes from. He brings people like Lee and I to his home to teach us what happened, and what he is doing. After the art walk I was so touched by his work that I donated $1000 to support the cause and bring more art to the people. Every dollar goes a long way. I understand the struggle of being an artist and raising funds to make more art. It is the hardest thing in the world, because there is no financial return, just a spiritual good. Which at the end of the day, I believe brings more abundance. When you give to a great cause, more joy, more love, more life comes from it. Marlon and his artists friends were thrilled by our givings. He can now work on the next mural! That is what it’s all about. That is why we are here. To do good, to learn and grow together. Art will always lead the way to truth, freedom, and expression. It is the soul of humanity, it is what makes us human. It is how we connect to one another. Through stories and ideas; communication. Marlon sat us down and fed us home mad Ital food by the don himself. He blessed me with a crystal necklace to remember this day. He blessed me with his presence to represent his neighborhood and artwork in this beautiful project. The embodiment of the regeneration of Tivoli Gardens. The center of the art world in Jamaica!

artworks.label: No. 327  —  February 28, 2024
artworks.title: Climbing Trees
artworks.diary: The beauty of meeting artists online is that you can always have a friend everywhere you go. This project proved to me that no matter where I went, there is someone willing to meet and show me their city. Even if we both don’t speak the same language. And in some cases, there were language barriers. But the art brought us together, and we live in a time where technology can translate with near to no delay. In fact, the tech is what allows us to connect deeper. Because we can understand each other a lot easier than waving our hands with gestures and pretending what the other person is talking about in their native tongue. We have the tools to communicate and there is no excuse. At the end of the day we are all communicating the same things. What to have for dinner, how we feel today, what happened at work. Every day life is common all around the world. We all face the same things, just in different languages. Ironically, it feels as if we reached the point in evolution where if you refer to the Bible, there was a story about the tower of Babel which humans were trying to reach the heaven. Everyone spoke the same language and can understand each other. Then we were all separated around the world to create new forms of communication and dialects. We are at the point where we have regained a collective consciousness. Though we are not reaching heaven, in a way we are trying to become god through the tools we built for a heaven on Earth! We can now talk to anyone in the world in any language with our phones, or even Artificial intelligence as the interpreter. We are all connected more than ever, not just with online but with how we can talk to each other. We can progress to live in the Age of Cooperation because we can communicate clear our intentions and ideas without delay of learning each other’s language. We can find common ground as we share common experiences. I met with Petra in the beautiful park of Chapultepec. He does not speak English and my Spanish is alright. We hung out for hours walking through the park, climbing trees and making art! We understood each other. Art was our native language, a dance. We took turns speaking into the phone to listen to one another. When you think technology takes you away from the moment or creates a medium between you and the world, it actually did the opposite. It grounded me in the present moment, to listen carefully and connected us deeper to what was happening. It created empathy because we were able to understand one another. We were able to open up. We live in an age of information and intelligence. So let’s use it wisely and connect with each other and the world around us more and more!

artworks.label: No. 328  —  February 29, 2024
artworks.title: Leap Year
artworks.diary: Every four years there is a leap year. An extra day in the shortest month of the year. February flies by quicker than the rest. When I started, Every Day is a Gift, a project where I found someone on their birthday every day without missing a day, I made a polaroid portrait. There was one day that had escaped me. Even though I started in 2012, which was already a leap year, I started the project in September. I finished the project in September 2013 to finish the year long work. I promised myself that one day I will fulfill the prophecy and make a portrait of someone on their birthday on the leap year. My best friend from high school was a kid named Matthew Haley. His birthday was on leap year and the only person I ever met with that date. Technically, he was 4 years old when he passed away. It was the most traumatic experience for me in tenth grade.
