I was with him one minute hanging out skateboarding, then later that day he was struck by a car. He died a week later. Leap year reminds me of Matthew. So, in a way this was not just for me to fulfill an invisible date for the project. It was to honor my friend who has long passed, that I dearly keep in my heart. Matthew taught me how to play music, to be kind, to be gracious, to be grateful, to have fun! He was a good friend. This portrait is for my buddy Matthew. And, to fulfill a project I started more then ten years ago. The birthday project is complete, in the Moments of the Unknown. Where two projects cross over and can connect over a decade. Stories intertwined, memory and meaning come together. Celebration of life, because truly, Every Day is a Gift on this Earth.

artworks.label: No. 329  —  March 1, 2024
artworks.title: Clap for the Gods and Goddesses
artworks.diary: Almost a year prior to this portrait I visited Teotihuacan for the first time in February 2023. Only this time we journeyed at sunrise to the pyramids. It was my first time ever in a hot air balloon and I was terrified of heights. The fire and gas made the giant balloon fill up and rise like the morning sun. This was the year I decided to embrace all fears. From Ayahuasca to heights in the span of 6 months. Courage guides my heart. We live this life to let go of what we are most afraid of because that is where all our healing is ironically. I reluctantly got in the basket. And we started to lift quietly and suddenly! It was surreal. I was freaking out and clutching the sides of the basket we are elevating in. Its an odd experience because you are standing still but the perspective is shifting drastically, it feels like you are hallucinating. For the first 15 minutes I was physically feeling the fear move through my body. There was a moment I decided to breathe and exhale. My friends who were with me, who was also in this portrait, said they saw a dark energy come out of my head and into the flame. It was fear itself being extinguished. The fear was removed like a shamanic exorcism. A past life fear no more. I was blinded by fright, but now as I look out in the horizon you see pure beauty in the skies. The colors, the pyramids beneath, the other balloons gleefully floating along the same path. We went even higher and my smile got even bigger. You simply need to endure the thing you are afraid to have exposure to it because you mind makes up stories and your body is adapting. Then you can really enjoy the moment and how glorious this experience is. And then it was over! I was proud of myself for doing this thing and it set me off to do more scary things. To live deeply and not be afraid of anything anymore. So we returned to the pyramids. With a new friend and to revisit the chef again. Walking through complete darkness like a snake as we held hands and crouched in the caves below to do a sacred ritual with smudging and corn to honor the ancestors of the lands we walk upon. To honor the history of this archeological site. To give respect. To clap for the gods and goddesses that make the chirping sound of the “feathered serpent” called, Quetzalcoatl.

artworks.label: No. 330  —  March 2, 2024
artworks.title: Peace on Earth
artworks.diary: From Mexico City to Los Angeles. I picked up a rental car and drove down to Torrance to pick up Tony. Tony and I had this plan tripped for months and today was the day! The vision was to ride down to the US and Mexican border to make a portrait connecting two people holding hands across the line. We came with an idea, and left with a pleasant surprise. On the way down to San Diego, Tony was telling me stories about the hills we were seeing. They were part of a large military base that spans for miles and he was sharing about his past in the service. The first time we ever met he was sharing about the nonprofit he worked on to help aid immigrants who were crossing the border and that stayed with me ever since, as I appreciate nonprofit work and the passion that goes into it to help people if you can. After a few hours and many stories by Tony we made it to a small town right at the border. We were searching for an opening, but there was no hope in sight. Only a bronze wall with barbed wire and vans securing the area. We drove around to find an opening but there was nothing. I felt defeated at first. Then we stopped at a small fruit stall and Tony asked the woman cutting the mangos with Tajin and squeezing the watermelon with lime. She suggested we go a few miles to the border center and try our luck there. We were following the signs, quite literally, where to flow on next and to make this portrait that we dreamed up. We parked the car, I pulled out my cameras and we sat in a coffee shop to strategize our next moves. We were right next to where people were walking in and out of the border. Then we heard sirens and noticed a parade of people with Palestinian flags and posters. There was a Gaza protest happening at the US / Mexican border. We walked over to check it out and followed the protestors. It felt quite significant that there was a protest like this at the border, because this is what was happening in the Middle East. Boundaries being crossed and borders in fraught. Even though we did not photograph people holding hands across the border, this protest felt meaningful to witness like this was the image we were supposed to make. It was real, and it was happening before our eyes. We followed the protest and heard their cries. People were angry and wanted justice for the innocent. There was a moment when we reached the border and the group started speaking in a loudspeaker with speeches. I noticed the flags blowing in the wind that were on the poles of the buildings. America, and Mexican. And here are people waving Palestinian flags and all they want is Peace in the Middle East. That is all we ever wanted; Peace on Earth. Where no one is killed in cold blood and people can live their lives freely without causing harm to anyone or being harmed by anyone. To love our friends and families. To make an honest living. To do our best to make this world a better place than we were born in it. I guess that’s the dream for a dreamer. Like the great Imagine a world where there is no borders, where would we be? Like the great John Lennon sang in his songs, “Imagine there’s no countries It isn’t hard to do Nothing to kill or die for And no religion too Imagine all the people Living life in peace”

artworks.label: No. 331  —  March 3, 2024
artworks.title: Footprints Write Short Stories in Sand
artworks.diary: Footprints write short stories in sand. By noon they’re gone. loving too fast, dreams too big. Santa Monica begins in light. Not the loud, burning blaze of the afternoon but that soft and misty marine layer glow, like a quiet secret waiting to be told. The pier hovers over the waves as if it’s asking the ocean a question. Ferris wheel turning slow with a handful of tourists and lovers, the neon lights shining against salt air, laughter riding through the wind watching the gulls stealing fries and bread bowls There’s an order here. Bike paths flow like measured lines. Joggers chasing better versions of themselves. Yoga mats unrolling at sunrise Silent discos raving on the shore Sunglasses hide both fame and failure. And yet, throughout it all, the same restless water that touches Venice touches here too. When the sun drops, the sky dissolves. Pink becomes gold, gold fades black. Like breath after noise. by sea wind and long afternoons. the Pacific keeps whispering the same thing it has always said: Keep going.

artworks.label: No. 332  —  March 4, 2024
artworks.title: Wisdom Tree
artworks.diary: A hike to Wisdom Tree. You can spot this tree on the hill driving on the 101 highway just as you pass Hollywood into Burbank. A sacred place to me in Los Angeles. One of my favorite hikes and places to go to watch the sunset other than by Venice beach off Rose Ave. The first time I ever came to this place was after a San Pedro ceremony with a group of friends who were local to Toluca Lake. It was past midnight and we hiked up the hill in the dark and had a few microdoses. It felt like there was an intergalactic war going inside my body by crossing the spirits, something I learned was a bad idea and it showed me intense fear and how to face it. We made it to the top and there was an astrophotographer there tripping on LSD. A band of freaks and misfits meditating till sunrise and the moon set. This was the first time I ever felt the middle was being on Earth. I looked to my right and saw the sun, and I looked to my left and saw the moon, perfectly aligned on different sides of the sky. And here we are on Earth, with the only tree that survived the fires, right up at wisdom tree. I guess that’s why it’s called that, a survivor. After that trip, I come back during the day and hike this place every visit. And when I lived there at least once a month, and every time I learn something new. Its my favorite place to be in LA. A 360 degree view of the entire city, and you can even see as far as the ocean horizon! Wisdom tree is a place I return to quite often in my art projects. It was first shown in Twin Flames with a set of twins named, Lina and Erica, who I had met just before we started the hike. There was a lot of trust there. Second time was to photograph Tara, the Four of Cups, for Smoke and Mirrors. Part of me felt bad we had to hike to make the portrait, and the other half felt it was the perfect place as I knew she liked nature and have not been before. I met Tara at the San Pedro ceremony from the first time I ever visited Wisdom Tree so it felt like a full circle closed loop. Now, here we are with Maria, who is also a twin, for the third and definitely not final time making art here! The day after this portrait I met her sister Xenia in Canada to make the twin connection span between countries. We hiked to the top and sat for a while watching the sun set. A perfect way to say goodbye to the city I used to call home. Wisdom Tree my old friend, until I see you again.

artworks.label: No. 333  —  March 5, 2024
artworks.title: A Mother and Her Son
artworks.diary: From Wisdom Tree to Vancouver to meet Maria’s identical twin sister, Xenia. I flew and was racing against the sun set trying to flow through customs until I was tapped on the shoulder by a border agent and asked to follow him behind the security checkpoint. I was confused and anxious as I was going to be late for the photoshoot in the park to match her twin sister at sunset. The officer held me there for an hour. Checking all of my luggage and opening all of my film canisters. He thought I was smuggled drugs, into a city that is known for its legalized flexibilities on drug use. I was outraged and confused on why he had profiled me. Was it my beard? Was it my tattoos? He looked just like me with beard and tattoos. Maybe he was me in another life on the side of the law. He did not say why he held me, but it was obviously mistaken identity for a drug bust of some sort. I was so angry because this unnecessary search made me late for the very reason I traveled here was to make a portrait. It is safe to say that he found nothing incriminating because I do not travel with drugs or do drugs anywhere. Cleaner than bleached laundry. What gets me high these days is making art, which this man made me late for. I played it cool and hurried along to my car and to Xenia’s home as she and her son were waiting for me. The light had gone to dark and she invited me upstairs to the playpen of her home. She served me tea and we sat for a while talking and thinking how to shoot. So her son picked up lights and started dressing his mom with it playfully and this was a precious moment to record, and so I did. A mother and her son. You can see the love in her eyes and the joy in his face. We had wrapped up the shoot and she walked me downstairs, in the elevator I had some film left and saw the reflections and thought to myself, this would be a great homage to her sister as a symbolic gesture of the mirrored duality. And so I shot until we made it to the first floor in this tight elevator. We stopped on two floors on the way down people entering and exiting, carefully sidestepping me as I recorded. We made it to the lobby and my film had finished and I felt we had made something special. The bond of a mother and her son. The connection between twins from across two countries. One twin standing on top of a mountain in her sovereignty, the other holding down the fortress for her new family. The inside and outside of the world be two people who look exactly the same, though their lives are completely different. Nature has a divine plan from the beginning, and the way we are nurtured conditions us how to live tomorrow.

artworks.label: No. 334  —  March 6, 2024
artworks.title: The Shutter Clicks on Both Ends
artworks.diary: Sean and I had met for breakfast at this hippie joint near his house. It was a tasty vegan spot. We rolled over to pick up another punk before heading to the nature park to find a place to photograph. There were a few spots we found like an abandoned zoo. Sean wanted to jump in for a sweet shot, but there was no way out. He would’ve been on view for the bystanders. We passed by some graffiti and rolled on to another spot. This time in the parking lot, with a tree his wife once did research on! She studied all the trees in this forest. Still did not feel like it was the right light to shoot the video, so we made his polaroid there instead to honor his loving wife and her work. On the way towards the Lions bridge we saw large totem poles installed throughout the park. We hopped in the car and made a wrong turn, twice, trying to park next to the walkway to the view of the bridge. It was a cloudy day so the light was scarce. There was a gap in the sky and the sun shined through as I had pointed my camera at Sean, and he pointed back at me. The way photographers communicate with one another, is how we see each other. The shutter clicks on both ends. Friendship is in the eye of the beholder, and it helps when you have a leica camera, and the other a Super 8. Same location, same moment, different perception and perspectives. Sean with his black and white vision, and myself with a colorful view on the world. Come together like photons meeting from particles into waves. A mirrored reality through the lens. To see one another, as we see ourselves in the reflection of the lens. Somewhere in Canada at the Lions gate bridge, Sean and I became friends. For the love of photography and crypto punks. The art is what connects us!

artworks.label: No. 335  —  March 7, 2024
artworks.title: Through the Looking Glass
artworks.diary: We return to the beginning, from whence it all came. The camera, a vision that took us on a journey like an alchemist around the world. Through the looking glass we followed the white rabbit, like Alice in her wonderland. Sprouting up in different countries like giant mushrooms across the Earth. Calmly cruising like a Cheshire cat smiling into the night. A gift to my Twin Flames, the camera that made it all. There is no artwork without its audiences and those that find their way. To feel what you had feel, to connect on deeper planes. The art becomes the fraternity. A brotherhood of man. To reach towards the stars and beyond lays our fate. To travel a million miles away from home, only to yearn to be on her land. What exists out there beyond what we know, and who we are, why we are from? Curiosity than contentment fuels the ego, fuels the soul; For knowing. The fundamentals and fabric of existence itself. A cosmological consciousness from where we were breathed into a glittery existence scattered across millions of galaxies like pixie dust sprinkled past black holes. The fire of wisdom burns deep in our souls. We wonder, we want to know, the architecture of the universe. Are we part of it or is it a part of us? Or both. Yet we evolve, by understanding that we know nothing at all. We have our tools and cameras. Our families and friendships. What gives us meaning is that curiosity and deep connection to life itself. Even if we will never understand why we are here. We just are. And maybe that’s all there is, so we can find joy in the nothing, to be ourselves. Art takes us home. No matter how far from her we go. Just like Alice, we find our way back. Following the white rabbit from the portal we slipped through space and time. A full circle with a friend who is now part of the journey. From witnessing it through portraits, to becoming a portrait in the place that it all began. Something new is born. A narrative, a story, lore that can keep building. When you revisit a place as you grow or life changes. With friends or by yourself, it will never be the same. Because the moment only happens once. Even when you are still.

artworks.label: No. 336  —  March 8, 2024
artworks.title: In Front of Giants
artworks.diary: It takes courage to be the one to stand up, against all odds, against the powers at be, against the control of illusion that exist. All that’s needed to start a revolution is a spark of rebellion, and an ember of truth. A chain reaction suddenly forms in places that were too comfortable to sit in. Too narrow in life outside of the system. A voice, so strong, yet gentle. Standing out in front of giants at their doorstep. With nothing but their strength at their hip. A young girl can make a difference. When her enemy is the bull that ravages the town with greed. She rises up to the occasion to stop the beast in its cold red sight. She is standing firm as he cracks the ground with his feet. Unwavered and unmoved by the steam from his nose and the clapping of his hoof. Facing your fear, facing the danger head on, is the metaphor. As we all have that strong inner child within us, that voice of innocence that still guides our heart. The fear is in the mind that tells us to stop, move, and give up. But that voice of strength echos deeply from the source of consciousness itself to remind ourselves, that everything will be okay. To fight what you believe is right. To stand up to all evil doers knowing that mom, and god, has our back. We are never alone when fighting for what is the greater good for mankind. The recipe for starting the revolution is a dream and a letting go of the fear, as they are part of the same emotion. Not holding back, only moving forward. Towards purpose; Towards freedom. Together, we move to create the movement. For things will be better now, once we make the choice to change. To stand up for what you believe in, to be the change you want to see.

artworks.label: No. 337  —  March 9, 2024
artworks.title: Where Two Myths Meet
artworks.diary: There are winged watchers among us flapping above like the white doves in central park. Carrying an olive branch. Nested by the bronze angel statue guarding the water where the lovers row their boats; Where the cherubs are beneath her representing temperance, purity, health, and peace. Natures romance breathes as the sun sets in the dark park. A fog settles into the grain. We read the name of the angel who protects the healing waters. The Disciple John. He prays, “Now there is at Jerusalem by the sheep market a pool, which is called Bethesda… whoever then first after the troubling of the waters stepped in was made whole of whatsoever disease he had.” Outdoors turn to indoors, from public art statues to private paintings at the Metropolitan. An aristocratic maze of ancient to renaissance to contemporary consciousness from the golden age till the now. Pillars of civilization from Syria, Egypt, Greece, the East, and Africa. From the Temple of Dundars stone halls to the 19th century wooden walls. Paintings come alive with the right light, perspective, and frame of mind. Each thought is a breath of the life in the images world to tell a story. To what we see and how we feel; Interpretation. Filming the in between place where two myths meet; “Venus hovers somewhere between an ancient deity and a modern dream.”

artworks.label: No. 338  —  March 10, 2024
artworks.title: Bowery and Houston
artworks.diary: At the intersection of Bowery and Houston St there is a wall always consumed by Street Art. It is an institution for graffiti and murals. It was a rainy day and Noah ventured out from Brooklyn to meet me at this strange corner to make art with Obey and Bad Brains. In Noah’s past life he held a significant position at Christie’s auction house. The legend says that he was the “Bad Brains” behind Beeple having his auction there in March, 2021. The pivotal moment that took the world by storm. Everyone can only think of one number with money signs gleaming in their eyes, 69… 69 Million! And don’t forget the hammer price. Noah was like the wizard of oz behind the curtain, he had the magic that gave the momentum for a movement to take off; NFTs! We became friends after I was hustling for a while in the space. By the fall end of the year, he had set me up with an opportunity with Darius Himes to take a leap of faith for the history of photography and showcase the Twin Flames along with them in October 6, 2021. 7 months after he broke the internet and international news cycles wide open. During the auction week I did 2 photoshoots, to finish Smoke and Mirrors, at Christie’s. The Ten of Cups with two sets of twins and the Twin Flames wall of twins. And, the Page of Swords. The cards chose Noah to represent this tarot archetype. A buddy of mine, Andrew, used to fence and he brought a sabre to the auction house. The security did not even budge when we walked in, it was antiquities, something that could have been installed on a pedestal in the halls of the house of auctions. It was the day before the big auction! We were standing in the big purple and empty room. Awaiting the performative theatrics of an auctioneer with a gavel and the crazy rich antics of collectors with their cold hard cash. I handed Noah the sabre and he wielded it at the Podium. The sacred place for the auctioneer to handle his business and gesture towards potential buyers. Noah motioned his sword to strike the air, cutting a hole in space and time. The superpower of the Page is simple; His mind is sharp and can be focused to manifest any dream with consistent work. Noah, a punk rocker, a cryptopunk, has taken a new path after my show. It was his last and a memorable way to celebrate a new milestone for photography history. The first NFT photo in Christies! Noah then went on to flow, like a fountain with the flamingos. A new direction, full autonomy with no corporate veil or grin. Joyfully teaching his son the ABCs of reality into the XYZs of his digital ingenuity.

artworks.label: No. 339  —  March 11, 2024
artworks.title: Liberty
artworks.diary: Have you ever been a tourist in your home city? Try it! You may end up discovering something new. The joy of riding a ferry at the break of dawn. Visiting a statue you’ve always seen but never been to. How close you can get to the giants in the sky. Holding up the torch of freedom, of Liberty you can see as high you can be past the New York City skyline from Wall st to the Upper West Side. A copper woman faded to green, facing the masculine city as its almighty protector as we have seen in Ghostbusters 2 when she comes to life through slime and walks under water to save you. With her light she ignites the spirit of New Yorkers, and all those who come pay a visit; Day and Night. To be a part of this living organism, where humans are the blood cells to our beloved New York City, the “big apple.” Tossed into the melting pot of a cultural stew. All walks of life on this tiny island that’s hundreds of years old. The piers and ports built this humble city with global trade routes and mason stones. All it took was nearly 3 miles wide and 13 miles long to become the financial capital of the world! In 1886, our allies, our friends, the French gave us this gift in celebration of American independence. An artwork to gesture for World Peace, a sculpture by Frédéric Auguste Bartholdi. Lady liberty what does shea mean? Our leading lady; the matriarch. Greeting the sunrise, every morning. Lighting her flame with the golden sun rays, our eyes glowing. We follow the women to freedom. “Give me your tired, your poor, Your huddled masses yearning to breathe free, The wretched refuse of your teeming shore. Send these, the homeless, tempest-tossed to me, I lift my lamp beside the golden door!”

artworks.label: No. 340  —  March 12, 2024
artworks.title: The Orange Glimpse of Sunset
artworks.diary: Michelle met me at the airport after a 16-hour flight to the last leg of the journey, on the final continent of Mother Africa. We drove right towards the water with her trusty pup to catch the orange glimpse of sunset. Michelle stood perfectly between the buildings where I can see a clear view of Lion’s head mountain. I knew I was going to go there tomorrow with my dear friend Lindi, so I thought it could be a great idea to shoot the far out shot from the ground, so tomorrow we were at a different perspective right on top of the mountain! Michelle and I made portraits of each other. That’s kinda what photographers do when they hang out. All three of us watched the clouds burn red and the crashing waves where the Atlantic ocean hugs the Indian ocean at the southern point of the Cape. The sun got quieter as it sunk into the sea and the runners stopped running and the street lamps illuminated the path. It was time to go as the shadows of the night emptied the park. I remember getting back to my room late after dinner with Michelle and settling in to rest and looked to the ceiling and thought to myself. I am back in Africa. Since 2019, I came back not only to heal, but to complete the journey that I set forth this entire year. On the final and seventh continent of Earth, Where some say humanity began in the cradle of life. We soon will discover the ancient traditions and our oldest known ancestor in the following weeks to come.. Little did I know then what was to come as each day was its own unknown. It’s in hindsight that I can understand the moments I shared with others and framed with the Super- 8 to express that person on that day. Time and Light, are the two most precious tools we have. As we live our time is limited to some odd years, and how we see light and bend it to our perception. What it will show us beyond how we can see the spectrum, but feel the heat of the sun’s rays working on us. Invisible forces that allow us to see the world and measure it as we take each breath and step; A cause and effect.

artworks.label: No. 341  —  March 13, 2024
artworks.title: Lions Head
artworks.diary: There is Strength at the top of Lion’s head mountain. A second chance, five years apart, in the same place with my sangoma, Lindi. She is a highly respected traditional healer from the Swazi community. She channels the ancestors and works with herbs for remedies and throwing bones for divine guidance. We first met back in 2018 in Peru when she visited Lesley at the mountain house in Cusco. It was a shamanic cross over between South America and Africa medicine workers. When two healers get together you can only expect magic and miracles. Lindi was the person who helped me release the black bat from my shoulder blade. A paranormal residue that sticks like a blockage until you let it out and let it go. In 2019, on my first trip to Africa we reunited only this time it was in her homeland. We were on the same journey across the Garden of Eden highway with Lesley and the gang like a merry band of pranksters. Microdosing cactus medicine and connecting to the people in the group and the land as we cross the southern coast. At the end of the trip I was supposed to fly home but was stuck in Capetown for an extra day. And mishaps like this are sometimes the universe urging you to stay because you need to be here. Lindi invited me to stay with her and her family until my next flight the following day. We did a bone reading and it showed me what was to come that year, it prepared me and protected me from when I got home and dealt with trouble with love and the law. She guided me to wear a cloth that was sacred to my mother’s jewish religion, pick up sea water from where I would go when I was a child at Corey beach, and rub this borage resin all over my body before I washed for bed. It was a distinct ritual and cleared the way. Lighting green candles to cut the cords of attachment, asking Archangel michael to use his flaming sword between me and the other. It worked! This time around, we did not go so deep in the ritual as we were simply enjoying each others company and we did a bone reading and everything felt and looked good. Just to keep going and doing what I am doing. Creating and staying true to the creative and healing path, as it will never end, only evolve. It felt more like being with family than needing to heal, which was the medicine after all. Love and belonging. Nature and sunshine. Bones and wild sage plants burning its aroma to ward off spells and evil spirits. Lindi and I ventured to her happy place, where there is a tree she favors most, I felt the calling to clean up all the trash around this tree for Lindi not to step on glass with her bare feet. We made her portrait for Smoke and Mirrors here and now we create for the Moments of the Unknown, as she represents herself this time instead of the archetype of strength. Strength reflects the ability to stay centered even when life becomes intense. It represents emotional resilience and quiet confidence. This time she emboldened Wisdom. For it is strengths twin sister. A mirror of how far we both have come in those five years passed. Daughters off to college working with new students from her craft, and me, around the world and back again following the sun around the moon. Friendship feels like family when you are part of the same tribe. It’s a deep knowing and recognition, like we have done this in many lifetimes…

artworks.label: No. 342  —  March 14, 2024
artworks.title: Bo-Kaap
artworks.diary: Lindy and her family and I visited the artistic area in Cape Town known for its iconic brightly colored, pastel homes, cobbled streets, and rich Muslim culture in Bo-Kaap. It was formerly known as the Malay Quarter, and is the hub of the Cape Malay community, Cultivating historic mosques along with local galleries and vibrant murals supporting the Palestinian cause to Free Palestine. Sudi stood under the literal word “Free” and approached the camera more so, where there are Palestinian flags waving and painted above his head. And an empowered woman with a fist in the air with one hand, and her baby in the other. A mother’s commitment to her beliefs, her people, and her children. While Lindy and I were walking around this neighborhood appreciating the art and meeting some of the artists we spoke about how to finish the project and where it should take place. Today’s portrait was very fitting to that conversation as I had originally thought I would end the project at the border of Palestine and Israel where the human aid was bringing in food and supplies. In the perfect world of “World Peace,” and resolving conflict. I had imagined a portrait of a Palestinian man and an Israeli woman holding hands interlocking in front of the military by the gates that seperated the countries. To be a beacon of hope for humanity to resolve its differences. That there are people who do not agree with this conflict and want to end it now. To respect the cultures and connect the people. A dreamers dream where we can all get along, yet politics has a different agenda to divide and conquer under the guise of racism and religion. No one wants to live or die in the state of warfare. Every human wants to live their life in peace. Goto work, buy groceries, spend quality time with family and friends, get good rest, to simply enjoy life without stress or anxiety of bombs or death on both sides of the equation. How do we get to that point of respect and cooperation? Why do we continue to fight and die for freedom of being and believing? Will this war ever end? Are we doomed to repeat these patterns or will we find a way forward? I have faith in us. In humanity to overcome. No one wants to live in fear, and that is what we can all agree on. So, as Lindy and I discussed this idea to finish the project there. She did her reading on me and whispered by the ancestors that this was not the path for me. It was too divisive at a sensitive time. There is something more compelling than controversy. I did not realize it at the time but there truly was something ahead, literally on the final day of the project that made it all make sense. It was our roots, it was where our humanity came from. It was preserved inside a museum. Along with a mother and her child in her arms. A reflection of the mural we came to see here. Everything is connected, it just takes time to see how.

artworks.label: No. 343  —  March 15, 2024
artworks.title: The Water Sets Us Free
artworks.diary: From the south to north of Africa, we step with both feet right to left into the ocean. Dancing and spinning into our human truths, our ancient selves. Washing ashore; The water sets us free when the salt takes what no longer serves us. Like a shamanic ritual, don’t look back once letting go. Let the waves play back and forth, its native instruments sparkles on the beach like a billion planets in the milky way. The suction of the porous sands and eroded pebbles filtering water from a brown to a tan shade. Busy are the chirps of the gulls scavenging food and mocking their feathered friends. Silence is also a noise we forget to hear. The harmony in nature is a song that she sings through the sounds in life like a symphony of synchronicity. The shaman’s daughter takes a different path from the family tree. To be an artist, and paint her body and mothers faces. When we come of age we decide what we want to do and how we be in life, fate meets us halfway there. You must make the choice, or the choice will be made for you. So, what do you want to be? I like to ask this question; If you were passionate about a cause and had unlimited resources, what would your nonprofit idea be? To help the world selflessly. To make this place better than we were born unto it. To live with purpose and contribute to society. What would that be? Do we choose our superpower, our gifts? Or, are they bestowed to us before birth to activate in our lifetime?

artworks.label: No. 344  —  March 16, 2024
artworks.title: Love Is the Common Thread
artworks.diary: It was Ramadan in Morocco, we sawm to foster piety, gratitude, and compassion. I met and prayed with Ismail and Fatima and their iconic pink textile outside of the Kutubiyya Mosque, near the Jemaa el-Fnaa. This sacred structure was built in 1147; Nearly 1000 years ago! We prayed through our art making and by honoring the holy days of the month until the crescent moon before the big feast. Ismail is a local and talented photographer who makes beautiful portraits about his culture and community. He uses this big pink sheet as the punctum for all of his photographs. The literal cloth that weaves his images together. The pink represents the divine feminine, but it also symbolizes the womb, the portal, that we arrive through onto this planet. All of us humans share this experience, we come from the same place inside our mothers who give us life. The safety and warmth. Religion are the stories that make us feel like we belong, to the bigger picture. To a community of like minded citizens. A belief system that we can reference as a historical artifact. These stories teach us morality, How to treat one another. The fundamental law of civilization. Is art a religion? A story that we create, a belief system that you can imagine? To connect with people, and even a community through the work. Or, is it all love. Love is the common thread between us. It is the vehicle of how we arrive on Earth, it is the energy that gives us purpose throughout our life. God…Allah…the universe… graced us with this time here. How did we get here, where do we come from, where do we go now? We are creators and dreamers. The custodians of Earth, for perhaps someday to go even beyond. Towards the source? To speak to the divine? We must listen to the wind, to the birds, to the intuition that whispers until it becomes a loud aum. A guide to become, who we were meant to be and what we were meant to do. To pray is to commune with the source. To be heard, to manifest our hopes into realization. We all have a dream, we all have needs, we all believe in something. These buildings are attuned and built with precision. A house of worship; They are the temples, churches, and mosques that are home to something greater than us, almost incomprehensible. Art and architecture are imbued into the faith. The frequency of geometric shapes reveals a hidden dimension. Something our ancestors knew, where does this lost knowledge go? In life we prepare and practice for death, so what then is the next phase of consciousness?

artworks.label: No. 345  —  March 17, 2024
artworks.title: Golden Hour in the Golden Desert
artworks.diary: Deep in the Sahara desert we took the camels from sunset to a full moon in the night sky. It was getting late and we had not shot the portrait of the day before there was no more light. Fouad dropped me off to where we ride the camels and he was going to pick me up the next day after sleeping in the sand dunes with 7 strangers. I was getting anxious as I knew it would be too dark to shoot anything. He said it would be okay and shoot after. My gut said no way, we need to shoot this right now. So, Fouad ran up the dune and I started rolling. The camel handlers were yelling at me and him that it was time to go. I was shaky and trying to get the right shot, I did not have much time as we were being rushed. But it was all the light we had left and it was golden hour in the golden desert. As the group kept calling out and started to go on the expedition, I ran up the dune and shot Fouad while they were starting to go. It was the picture perfect shot I was looking for. The guides were yelling at me when I ran over with my cameras hanging on my neck. Hopped on an camel and started the journey. We were clacking along for a couple hours then in the purple dawn we made it to our stop. It was like a village built into the dunes. The host took us for some tea, and had dinner after the fast. Once we settled down we all went for a walk in the pillowy sand that was soft and warm at the touch. When you bury your feet or hands in the sand it was colder. We all sat in a circle and listened to music for a while, then we heard music coming from another campsite a hundred yards away with a large fire burning. A celebration was there, while we remained quiet over here. Talking and connecting under the moon and stars. My italian friends from Milano sparked up some hash and we laid under the moon for hours just watching and listening. It was quiet and bright and beautiful. It felt like time did not want to end in this ever present moment of sand and sky. It was serenity…. And then it was over. I’ll never forget those sensations and colors. Like a symphony of synesthesia, absorbed by dark matter that was purple all over. A nocturnal glow, like a black light blanketed the desert as far as your eyes can perceive. Soft, yet expansive. The stars were faint but visible. All I could think was, How lucky are we to be there for a full moon?

artworks.label: No. 346  —  March 18, 2024
artworks.title: With Open Arms
artworks.diary: Waking up at sunrise for a celebration. To salute the sun. and to accomplish a task I had taken on since the first week into the project that randomly fell into place when I was gifted 7 empty vials back in Iceland. To collect the final Sacred sands of the Earth was collected in the golden heart of the Sahara, the heart of the African sand dunes. After traveling across 7 continents and collecting a geological sample in a small vial of each place; from beaches and deserts we unite the world through its sediment. Some are stars, others are volcanic, each have their own minerals and colors which make them vary of their carbon make up. A scientific collection to peek through a microscope and study each corner of the Earth to make art with. I will be honest, It felt like I was wielding the power of Thanos gauntlet with the keystones upon completing this set of 7, in a more innocence sense. It was a childhood dream, and adult wish to visit the entire Earth and now here is the proof, the data. The mindfulness to be careful, to respect and be responsible with the sands and create good with it than having collected it. During the painting portion of this project, I laid out a long 30 foot piece of handmade paper. Threw down some purple paint on the floor, and plunged my foot into it. I jumped onto one end of this paper and imprinted a single purple print. It had dawned on to me, I wanted to silkscreen all 7 continents from the Sands of the Earths I had collected on one big piece. I silkscreened the Iceland image with the woman who had gifted me the vials and later that day collected black sand from the beach. Where the story began. This print began with her at the opposite end of the paper. Week after week I slowly danced, jumped, slapped my hands down, walked perfectly straight, scrambled across, and wore my socks and shoes on it too. Every color of the rainbow to be different in some way, either how I stepped or the shape of the foot. I wanted to communicate all the ways how we touch the Earth with our feet, to make contact. And in some cases, to lift the sands with our hands. And as I write this message to whoever may be reading this. At the same time I post this image, I had also completed this giant paper painting over the course of 6 months, yesterday! Everything comes full circle, even when you walk a straight line. That’s when things can become aligned, in time. There are no mistakes, only lessons and the timing of things to happen. Just as in this image, with open arms, I welcome you to join me to step on this Earth with grace. One step at a time, we end up where we need to be.

artworks.label: No. 347  —  March 19, 2024
artworks.title: The Mother, the Protector
artworks.diary: Blue, my favorite color. The color of the sky and reflection of what we see as the water. The slowest wavelengths of light on the visible spectrum for human sight. There was one place in the world I had always dreamt of visiting. The small blue city in Morocco called, Chefchaouen. Every building, every alleyway is painted this signature color of light blue. The city itself is an artwork. It has charm and character, a visual identity like no other place on the planet. Its blue is its own. The people who dwell here even wear the colors as if it were a flag to represent. I met Fatima after a climb to the Mosque at the top of the city where you can see a panoramic view. Chefchaouen looked like a quilt of colors stitched together as the buildings blended into each other because of their camouflage of colour. As if I were in an M.C Escher illustration of infinite staircases and shapes intertwined. I walked down the steepness of the cemetery and found a pleasant stall of a man with his bright oranges sitting in a fountain with gently dripping water. It must’ve been the sun and heat but those oranges looked like the most beautiful fruits I had ever seen. Or, perhaps it was the blue sidewalks and walls that made it pop out just a bit brighter in that sun stricken scene, It was so pure and beautiful, as if I was discovering a new fruit. For 20 minutes I sat there watching this water fountain of oranges and observing all the small details from the leaves, to the pores on the skin, to the sounds of the droplets. The orange man came up to me and asked if I would like a glass of Orange juice. Absolutely! I had seen two other people drink a cup and move from their seats where I had sat down to continue to watch this little fountain and made cell phone videos of it. I was in pure awe, like a child. The man set down a glass beside me and I gulped it down with great thirst and enjoyment. It not only was the best looking oranges I had ever seen, it tasted so fucking good! I was like a monk enjoying every second of every presence of this juicy experience. Fouad had met back up with me here as he took a different route. I treated him to a glass of OJ too. It was time to shoot the portrait of the day and that’s where we had met Fatima, dressed in blue like her home city. She was with her friends and was at a textile stall. She held my hands as we stood in her store and Fouad had asked her to be a part of the project. She smiled big and her friends shook their heads and we walked her to the blue alleyways I was drawn to for the shoot. She was the perfect model, the embodiment of this city. She was the soul of Chefchaouen. The mother, the protector, the spirit of this place as this was her home and she shared that with us. She was no stranger to the camera, she played with us in a few different scenes wearing a few different outfits she had carried with her. We were making art, we were honoring her in her home. As it was always my dream to come visit this very special place she was from. I always told myself I would make art here, cyanotypes as this place was blue just like the pigment of the pictures the chemistry creates. To make a movie in this cinematic paradise. It is very artistic place, and it is where all the hash is made… During the night we sat in the town square where everyone eats and there are the hash dancers jumping and dancing and clapping their symbols while singing. I was hypnotized by their performance and joined in their fun. From a dream, to a waking reality, I look forward to the day I return to you sweet blue city. You know your soul is drawn to somewhere you never been, and when you go there you knew it was meant to be all along. Goto those places, because that’s where you will find a part of yourself you always wanted to be. Chefchaouen, that dear blue city, was that for me.

artworks.label: No. 348  —  March 20, 2024
artworks.title: Every Human Is a Flower
artworks.diary: When you pick a flower it dies. So how to appreciate its beauty while it is still growing, blooming its fragrant nectar in the air. Men pick flowers for their lovers as a gift, to make their other feel special, to be thought of. Flowers are the greatest gift, as such are fruits they bear. Seeds are the true gems which grow a hundred fold from its own life force. Abundance is truly around us as it is programmed in nature herself. To embrace the beauty is to embrace life with awe and awareness. Curiosity guides our soul to taste the honey and sweetness in the unknown. We learn because that’s what life is, one big lesson. How we live until the day we die. Adaptation and flexibility; in a world of change how do we identify ourselves, and with what means? Our genes evolve every generation, to do better, to be better. For our offspring to learn from our mistakes and make a life of their own. To be proud of them, and for them to feel proud of us. A reciprocity of experiencing the other with an understanding, a respect. What is learned and what is taught, what is right and which is wrong, as things change so does what’s accepted. What is true will always be yours. Like flower in the field, or a fruit in a forest, the beauty will present itself as pure. The beauty that gives life to a thousand others. Makes the world a better and brighter place than before. Every human is a flower meant to shine its beauty into the world. Humans are like plants, we crave the light and soil and water to continue to live. To feel the sun on our skin to be happy. To touch the ground and connect with Earth through our hands and feets. To drink the rain that dropped a million times before across many oceans, rivers, and mountains. A cycle that replenishes us in a harmony. A balance that we forget to remember. That we too are part of this system. From eco, to economy we had built our own. From trading Tulips for gold to deliver it to kings. How do we return to simplicity, to return to the beauty of nature after all of this technology conditioned to our lifestyles? The flowers help us remember, even for a second when we look in her direction. There is still beauty in the world and it grows in a bush, as a weed, in the park, or even at the supermarket waiting for us to plant them ourselves. In a vase, or in a pot. She finds our way; where beauty attracts us to her again. The flowers in the Garden of Eden are all around us, as we never left it in the first place. We just simply forgot we were still there.

artworks.label: No. 349  —  March 21, 2024
artworks.title: A Million Questions with No Answers
artworks.diary: t was the spring solstice at the Pyramids of Giza and the great Sphinx. The ancient wonder of the world. How did these pyramids get built, who built them, and why? Where did these ancient civilizations go, and how did we forget over time as we evolved into the modern day the stories of the past? Is it some sort of cultural amnesia over generations? Will it happen again with new empires and dynasties that form in the world today? How can we imagine a past from 3000 years ago and the environment that the sands of time blown over what we see now. To transport ourselves to a forgotten world with technologies that we still do not understand today. The pyramids are aligned with Orion’s belt. They are built on ley lines that are so succinct to instruments we have today. Isn’t it uncanny that the latitude of the Great Pyramid of Giza is at29.9792° N and the Speed of light is approximately 299,792,458 m/s. Are the pyramids older than we think or are told? How will we ever know, if we do not have the technology to build them now, so they say. Were they resting places for pharaohs, a healing chamber, a portal to another dimension? Perhaps they all are true. Have you ever meditated inside the great pyramids and felt the reverberations? What is below what we know in the queen’s chamber. Even at 4,500 years old, the Great Pyramid of Giza is still revealing new secrets. What did our ancestors know that we do not? Are these building transmitters and receivers to the cosmos, or the life after death? There are a million questions with no answers, we can only wonder and think about what this place is for and why. We will never know, which makes us ever more curious. The stories of our collective past tell us who we are and what we can become in the future. And in this future, how will we communicate our past to those who come long after us? The hieroglyphs that are chiseled into stone tables and limestone temple walls are records of people, kings, and gods. What of the words and images we write and transcribe on the internet. Are these our temple walls, and each post the stories we tell and how we communicate with one another? Will a simple grocery list be a sacred text for the future looking back into the pas to discover our secrets of how we lived our lives? What message do you want to leave for 4,000 years from now? I leave you with only questions because that is what the past gives us, questions and the future tries to give us the answers. But here we are, right now. Left with only one last question, a riddle to think about. Asked long ago in a Sophocles story that no one else could answer, except by the king of Thebes, Oedipus Rex. “What walks on four legs in the morning, two legs at noon, and three legs in the evening?”

artworks.label: No. 350  —  March 22, 2024
artworks.title: Who Holds the Key?
artworks.diary: The Ankh, is the Key of Life. A symbol of vitality. The totemic shape for the union of opposites: male and female, Osiris and Isis, representing heaven and earth. Death is the doorway. And this key, this golden ankh is the master key. Birth is the entry to life. The ultimate portal into material consciousness. What were we made up of before we came into being? Do we have memories, dreams, or thoughts? Was it all arrived from thin air, a crystalline clarity of pure light nothingness? Is it the same when we go, when we die? Or does it all get painted black to the abyss when the flame of our mind is extinguished? Perhaps, it is the same place before and after. And here in the now is the flash of light from the darkness. Seeing into the night of the cosmos. Where the universe experiencing itself through our eyes and senses. Life is a dream unto itself. So who holds the key? And where did this symbol come from? Is it where the man meets woman to give birth to their child. The key to life itself is giving life from itself. Generations and evolution; human nature is the gateway. The Ankh is written all over the walls in Luxor, and in every temple you will see in Egypt. It is used as many times as you would see a period in the English language. What symbols are sacred to us as this was the most precious to ancient Egyptians? Do we have a word, or a use for something so powerful? The original cross before Christ himself. A code written into our language that goes deeper than we can remember. Bestowed onto us by the gods themselves; Ra, the sun. From the heavens of life-giving power. Isis, the mother grants us fertility. Osiris, the god of the underworld, holds the ankh towards resurrection. And, Anubis, The dog headed god who is the guardian of the dead. He uses the ankh in funerary rites to ensure safe passage to the afterlife and weighs the deceased’s heart against the feather of truth and justice in the Hall of Two Truths to decide your fate between the fields of paradise and a heavy heart causing the soul to perish forever. In the end, key to eternal life, the clear quartz crystal wrapped golden Ankh, says to thee, May you be healthy and alive for all of eternity.

artworks.label: No. 351  —  March 23, 2024
artworks.title: Uncle
artworks.diary: In the city of Aswan is the Philae temple complex sitting atop of the Nile. It was moved to new heights when they were building the dam in the early 1900’s. There are stone stories of mythological figures that tower over you when you stand in front of the outer walls. Inside are patterns of hieroglyphs like lines of code across every surface. There is one pillar that was etched with the mark of a templar cross, a sign that they hid out here during persecution. Perhaps to leave a trail behind. We made uncles portrait outside in the sun with the life size murals of Isis, Hathor, and Osiris history playing out like a theater casted into the walls for thousands of years. What does it mean to move the stones from its original placement? Is it still the same place, or somehow altered. Yet, it feels like it had never moved in the first place and is intact. You could not tell unless you were told. They call this the temple of Isis. She is the premier goddess of magic, motherhood, fertility, and healing in ancient Egyptian mythology. As the devoted wife of Osiris and mother of Horus, she was revered as a powerful protector, a mourner of the dead, and a protector of women and children. Across the water is a small relic of Osiris temple that the tides go up and down from the few stones remaining. A quiet place where you can do morning yoga at the sun gate while the water rests. You need a boat to get there, on both islands. After being murdered and torn into pieces by his brother Set, Osiris’s wife, Isis, gathered his remains (except the phallus) and revived him with magic. He did not return to the land of the living, but became the ruler of the dead. He holds power over life, death, and the annual flooding of the Nile, representing agricultural fertility. Were these gods real people, or stories imagined? To create something is to live through the experience from your knowledge. Were these deities among the people, or representations of the plant and animal spirits through anthropomorphic forms? Who communicated these stories to their people. Was it the priests or kings that ordered the walls be sculpted with these images that communicated what had occured? A sort of record keeping, an obsession of knowledge. Who was telling the stories, and what were the stories trying to tell us. The pictures and hieroglyphs were based on shapes and patterns, items and forms. Their language was reflecting reality, not an abstract tongue. Symbols of living things. Like waves and cranes and owls or crocs and serpents. Marks that mean something when together in the past, and what we can only imagine to ourselves now that we see it from the future. Who created the Rosetta stone? And when did language shift from images to letters?

artworks.label: No. 352  —  March 24, 2024
artworks.title: Echoes of Eternity
artworks.diary: Nuby took Max and I on a road trip down to Abu Simbel with his uncle who we shot with at the Philae temple. Little did we know we would have to hide out at every checkpoint on our way. What literally felt like every 20 minutes for 5 hours we stopped and got checked out. Nuby told us to hide behind the curtain or look like we were asleep in the back of the van because we were American and Europeans. I don’t know what was up but it killed our high. We were smoking hash out of my carved out apple the whole way through, the driver was smoking cigarettes to mask the smell from the cops. Luckily nothing had happened to us. Max and I were paranoid as fuck all the way, it was exhilarating and stressful at the same time. Also it was hilarious to see Nuby pass 50 notes to the cops at every checkpoint like it was a code of conduct here. Bribes are a way of life in these parts, especially if you want to stay out of trouble while you are in the middle of it. We finally made it to our refuge in the evening before the shoot. We had some dinner and passed out to wake up at 4:20 am for a boat ride on the Nile to a sunrise view of Abu Simbel. I’ve been to Egypt the year before and this was one temple we did not make it to, and was one of the most interesting ones I wanted to see. So we made sure of it to go this time around. Right before the boat ride, Max pulled out two tabs of LSD, and we smiled at each other and dipped it under our tongues. We got on the boat and the engine started roaring! The giggles started to hit us immediately. And Nuby asked what was going on so we told him, he was a bit bummed that there was no more left but he smiled and sat the trip for us. It was still dark out and we had arrived, the onset was rising just as the sun started to lift into the sky over the watery horizon. The moment I started shooting the sun hit Nuby as he clapped, sang, danced and prayed around the boat right in front of Abu Simbel illuminating n the distance. I can see the kings on their thrones in the stone walls, they were gigantic! It was crazy to me that there were virtually no other boats around us. We had the Nile to ourselves this morning. Our captain headed toward the docks right next to the temple and we departed. We entered the gate to the back of Abu Simbel and the veil was lifted. I felt like I was behind the scenes at Disneyland because when you approach Abu Simbel you see it’s just a facade! It had been moved because of the dam and to protect it from a flood it was lifted higher. I still don’t understand how they can extract, remove, and replace the sacred site so perfectly you could not tell it was not the original placement. It was too perfect. Like it was never touched since it was first created. The acid was kicking in pretty hard when I came to this realization. And again, there was no one there! We had Abu Simbel to ourselves. Nuby said to go in and have fun as he waited outside the temple. Max and I entered the tombs together and felt the images on the wall and the echoes of eternity sync in. Was it the acid, or was it this special moment of being somewhere I always wanted to be and have the privilege of having it to ourselves? Perhaps both! The walls were singing stories, and for a second there I thought I could understand and read the hieroglyphs, what they were saying to us. It all came to life! We were in there for what felt like 10 minutes but was really an hour long enjoyment. As we exited, we saw a massive crowd standing 20 or so meters from the entrance. As if they were waiting for us to exit, it felt very funny to me at the time. But now I reckon they were listening to their guide teach them about the temple before going in and we had just timed it all so perfectly somehow. I made a ton of double exposure photographs of the kings sitting on their thrones and touching the sun in the sky with light strokes. Being an artist, feeling the moment, creating a vision and a memory at the same time. It was sensational. Looking deeply one last time of the giants who greeted us and gifted us the time to be alone with them. I waved goodbye and one of them winked at me. Like the universe was playing along, like a big joke, in the best way possible. We entered the second tomb and again had it all to ourselves. The timing was so aligned it was crazy. Again, was it us or the acid? Everything seemed to be working out in a beautiful flow. We ended our trip there and walked Nubys uncle back to the van, since he has a bum leg. Max and I smiled so big as we processed we were leaving this strange and exceptional place that was far removed from its original place. Again I thought, how the fuck did they move these stones and put them back like nothing ever happened? Also, because the Egyptians were deeply connected to the stars at precise measurements. What does it mean for the angles to be off by a few degrees? For instance, the sun shining through the doorway of Abu Simbel as the giants greet the sun. Does the math add up, does the light hit where it needed to be originally? What was lost and sacrificed when this dam was built and the temple shifted? These buildings were built with such great care and precision. How does change this affect it? I left with so many questions as well as so many memories I always dreamed of having. Abu Simbel is worth the time and energy to get there. As there is nothing else like it. So, take a trip down the Nile and enjoy the views and this ancient waterway that gave an entire civilization life, and continues to do so as time goes on like the river continues to flow in the stream of consciousness.

artworks.label: No. 353  —  March 25, 2024
artworks.title: We Drink, We Become, We Remember
artworks.diary: Nile, a river, and a frequency. A flood is not just water, it is memory. Like the fractal womb birthing a new universe for the blooming papyrus . To write, to record keep. We drink, we become, we remember. The Nile is not past nor future. It’s always hurrying in to the present. Refreshing endlessly, like us. Dna of the deserts, people swim like crocodiles with chrome teeth and Ibis birds flexing their filtered wings. The Nile nourishes us with quantum relays broadcasting pharaonic dreams. Just water, just mind, just here. Still flowing, still ancient.

artworks.label: No. 354  —  March 26, 2024
artworks.title: In Every Man Chest, There Beats a Heart
artworks.diary: When I visited the tree of life in Victoria falls I met Brian and Prince selling their sculptures and trinkets along with dozens of their colleagues at the market they built there. Brian held up a chess board, and Prince held up a pair of Zebras that I thought created a heart shape space between them. It reminded me of a song I would sing to myself. It is a Bob Marley’s song called, Zimbabwe, and I thought how perfect because I am finally in Zimbabwe. Let’s play the music, and he sang out, “Every man got a right to decide his own destiny…. We come together to overcome the little trouble… To divide and rule could only tear us apart. In every man chest, there beats a heart.” Chess is a game of mind, and art, well art is a sensation in the heart. And, when singing the Zimbabwe song, in Zimbabwe in the car ride home with Simon and Jacob, I felt a great sense of alignment. Where I would sing this song on my skate across New York City, little did I know I would be fulfilling this idiosyncratic prophecy that this song had urged me to visit the country itself a decade later. It is uncanny how our subconscious mind can guide our awakened state and propagate influences or ideals. In a way, singing that song over and over, because how it made me feel alive, inspired and human, led me here with Brian and Prince, where the elephants and zebras roam freely.

artworks.label: No. 355  —  March 27, 2024
artworks.title: Between the Rainbow and the Waterfall
artworks.diary: The night we arrived to Victoria Falls, Simon and I were sitting outside on the patio having a meal and prepping our adventure. Christopher and his acapella group came over to us and started singing their songs. We were their only audience and they lit up the entire room. Simon and I listened to about 5 doo waps then Christopher set down a CD next to me and we invited him to sit with us for a while since his group was leaving the show. He was telling Simon and I about his musical dreams. We invited him to hang out with us the next day as we were going to Victoria Falls to see the water falling and the mist rising. The next morning he picked us up and we rode over together to the park entrance. Christopher was guiding us through and telling us stories about his home and the where the water comes from across the Zam to the Zim. We went from spot to spot to find the right shot. It was near the end we found what we were looking for and what Christopher wanted to show us. He told me to be careful of the rocks and not past the chain. It is slippery wert and its easy to get dazed by chasing the sight of the rainbow that can make you fall over the cliff. Simon pulled me back just as I was looking deeply over the ledge following that said rainbow in the air. Christopher stood between the rainbow and the water fall. He threw up his hands to me what felt like a peace sign. And in this moment, while seeing, experiencing, listening to the sounds, and shooting this portrait I knew deeply. This was going to be the shot the represented the entire project. Its mystical, its beautiful, its inspiring, and the whole world just froze in motion to the spirit of this project. This was it, this is the Moments of the Unknown. It’s about that human beauty, the natural wonders, the mystic spirits, the love of the arts, the connection to each other. I felt that deeply in this portrait. As I reached my arm out to Christopher in the frame for being with us, sharing his presence in such a beautiful place he calls home. To be there with him and learn about him and where he is from and how special that is. Is what this project symbolizes. Pure presence and noticing the other in a deep and meaningful way. Respect the life we have, while we have time, in this wonderful world we live, while we are still here, and the people who dwell on this funny little planet. To see and bring out the beauty in others, to learn how to be in the world of understanding, to make this world a better place than before we arrived. To do good and take care of planet Earth, together. Our one true home.

artworks.label: No. 356  —  March 28, 2024
artworks.title: White Rhino
artworks.diary: Jordan picked up Simon and I from our hostel to drive down to his home city where he grew up in Bulawayo. It was a long drive on a broken road where you would see children on the side of the road shoveling gravel into large potholes. It was a gnarly highway and we had saw a terrible crash on the way down. He set us up in his parents home to rest and prepare us for an early morning hike to see the endangered white rhino. There is an estimated southern white rhino population at approximately 15,752 as of August 2025. Jordan knew this rhino very well as he had been tracking it for years, so he knew exactly where in the wild he would be. We ducked down low in a field and hiked for an hour until we found her. We stayed very quiet and out of sight as he told us they have some of the worst eye sight but the best hearing sense. There was a moment that I literally witnessed the awareness like a dust devil traveling towards the rhino in a quantum field like traces of a ghost sonically hit the rhino and made him perked up. We walked a few meters out of the way, and out of nowhere this mini tornado swept in from where we just were standing and directly hit the rhino and covered him with dust and made him angry and anxious to a standing position stomping its feet. I could not believe what I was seeing, could that be him becoming aware of our presence? It sure as shit felt like thats what had just happened. Consciousness noticing and a delay swept through the field from where we stood. We waited for him to calm down and lay back down to move closer in. It was scary but exhilarating. Once he caught wind of us, no pun intended, he became chill and was okay with us being there as we meant no harm and wanted to say hello. He sniffed and exhaled like, its all good, I see you now, you scared me guys. We got as close as Jordan said was reasonable, made art and peacefully and respectfully left slowly and quietly to let him rest. We went on to see the petroglyphs on rock formations nearby to see what art people were making many, many years ago.

artworks.label: No. 357  —  March 29, 2024
artworks.title: A Living Artwork
artworks.diary: Jordan brought us deep into the Matobo Hills to visit traditional Ndebele painted homesteads. These were custom buildings where art is not separate from life, but lived inside of. The families welcomed us in, opening their doors with a quiet generosity. From the outside, the homes are geometric and rhythmically painted in repeating patterns that feel both ancestral and modern. But inside, they transform. The walls curve and the spaces soften with everything becomes organically ornate, as if the structures were grown from the ground rather than built. We visited two of Jordan’s friends, each living on opposite ends of the hills. The landscapes stretched far apart, the spirit felt shared with one another becoming rooted, expressive, deeply handmade. At one home, we arrived on a child’s birthday. There was no performance, just life unfolding. We celebrated with them, sharing homemade cake, laughter, and a moment that felt both intimate and universal. For a brief time, we weren’t visitors. We were part of their community standing inside a living artwork shaped by generations. In places like the Ndebele homesteads, the home itself comes from the land. The walls are made from soil, dung, ash. Made from materials that breathe, crack, and return back to the earth over time. Nothing is permanent. Everything in cycles when collaborating with the land. The patterns painted on the homes carry cultural identity and lineage. Ndebele women used these geometric designs as a visual language marking family, resistance, and continuity. The act of painting is a ritual, repeated generation after generation, passing knowledge through their artworks and architecture.

artworks.label: No. 358  —  March 30, 2024
artworks.title: The Drums Are the First Sound We Hear
artworks.diary: The drums are the first sound we hear. When the hearts are beating for the first time it is the sacred rhythm of our soul coming into consciousness. The sound made from light ignited from within the womb. The drums beats move our feet to the music around the fire telling stories through movement when we dance around the flames together at the end of the night. What makes us human is what moves us. The sacred sound of the drums beating into our hearts, give us life and hope and might. We create our own melodies when hitting the echoing leather. Organic matter; Drums made from wood and skin. Intensity and speed creates the beat. Years spent refining the sound that meets the ears which moves your feet. The drums are the first sound we hear before birth and the last sound we remember when the heart goes to sleep; after life. Music brings us closer, tuning a group into alignment. A quantum frequency that waves through the field and strings us all together to step to the same beat. The drums are a ritual, a portal to our spirit waiting to greet us. A shamanic trance to see the animal spirits wander above our third eyes while two are closed. Listen to the beats. Listen to the sounds of the waves. Listen to your heart beat in sync with the drums. Listen to where the point of the bass hits the base of your brain. Just listen to your rhythm with you eyes closed, and one hand on your chest; beating… Feeling the pulse of life. the presence. The blood flowing through each clap, clap. The source of sounds, when it’s time to face the music. A time to open your heart.

artworks.label: No. 359  —  March 31, 2024
artworks.title: Rich with Greenery!
artworks.diary: It was our last day in Bulawayo. Jenifa was our wonderful host that works with Jordans family. She woke up at sunrise to start her day with us. Some time during the week I asked if she would like to be in the art project before we left back to Victoria Falls. Jenifa was all dressed up for her close up the morning we departed; Everything was rich with greenery! A couple days before, there was unbeknownst to me a serious break in to the house. Jordan and Simon kept quiet about it until we left the house back on the road to Victoria Falls. I was stunned that they did not tell me when it happened. It was 2 in the morning, Simon said he heard a metal rumbling in the kitchen so went to check it out. He saw 5 min outside breaking through the window after pulling off the gated window. He grabbed a club and started whacking the man entering through the window and he jumped back outside and shooing them away. Funny enough, Simon and the thieves saw my lights turn on in the hallway and heard me unlock my bedroom door as I walked to use the toilet for a late night pee. They all froze what they were doing until I was done and went back in my room, and Simon continued on to fight them through the window until they scurried away in defeat. It was one of those, oh best not he doesn’t know scenarios. I was pissed when I found out they didn’t tell me about the home invasion when it happened. Thats I realized why we started to have armed guards for the rest of our stay. I thought to myself, well fuck, I have all the film from this project sitting in this pelican case, which is the only thing of value I had with me. All the exposed footage I had shot and 4 cameras; A polaroid, a Rolleiflex, and my day and night super 8 cameras, and a fuck ton of film. Thankfully Simon scared them off, otherwise I would have had to fight my life to keep that film safe from harm. It was funny too as there was only a week left of the project, and Thank the lord we were saved and safe from evil doers. As silly as it may sound, I felt divinely protected doing this project no matter where we went. Call me naive, but I had faith every step of the way, even when things turned dark. The light founds it way through and flowed like white lighting through all the beauty and all the hardships. Trust, not everything will be easy, but you will learn a thing or two along the way.

artworks.label: No. 360  —  April 1, 2024
artworks.title: The Elder Teaching the Youngling
artworks.diary: Christopher brought us to a village in Zambia where we met Obert and his friends. At first we sat under a straw hut and smoked their ganja out of school construction paper. It was quite harsh but it did the trick. We all riff raffed about music and making art. The guys walked us through their village to meet their families. Simon busted out a big bag of toys and treats for the young ones and all the kids run up to him from all over the village. Once we were out, we headed back towards Zim. And on the way, Obert and his son met us with his other friends who were playing in the water. Obert stood in the Zambezi river with his baby brother and picked him up to hold him in the water for the moving portrait. Their sacred river, that brings life and rainbow to Victoria Falls. You have to be careful when playing in this water, as there are crocs and hippos swimming around feeding on their turf and the ancient rip current is strong and silently creating vortexes underneath the surface. Obert and his family; The elder teaching the youngling. Life will go on like the current flows never stop. Cycles of rebirth and renewal with all the generations between sharing stories of wisdom and their memories to be passed on. Why water means life on a planet? A reflection to the liquid that flows within us. Just as consciousness is a thought, water is life.

artworks.label: No. 361  —  April 2, 2024
artworks.title: Where the Heart Remembers
artworks.diary: On the bridge above Victoria Falls to Zimbabwe to Zambia, we met a couple of local women from Zambia carrying boxes of fruits and groceries balanced on their heads. Traveling back to their families village after gathering food. One of the women had her baby strapped to her chest while they were breastfeeding. We walked, made art, and talked across the bridge with Naomi and Brenda until we reached the immigration checkpoint. I thought to myself, you can make art anywhere in the world, with anyone if you realize the present and what happening right in front of you. All of it is special, it is life, it is infinite choices. To meet and create with these women on their way home from work was what the spirit of the project and the moment urged me to do. When shooting portraits, I am really feeling into the moment more than I am seeing what is outside. It is an energy, an idea, that arrives, that feels deeply familiar. That feeling of intuition is a deep knowing, and to trust that force is for me part of the art and using the limitations of 24 hour to find someone to make a portrait with, and in those 10 seconds create a work that will last a lifetime. Under those confines, I attempt to open my eyes and observe. See who is around, what is the light conditions, where is this place, who are the people, how to represent culture, does my camera have enough film or battery. It’s all a beautiful recipe of creation. It is being in the present moment, and making a photo or a video of someone not only honors that time forevermore, it is the noticing of and acknowledging others existence. The beauty of the light that reflects on them and into the camera. Is an honor. To see the light in others, to make something meaningful, to make the present moment count every second thereafter. Creation is the greatest connection to the power of love. To create is to love something into existence from the ether. To create with others is to respect their being and see them with kind eyes as they are and aim to be. At the end of the day, we are all human and we are all one and the same. The singularity of consciousness is the understanding that we as humans are all animals alike. We love to love, we love to eat, we love to be with family, we work and try to love what we do. We sleep, we all just want to be loved and belong. The bridge to Zim to Zam is where the heart remembers. The answers to all our questions are already inside of us. We just have to walk the line of getting their from the in between of self doubt and confidence. The bridge to who we are and who we want to become.
