We cross it with one foot in front of the other, as long it may need to take. Take action to move. Take each step, to continue. In this present moment; On the path somewhere between both sides of beginning and the end, you will meet your past and future self.

artworks.label: No. 362  —  April 3, 2024
artworks.title: A Generation of Dreamers
artworks.diary: On our last day in Zimbabwe, Simon and I visited Christopher’s family at his home. his children and all the kids from his neighborhood gathered on his patio. We were making art and teaching the kids how to make photographs and polaroids. I let the kids take over my Polaroid camera and photograph one another until all the film ran out, I had about 3 packs to go through since there was only 4 days left in the project now. Christopher’s brothers daughters, who happen to be identical twins, stood in the doorway. All the children waited and waved out front of Christopher’s family house. They ran towards my camera and danced around in utter joy and excitement. There were dozens of them laughing and screaming. It is the little things us together. The way a camera can change someone’s life, to inspire them to become an artist. Perhaps, we were all born artists. Being taught how to create is a skill that can be refined from the brink of a playful youth all the way to a serious practice in adulthood. Art frees us from the world, and even from ourselves. Sometimes we need that little push, and awareness that something like art is possible, or exists. Sometimes you carve out your own path that was never possible until you did it yourself. We need to show the youth they are capable of anything they can dream of. To learn from our mistakes , and successes. We need a generation of dreamers instead of worker bees. For them to bring in new ideas and innovative technology to sustain and regenerate the world, to build the future and explore the universe. It’s funny, the youth will always be the ones to shape the future, while we are too busy living to remember the past. So believe in them! Give them a chance to lead. Learn from them, and what they are interested in. To not fall behind. To keep that curiosity and learning alive, because when your brain stops growing and your mind starts slowing all that is left is already gone. Keep that inner child alive. Don’t forget to laugh, and play, and enjoy this life. Because art is where the kid part of you that never went away when you grow up. Art with others is connection to each other and the world. A language, a dance, a way of living with one another on this planet.

artworks.label: No. 363  —  April 4, 2024
artworks.title: Uganda Sunrise
artworks.diary: Uganda sunrise. A crane playing in the wind and spreading its wing. To fly, to dive. Catch a fish, then another one, two. See two little women standing between the middle of a bent tree, where the glow of its light strikes a small part of me. Third eye, in the bright sunshine. Sing that song just one more time. You know the words, the verse, the rhythm. Stirring the sounds of my heart breathing in, then bleeding out; Breathing in, bleeding out. Like a bird I see the world, from the top. Somewhere up above. My love rains down, where Victoria Falls meets Victoria’s Lake. The place that makes my eyes ache. Tears of prayers that sink beneath the surface. Light up the fish that swim underneath us. Call it love, call it whatever you want, the warm feeling I have inside me, for you. My woman, my best friend, I hum that little beat again. A kiss to your chest, when we be rocking in the nest. To lay an egg of freedom, a part of you and a part of me, together. The kind of miracle that comes in threes. You keep us grounded like the roots of that bent tree. Flying through, like the big bad blue. Magic crane. Will you guide us one last time, the place where spirit is awakened, the source connecting to the divine. Keep facing with faith, and a strange bit of hope. Sprinkle it with love, then you got your self worth. What’s it worth? The world. Tis Wisdom. Bob said, to keep your soul over silver and gold. You want freedom. Believe him.

artworks.label: No. 364  —  April 5, 2024
artworks.title: Live and Let Live
artworks.diary: Simon and I trekked inside of the Bwindi Impenetrable National Forest. It was a bumpy 5 hour hike up and down the hills of the jungle. It was misty and raining. The forest floor was slippery and had us sliding around falling a bunch. We had to rely on each others grip to stay steady and catch each other if we fell. There was a french family with us as part of the group. Somewhere close to the encounter with the Gorillas the parents in the family had a stomach bug. Mom and Dad were not doing so hot so they stayed at the last checkpoint where we had stopped for lunch. The son and daughter were fine and stood by their parents while our guide sent Simon and I on a mission onwards with one of our armed guards to meet the Gorilla families they had been tracking for months migrating through the forest grazing on leaves from the trees and naps in the canopy. We drew closer to the Gorilla clan, we could start hearing the cries and yells of all sorts of apes. We found the trackers and they had giant machetes cutting through the jungle. We kept on going and there it was, I saw a dark mysterious furry figure escape into the trees after making a loud roar. I thought it had looked like someone in a halloween costume. It did not feel real! We drew closer and closer, until we saw the son of the silverback sitting there in the bush with his back towards us eating smaller leaves. We watched in aw, Simon stepped a few feet closer. BAM, an electric shock of fear shook my soul. I had never been that terrified in my life that instantly. The gorilla crashed is arms down to scare us and faked charged at Simon. He had quite literally and physically struck us with fear, he paralyzed us like we were Pokemon in a duel. We looked at each other thankful we were still alive. We shook it off and headed closer again. He knew we were there and let us in. We gazed at him around the corner as he stood there watching us back. Grabbing a leaf and feeding himself. He looked like a little Buddha meditating in the sunlight. After eating a bunch of leaves, He scurried off to where his family was climbing and chilling around. Suddenly, the french family came from behind. They had made it and their success and excitement had cleared all their ailments. It was good to see that they made it, after coming this deep and far away into the woods. The trackers introduced us to each member of the group. There were some cute scenes with the newborns climbing on their mommas and on smaller trees. They were fun to watch “learning the ropes.” The big bad alpha was chilling in his lair with his wives. Never look at these guys directly in their eyes, or they will stand their ground. They are the boss in these parts. Thankfully, I had my camera to come between he and I. So, I could look and stare without him even shuttering a glare. I nodded to him and he nodded back. This species is not just an animal, Apes have consciousness. They think. They can communicate with us through signs and sounds. They are part of our family tree. There was a female gorilla sitting in the bush, very calm and docile, she came close to me and laid down right where I stood. I kneeled and got close with my camera. She looked deep into my lens, looking right into my soul. I felt her presence acknowledging mine. Perhaps the feeling of an ape meeting us is us meeting an alien. A being “smarter” or more “evolved” than us, communicating with us. Reaching out our arms like Adam did to God. Prometheus with his fire. Our hands to the Apes like Our minds connect to higher life forms. The universe reaching out as we reach ours too. A reflection of itself, experiencing itself in nature. That ape made me feel more human. Although, I felt as she had expressed human qualities too. That gentle look, vulnerable and graceful, is part of us, part of our DNA. To communicate across species this way. We spent hours playing with the Gorillas, and respecting their space. The most footage I shot on the project was on this day. Where human becomes one with nature and the natural world. There are no bored apes in the jungle, only playful and fun. They even have a sound that calms them down, and it sounds like a loud hum in the corner of your throat as if it was an aum. You use this when they are fighting or getting aggressive. It is the sound the alpha makes to calm down two of his young. We were leaving the Jungle and I wanted to take one last portrait of Simon and our guide, Innocent. When all of a sudden, all the gorillas we had been watching started cross our path. We were terrified and not supposed to be this close. But they randomly intersected with us on our way out of their zone. I kept shooting and the guys stood very still. Their backs were turned towards the Gorillas while I had the perfect spot to see them migrate altogether as a family unit. The last Gorilla to cross was the big guy we saw earlier deep in the woods. He grunted while passing us slowly and very intently. Watching us and protecting his kin. It was a synchronistic phenomenon, like it was meant to be shown this way. Our family and his, co-exist. As it should be for all us animals. Not the survival of the fittest, or who is the apex predator, why not a world of respect and live and let live? A planet with a conscience for us to have peace of mind.

artworks.label: No. 365  —  April 6, 2024
artworks.title: A Handful of Masks
artworks.diary: On the way back to Entebbe, we found ourselves in the middle of the Uganda Equator crossing. To be on the center of the Earth, where the most solid point of gravity grounds you like a hug to your body from your mother. I think of all the miles we swept and the hours of the year that have been shot on film. 366 days distilled into 1 hour. Time stretches for 20 thousands miles and another 20 thousand kilometers on seperate road trips on different continents. We make time shrink into a vial, or a film canister. For so much life, to edit it down into a vision, or a dream. Gently remembering once we started how much time was yet ahead, and now coming along as a changed man looking back to forget how much time had really passed. Patience and anxiety altogether, every day. Like the click of a shutter it had calmed my nerves. Pressing that button every 24 hours, feeling into the moment. Attempting to come to understanding a person, how they see, and seeing them as they are; In their trust and honor. To all the friends we had gained, and to all the friends we had lost. Time uncovers truths, and unravels the shadows. Are we ready to meet them? Another year gone, creating art with everyone. From the outside world to the inside digital cube: X marks the spot. To speak listen and follow along for the future to be written inside and out. Voices and ideas all in one. The endless feed that constantly feeds our temperamental. Community breaks us free from being alone. As we spend our time online, all the time. Art saves us. It is the equilibrium of our selves as is the equator is to the Earth. Where do we draw that fine line? Morals and ethics and boundaries to cross protect. Listen to the voices of our ancestors. Respect. Their calling wisdom and it lives in our DNA. Humanity all came from the same place, with sacred rituals lined in our hearts. From our ancestors who whispered deep into our souls from a thousand years ago. Jacob wore his mask with the men who sell them too. Honoring the art of the tribes, the people and their ancestors of mother Africa, from whence we all came. In the middle of the world, the rain had started. Halfway to the airport. Stranded until it passed, we supported the shops and loaded up a couple of handmade drums, a handful of masks, and a nkondi figure that was used as a door holder for the merchant. A lesson I learned on this big adventure, when you see something that calls to you. Ask yourself when will you ever be back to this place? Support the locals and enjoy the gifts to your friends family and the ones you want to give to yourself. A memory to enjoy and share, to tap into that moment as you had once lived it. Memory is like time travel.

artworks.label: No. 366  —  April 7, 2024
artworks.title: The Ending Is Also the Beginning
artworks.diary: The ending is also the beginning. Where can a year take you to? How much can you change, even in a day. Reciting the lessons that I learned and stories that were told. People across the Earth are all the same. We are all human. And us humans want the same things, eat the same things, sleep the same way, we work, we play, we become. We are like ants and the bees in community, so why don’t we act like a team? We live our lives, seperate from the hive. Did we evolve to be this way, how did we learn to individualize? What would happen if we all cooperate as a species and stopped wasting resources on wars and conflicts, and pool all our collective might forward to explore new dimensions in space and time as the human race. We can begin setting up new ways to survive and thrive on planets across the blinking suns and swirling moons. Look how far we have come. We started as less than an animal in the wild that grew into something beyond words. How does consciousness let us think? To be aware, that we are even aware right now, is what makes us unique. For every generation we get smarter, better, stronger, that is how the chains are linked through blood and family. DNA ladders waiting to go even higher, some gene mutations others are genuine miracles. Think of how many family members it took for us to get here right now, to read this sentence. We are the miracles, beyond all odds of existence, yet here we are! What are we doing here, and why does art make us feel? Perhaps life is just one big question mark, and the more questions we ask, the more we learn. The more we answer, the more we really don’t even know. To take on this year long project, twice took a lot of my heart and soul, body and mind in all the most beautiful and difficult ways. The ways the help us grow when we never give up on those dreams of ours. Yet here we find ourselves in a special museum in the middle of Addis Ababa with the oldest humans on Earth. Her name is Lucy, and she is our great, great,great, great, great… you get it… grandmother. She connects us all, because scientist say she was THE first human. It all started with her, and here we are! Fetiha Was with her son, Liqu, as well as another baby on the way. I thought to myself,. as we walked through the museum exhibit, how many layers of bloodlines exist in this one room. From the elders of our ancient past, we to are the children of the present, and for the future generations to come the unborn ready to embark on this world. When I saw her hold her child beside Lucy. Something inside me started to glow. I saw time unfolding, and the meaningful action of this artwork being made. It was dearly human. Stretching across generations after generations after generations. A portrait of a family through time, in time with the videos I have shot. Somewhere between a still memory and a moving image of the present moment that stretches and flexes past our mind. The feeling of completing an artwork that was the main purpose and focus of life, was the most joyous experiences. All the discipline, all the hard work, we create the rules and live by them like gospel. Who is enforcing the rules? Only yourself really. A scream of joy, a cathartic release of emotions bottled up across 7 continents like the sand vials. It’s time to let it all go, so much life was lived, and a only a fragment remains. The beauty of humanity is infinite. So how do we choose what represents what we are? NASA had an idea, through sound. This project too, honors that. Their legacy. To communicate with something outside of ourselves. Perhaps we may have even created it. What comes to meet us first? Extra Terrestrials or Artificial General Intelligence? Both at the same time? I have a dream, as large as the cosmos. To send this project out into the stars. Channeling our distant spacefaring cousins in the deep dark. When I look into the diamond of the night all I can whisper a breath into infinity, because when I look at those stars all I can see into something vastly endless and alive at the same time, we live inside of it as we are made of the same strings. I believe, we can meet our makers, as we also the ones who are making. The moral of the story here is that we are all one. We celebrate and learn from each other’s uniqueness, and come together in unity as the same species. Like brothers and sisters, Lucy is our shared ancestor. She brought us all together simply by being; and all of humanity is just one big happy family.

artworks.diary:
Have you ever been a tourist in your home city? Try it! You may end up discovering something new. The joy of riding a ferry at the break of dawn. Visiting a statue you've always seen but never been to. How close you can get to the giants in the sky. Holding up the torch of freedom, of Liberty you can see as high you can be past the New York City skyline from Wall st to the Upper West Side. A copper woman faded to green, facing the masculine city as its almighty protector as we have seen in Ghostbusters 2 when she comes to life through slime and walks under water to save you. With her light she ignites the spirit of New Yorkers, and all those who come pay a visit; Day and Night. To be a part of this living organism, where humans are the blood cells to our beloved New York City, the "big apple." Tossed into the melting pot of a cultural stew. All walks of life on this tiny island that's hundreds of years old. The piers and ports built this humble city with global trade routes and mason stones. All it took was nearly 3 miles wide and 13 miles long to become the financial capital of the world! In 1886, our allies, our friends, the French gave us this gift in celebration of American independence. An artwork to gesture for World Peace, a sculpture by Frédéric Auguste Bartholdi. Lady liberty what does she mean? Our leading lady; the matriarch. Greeting the sunrise, every morning. Lighting her flame with the golden sun rays, our eyes glowing. We follow the women to freedom.

"Give me your tired, your poor,
Your huddled masses yearning to breathe free,
The wretched refuse of your teeming shore.
Send these, the homeless, tempest-tossed to me,
I lift my lamp beside the golden door!"
